constants.SIGN_NOVICE_AREA: A new Novice or Respawn Area is being planned somewhere in this sector. Please make sure all important rooms are reserved.
constants.SIGN_RESPAWN_AREA: A new Novice or Respawn Area is being planned somewhere in this sector. Please make sure all important rooms are reserved.
constants.SIGN_PLANNED_AREA: A new Novice or Respawn Area is being planned somewhere in this sector. Please make sure all important rooms are reserved.

constantNotes.LAB_BOOST_ENERGY: Energy a lab spends per body part it boosts.
constantNotes.LAB_BOOST_MINERAL: Compound a lab spends per body part it boosts.
constantNotes.LAB_UNBOOST_ENERGY: Energy dropped per part when a creep is unboosted.
constantNotes.LAB_UNBOOST_MINERAL: Compound dropped on the creep's tile per part when it is unboosted; it also scales the lab cooldown after unboostCreep.
constantNotes.BOOSTS: BOOSTS[part type][compound][action] is the multiplier for that action of a part boosted with that compound. For TOUGH, damage is the share of damage taken.
constantNotes.LAB_MINERAL_CAPACITY: Most a lab holds of its one mineral or compound.
constantNotes.LAB_ENERGY_CAPACITY: Most energy a lab holds; the energy is used only for boosting.
constantNotes.LAB_COOLDOWN: Not used by the engine. The cooldown after a reaction is REACTION_TIME of the product.
constantNotes.LAB_REACTION_AMOUNT: Units taken from each source lab, and units of product made, per reaction run.
constantNotes.REACTIONS: REACTIONS[a][b] is the compound made from a and b; every pair is listed in both orders.
constantNotes.REACTION_TIME: Cooldown in ticks of the producing lab after one run, by product. Reversing the compound costs the same.
constantNotes.TERMINAL_CAPACITY: Most a terminal holds, all resources together.
constantNotes.TERMINAL_SEND_COST: Not used by the engine. The transfer cost is ceil(amount × (1 − e^(−distance / 30))) energy.
constantNotes.TERMINAL_MIN_SEND: Not used by the engine: send has no minimum amount.
constantNotes.TERMINAL_COOLDOWN: Ticks a terminal waits after it sent something or was used to make a deal.
constantNotes.MARKET_FEE: Share of price × amount charged in credits when an order is created, extended or raised in price.
constantNotes.MARKET_MAX_ORDERS: Most orders one player can have at a time; inactive and filled ones count.
constantNotes.MARKET_ORDER_LIFE_TIME: Life time of an order in milliseconds of real time: 30 days. Then it is removed and the fee of its unfilled part is paid back.
constantNotes.ORDER_SELL: Order type: you offer a resource out of your terminal.
constantNotes.ORDER_BUY: Order type: you ask for a resource to be delivered to your terminal.
constantNotes.ENERGY_REGEN_TIME: Ticks from the moment a source drops below full until it is refilled completely.
constantNotes.SOURCE_ENERGY_CAPACITY: Energy of a full source in a room that is owned or reserved.
constantNotes.SOURCE_ENERGY_NEUTRAL_CAPACITY: Energy of a full source in a room whose controller nobody owns or has reserved.
constantNotes.SOURCE_ENERGY_KEEPER_CAPACITY: Energy of a full source in a room without a controller, such as a source keeper room.
constantNotes.EXTRACTOR_COOLDOWN: Cooldown a mineral harvest puts on the extractor; the next harvest is possible 6 ticks after the last.
constantNotes.MINERAL_REGEN_TIME: Ticks from the moment a mineral is emptied until it is full again.
constantNotes.MINERAL_MIN_AMOUNT: Not used by the engine; a refill takes its amount from MINERAL_DENSITY.
constantNotes.MINERAL_DENSITY: Amount a mineral is refilled to, by density (1 low to 4 ultra).
constantNotes.MINERAL_DENSITY_PROBABILITY: Cumulative thresholds for drawing a density: a random number up to the value picks that density.
constantNotes.MINERAL_DENSITY_CHANGE: Chance that a moderate or high mineral gets a new density at a refill. Low and ultra always get a new one.
constantNotes.DEPOSIT_EXHAUST_MULTIPLY: Factor of the deposit cooldown: ceil(DEPOSIT_EXHAUST_MULTIPLY × total harvested ^ DEPOSIT_EXHAUST_POW) ticks after each harvest.
constantNotes.DEPOSIT_EXHAUST_POW: Exponent of the deposit cooldown: above 1, so the cooldown grows faster than the total harvested.
constantNotes.COMMODITIES: COMMODITIES[product] = {amount made per produce call, cooldown in ticks, components taken from the factory, level: the factory level needed (absent = any factory)}.
constantNotes.LINK_HITS_MAX: Most hits a link can have.
constantNotes.LINK_COOLDOWN: Cooldown ticks of the sending link per tile of distance to the receiving link.
constantNotes.LINK_LOSS_RATIO: Share of the sent energy that is lost on the way, rounded up.
constantNotes.SUBSCRIPTION_TOKEN: Account item "token". It is held by the account, not in a room, and trades on the market without a terminal.
constantNotes.CPU_UNLOCK: Account item "cpuUnlock", used up by Game.cpu.unlock. It trades on the market without a terminal.
constantNotes.PIXEL: Account item "pixel", made by Game.cpu.generatePixel. It trades on the market without a terminal.
constantNotes.ACCESS_KEY: Account item "accessKey", used up by Game.shard.activateAccess. It trades on the market without a terminal.
constantNotes.RESOURCES_ALL: Every resource a store can hold. transfer, withdraw, drop and terminal send accept only these names.
constantNotes.INTERSHARD_RESOURCES: The account items (token, cpuUnlock, pixel, accessKey): listed in Game.resources and traded on the market without a terminal.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYST: "X", a base mineral: tier 2 compound + X makes the tier 3 compound.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_GHODIUM: "G": not mined, made from ZK + UL. Base of the TOUGH and upgrade boosts; a nuker and generateSafeMode use it too.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_HYDROXIDE: "OH" = H + O. Tier 1 compound + OH makes the tier 2 compound.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ZYNTHIUM_KEANITE: "ZK" = Z + K. Its only use is making G together with UL.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_UTRIUM_LEMERGITE: "UL" = U + L. Its only use is making G together with ZK.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_OPS: "ops": made by a power creep with PWR_GENERATE_OPS and spent when it uses its other powers.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_SILICON: Raw resource from deposits; with utrium bars it makes wire.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_BIOMASS: Raw resource from deposits; with lemergium bars it makes cell.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_METAL: Raw resource from deposits; with zynthium bars it makes alloy.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_MIST: Raw resource from deposits; with keanium bars it makes condensate.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_UTRIUM_BAR: Compressed U: 500 U + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_LEMERGIUM_BAR: Compressed L: 500 L + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ZYNTHIUM_BAR: Compressed Z: 500 Z + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_KEANIUM_BAR: Compressed K: 500 K + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_GHODIUM_MELT: Compressed G: 500 G + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_OXIDANT: Compressed O: 500 O + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_REDUCTANT: Compressed H: 500 H + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_PURIFIER: Compressed X: 500 X + 200 energy make 100 in a factory, and back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_BATTERY: Compressed energy: 600 energy make 50 in a factory; 50 give 500 energy back.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_COMPOSITE: Shared component for higher commodities, made from utrium and zynthium bars at factory level 1.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CRYSTAL: Shared component for higher commodities, made from lemergium and keanium bars and purifier at factory level 2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_LIQUID: Shared component for higher commodities, made from oxidant, reductant and ghodium melt at factory level 3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_UTRIUM_HYDRIDE: "UH", tier 1 compound: boosts ATTACK parts, attack ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_UTRIUM_ACID: "UH2O", tier 2 compound: boosts ATTACK parts, attack ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_UTRIUM_ACID: "XUH2O", tier 3 compound: boosts ATTACK parts, attack ×4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_UTRIUM_OXIDE: "UO", tier 1 compound: boosts WORK parts, harvest ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_UTRIUM_ALKALIDE: "UHO2", tier 2 compound: boosts WORK parts, harvest ×5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_UTRIUM_ALKALIDE: "XUHO2", tier 3 compound: boosts WORK parts, harvest ×7.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_KEANIUM_HYDRIDE: "KH", tier 1 compound: boosts CARRY parts, capacity ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_KEANIUM_ACID: "KH2O", tier 2 compound: boosts CARRY parts, capacity ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_KEANIUM_ACID: "XKH2O", tier 3 compound: boosts CARRY parts, capacity ×4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_KEANIUM_OXIDE: "KO", tier 1 compound: boosts RANGED_ATTACK parts, rangedAttack and rangedMassAttack ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_KEANIUM_ALKALIDE: "KHO2", tier 2 compound: boosts RANGED_ATTACK parts, rangedAttack and rangedMassAttack ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_KEANIUM_ALKALIDE: "XKHO2", tier 3 compound: boosts RANGED_ATTACK parts, rangedAttack and rangedMassAttack ×4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_LEMERGIUM_HYDRIDE: "LH", tier 1 compound: boosts WORK parts, build and repair ×1.5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_LEMERGIUM_ACID: "LH2O", tier 2 compound: boosts WORK parts, build and repair ×1.8.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_LEMERGIUM_ACID: "XLH2O", tier 3 compound: boosts WORK parts, build and repair ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_LEMERGIUM_OXIDE: "LO", tier 1 compound: boosts HEAL parts, heal and rangedHeal ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_LEMERGIUM_ALKALIDE: "LHO2", tier 2 compound: boosts HEAL parts, heal and rangedHeal ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_LEMERGIUM_ALKALIDE: "XLHO2", tier 3 compound: boosts HEAL parts, heal and rangedHeal ×4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ZYNTHIUM_HYDRIDE: "ZH", tier 1 compound: boosts WORK parts, dismantle ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ZYNTHIUM_ACID: "ZH2O", tier 2 compound: boosts WORK parts, dismantle ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_ZYNTHIUM_ACID: "XZH2O", tier 3 compound: boosts WORK parts, dismantle ×4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ZYNTHIUM_OXIDE: "ZO", tier 1 compound: boosts MOVE parts, fatigue removed ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ZYNTHIUM_ALKALIDE: "ZHO2", tier 2 compound: boosts MOVE parts, fatigue removed ×3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_ZYNTHIUM_ALKALIDE: "XZHO2", tier 3 compound: boosts MOVE parts, fatigue removed ×4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_GHODIUM_HYDRIDE: "GH", tier 1 compound: boosts WORK parts, upgradeController ×1.5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_GHODIUM_ACID: "GH2O", tier 2 compound: boosts WORK parts, upgradeController ×1.8.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_GHODIUM_ACID: "XGH2O", tier 3 compound: boosts WORK parts, upgradeController ×2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_GHODIUM_OXIDE: "GO", tier 1 compound: boosts TOUGH parts, damage taken ×0.7.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_GHODIUM_ALKALIDE: "GHO2", tier 2 compound: boosts TOUGH parts, damage taken ×0.5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CATALYZED_GHODIUM_ALKALIDE: "XGHO2", tier 3 compound: boosts TOUGH parts, damage taken ×0.3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_WIRE: Commodity of the silicon chain, made in any factory from silicon.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_SWITCH: Commodity of the silicon chain, factory level 1.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_TRANSISTOR: Commodity of the silicon chain, factory level 2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_MICROCHIP: Commodity of the silicon chain, factory level 3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CIRCUIT: Commodity of the silicon chain, factory level 4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_DEVICE: Commodity of the silicon chain, factory level 5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CELL: Commodity of the biomass chain, made in any factory from biomass.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_PHLEGM: Commodity of the biomass chain, factory level 1.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_TISSUE: Commodity of the biomass chain, factory level 2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_MUSCLE: Commodity of the biomass chain, factory level 3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ORGANOID: Commodity of the biomass chain, factory level 4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ORGANISM: Commodity of the biomass chain, factory level 5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ALLOY: Commodity of the metal chain, made in any factory from metal.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_TUBE: Commodity of the metal chain, factory level 1.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_FIXTURES: Commodity of the metal chain, factory level 2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_FRAME: Commodity of the metal chain, factory level 3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_HYDRAULICS: Commodity of the metal chain, factory level 4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_MACHINE: Commodity of the metal chain, factory level 5.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CONDENSATE: Commodity of the mist chain, made in any factory from mist.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_CONCENTRATE: Commodity of the mist chain, factory level 1.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_EXTRACT: Commodity of the mist chain, factory level 2.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_SPIRIT: Commodity of the mist chain, factory level 3.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_EMANATION: Commodity of the mist chain, factory level 4.
constantNotes.RESOURCE_ESSENCE: Commodity of the mist chain, factory level 5.
constantNotes.RAMPART_DECAY_AMOUNT: Hits a rampart loses at each decay step.
constantNotes.RAMPART_DECAY_TIME: Ticks between two decay steps of a rampart.
constantNotes.ENERGY_DECAY: Divisor of the loss of a dropped resource pile: each tick it loses ceil(amount / 1000).
constantNotes.ROAD_WEAROUT: Ticks the next decay step of a road comes closer per body part of a creep that steps on it.
constantNotes.ROAD_WEAROUT_POWER_CREEP: Ticks the next decay step of a road comes closer when a power creep steps on it.
constantNotes.ROAD_DECAY_AMOUNT: Hits a road loses at each decay step; multiplied on swamp and on a natural wall.
constantNotes.ROAD_DECAY_TIME: Ticks between two decay steps of a road.
constantNotes.POWER_BANK_DECAY: Ticks a power bank exists before it vanishes together with its power.
constantNotes.DEPOSIT_DECAY_TIME: Ticks a deposit stays after it appeared or was last harvested; then it vanishes.
constantNotes.CONTAINER_DECAY: Hits a container loses at each decay step.
constantNotes.CONTAINER_DECAY_TIME: Ticks between decay steps of a container in a room without a controller or with one at level 0.
constantNotes.CONTAINER_DECAY_TIME_OWNED: Ticks between decay steps of a container in a room whose controller has level 1 or more.
constantNotes.TOMBSTONE_DECAY_PER_PART: Ticks a tombstone lasts per body part of the dead creep.
constantNotes.TOMBSTONE_DECAY_POWER_CREEP: Ticks the tombstone of a power creep lasts.
constantNotes.RUIN_DECAY: Ticks a ruin lasts, unless RUIN_DECAY_STRUCTURES names its structure type.
constantNotes.RUIN_DECAY_STRUCTURES: Ruin lifetime by structure type where it differs: the ruin of a power bank lasts 10 ticks.
constantNotes.PORTAL_DECAY: Ticks a portal has left once it has turned unstable.
constantNotes.STRONGHOLD_DECAY_TICKS: Ticks a stronghold lives after its deploy, ±10%; then all of it is removed.
constantNotes.NUKER_COOLDOWN: Ticks a nuker cannot launch after a launch, and after it was built.
constantNotes.NUKER_ENERGY_CAPACITY: Energy a nuker holds. A launch needs it full and uses all of it.
constantNotes.NUKER_GHODIUM_CAPACITY: Ghodium a nuker holds. A launch needs it full and uses all of it.
constantNotes.NUKE_LAND_TIME: Ticks from the launch of a nuke to its landing.
constantNotes.NUKE_RANGE: Largest distance in rooms, on each axis, between the room of the nuker and the target room.
constantNotes.NUKE_DAMAGE: Damage to structures by range from the landing tile: key 0 is the tile itself, key 2 the rest of the 5 × 5 tiles around it.
constantNotes.INVADERS_ENERGY_GOAL: Energy harvested from the sources of a room that makes a raid due; after each raid the goal is drawn anew around this value.
constantNotes.INVADER_CORE_HITS: Hits of an invader core, the same at every level.
constantNotes.INVADER_CORE_CREEP_SPAWN_TIME: Ticks per body part a stronghold core needs to spawn a defender, by core level; 0 means that level spawns none.
constantNotes.INVADER_CORE_EXPAND_TIME: Ticks between two lesser cores a stronghold sends into nearby rooms, by stronghold level.
constantNotes.INVADER_CORE_CONTROLLER_POWER: Ticks of reservation an invader core adds for itself, or takes off the reservation of a player, each tick.
constantNotes.INVADER_CORE_CONTROLLER_DOWNGRADE: Downgrade timer a stronghold core keeps on a controller it owns.
constantNotes.STRONGHOLD_RAMPART_HITS: Hits of the ramparts of a stronghold by level; also the value its fortifier repairs them back to.
constantNotes.WORLD_WIDTH: Deprecated: width of the world in rooms. Use Game.map.getWorldSize().
constantNotes.WORLD_HEIGHT: Deprecated: height of the world in rooms. Use Game.map.getWorldSize().
constantNotes.MODE_SIMULATION: Defined as null; the public server code does not use it.
constantNotes.MODE_WORLD: Defined as null; the public server code does not use it.
constantNotes.TERRAIN_MASK_WALL: Terrain bit of a natural wall.
constantNotes.TERRAIN_MASK_LAVA: A third terrain bit; the public server code does not use it.
constantNotes.FLAGS_LIMIT: Most flags a player can have; createFlag returns ERR_FULL beyond it.
constantNotes.PIXEL_CPU_COST: Bucket CPU that Game.cpu.generatePixel turns into one pixel.
constantNotes.PORTAL_UNSTABLE: Milliseconds (10 days): the stable time the reference gives for a portal. The public server code does not read it.
constantNotes.PORTAL_MIN_TIMEOUT: Milliseconds (12 days): a portal timing value of the official server. The public server code does not read it.
constantNotes.PORTAL_MAX_TIMEOUT: Milliseconds (22 days): a portal timing value of the official server. The public server code does not read it.
constantNotes.SYSTEM_USERNAME: User name of the game itself: the author of signs it puts on controllers and the owner of the ruins a respawn leaves.
constantNotes.SIGN_PLANNED_AREA: Text of the controller sign the game sets in a sector where a novice or respawn area is planned.
constantNotes.POWER_BANK_CAPACITY_MAX: Upper end of the power rolled for a new power bank; a critical bank gets this amount on top.
constantNotes.POWER_BANK_CAPACITY_MIN: Lower end of the power rolled for a new power bank.
constantNotes.POWER_BANK_CAPACITY_CRIT: Chance that a new power bank gets POWER_BANK_CAPACITY_MAX extra power.
constantNotes.POWER_BANK_HIT_BACK: Share of the damage done to a power bank that the attacker takes itself.
constantNotes.POWER_BANK_RESPAWN_TIME: Base number of ticks between two power banks in one highway room; the real wait is 0.75 to 1.25 times this.
constantNotes.POWER_SPAWN_ENERGY_RATIO: Energy burned with each unit of power in processPower.
constantNotes.POWER_LEVEL_MULTIPLY: Factor of the Global Power Level formula: level n needs POWER_LEVEL_MULTIPLY × n^POWER_LEVEL_POW processed power in total.
constantNotes.POWER_LEVEL_POW: Exponent of the Global Power Level formula.
constantNotes.POWER_CREEP_SPAWN_COOLDOWN: Milliseconds of real time after a death before the power creep can be spawned again (8 hours).
constantNotes.POWER_CREEP_DELETE_COOLDOWN: Milliseconds of real time between delete() and the removal of the power creep (24 hours).
constantNotes.POWER_CREEP_MAX_LEVEL: Highest level of a power creep.
constantNotes.POWER_CREEP_LIFE_TIME: Ticks a power creep lives after a spawn or a renew.
constantNotes.POWER_CLASS: Classes PowerCreep.create accepts; OPERATOR is the only one.
constantNotes.POWER_INFO: Per power: class, creep level needed for power levels 1–5, cooldown, and where they apply range, duration, ops cost and effect per level.
constantNotes.PWR_GENERATE_OPS: Adds ops to the power creep's own store.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN: Shortens the spawn time of creeps started at the target spawn.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_TOWER: Raises attack, heal and repair of the target tower.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_STORAGE: Raises the capacity of the target storage.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_LAB: Raises the amount the target lab handles per reaction.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION: Fills the extensions of the room at once with energy from the target storage, terminal, factory or container.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_OBSERVER: Lets the target observer look at a room at any distance.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_TERMINAL: Lowers the energy cost of transfers and the cooldown of the target terminal.
constantNotes.PWR_DISRUPT_SPAWN: Pauses the creep being spawned at the target spawn.
constantNotes.PWR_DISRUPT_TOWER: Lowers attack, heal and repair of the target tower.
constantNotes.PWR_DISRUPT_SOURCE: Stops the regeneration timer of the target source.
constantNotes.PWR_SHIELD: Puts a temporary rampart on the power creep's own tile.
constantNotes.PWR_REGEN_SOURCE: Adds energy to the target source every 15 ticks.
constantNotes.PWR_REGEN_MINERAL: Adds units to the target mineral every 10 ticks.
constantNotes.PWR_DISRUPT_TERMINAL: Blocks withdrawing from the target terminal.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_POWER: Lets the target power spawn process more power per processPower call.
constantNotes.PWR_FORTIFY: Makes the target wall or rampart take no damage from attacks.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_CONTROLLER: Raises the upgrade limit per tick of a level 8 controller.
constantNotes.PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY: Sets the level of the target factory and lets it produce commodities of that level.
constantNotes.EFFECT_INVULNERABILITY: Effect id on a stronghold core before it deploys and on the controller of a stronghold room: attacks on the object are refused.
constantNotes.EFFECT_COLLAPSE_TIMER: Effect id on the structures of a deployed stronghold: when it runs out, they are removed.
constantNotes.OK: The call passed its checks and the action is queued for the end of the tick. It can still fail there.
constantNotes.ERR_NOT_OWNER: The object, or the room it is in, is not yours to use this way.
constantNotes.ERR_NO_PATH: No path or route to the target was found.
constantNotes.ERR_NAME_EXISTS: The name is already in use (creep, spawn, flag or power creep).
constantNotes.ERR_BUSY: The object cannot act now: a creep that is still spawning, a spawn that is already spawning, a power creep that is not in the world.
constantNotes.ERR_NOT_FOUND: What the call refers to is not there: no step of the path at this position, no queued order to cancel, no parts to boost.
constantNotes.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_ENERGY: Not enough energy for the action. Same number as ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES.
constantNotes.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES: The object lacks the resource or the amount the action needs.
constantNotes.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_EXTENSIONS: Spawns and extensions hold too little energy for the body. Same number as ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES.
constantNotes.ERR_INVALID_TARGET: The target is the wrong kind of object, does not exist, or cannot take this action.
constantNotes.ERR_FULL: The target cannot take more, or a limit is reached (store, flags, construction sites, deals per tick).
constantNotes.ERR_NOT_IN_RANGE: The target is too far away for this action.
constantNotes.ERR_INVALID_ARGS: An argument has the wrong type or a value that is not allowed.
constantNotes.ERR_TIRED: Still cooling down: fatigue of a creep or the cooldown of a structure.
constantNotes.ERR_NO_BODYPART: The creep has no working body part of the kind this action needs.
constantNotes.ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH: The room controller level is too low for this structure or action.
constantNotes.ERR_GCL_NOT_ENOUGH: Your Global Control Level does not allow one more room.
constantNotes.ERR_ACCESS_DENIED: You have no access to this restricted shard. Returned by claimController, reserveController and upgradeController.
constantNotes.EVENT_ATTACK: A creep, a tower or a nuke damaged something. data: targetId, damage, attackType.
constantNotes.EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED: A creep died, or a structure was destroyed by damage. data: type.
constantNotes.EVENT_ATTACK_CONTROLLER: attackController was used on the controller of the room. No data.
constantNotes.EVENT_BUILD: A creep built on a construction site. data: targetId, amount, structureType, x, y, incomplete.
constantNotes.EVENT_HARVEST: A creep harvested a source or a mineral. data: targetId, amount.
constantNotes.EVENT_HEAL: A creep or a tower healed a creep. data: targetId, amount, healType.
constantNotes.EVENT_REPAIR: A creep or a tower repaired a structure. data: targetId, amount, energySpent.
constantNotes.EVENT_RESERVE_CONTROLLER: The controller was reserved. data: amount, the ticks added.
constantNotes.EVENT_UPGRADE_CONTROLLER: The controller was upgraded. data: amount, energySpent.
constantNotes.EVENT_EXIT: A creep left the room through an exit. data: room, x, y, where it arrives.
constantNotes.EVENT_POWER: A power creep used a power. data: power, targetId.
constantNotes.EVENT_TRANSFER: Resources moved from one object to another by transfer, withdraw or a link. data: targetId, resourceType, amount.
constantNotes.EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_RANGED: attackType of Creep.rangedAttack and of a tower attack.
constantNotes.EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_RANGED_MASS: attackType of Creep.rangedMassAttack; one event per target hit.
constantNotes.EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_HIT_BACK: attackType of the damage that a creep attacked in melee, or a power bank, deals back.
constantNotes.EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_NUKE: attackType of the damage from a landing nuke.
constantNotes.EVENT_HEAL_TYPE_RANGED: healType of Creep.rangedHeal and of a tower heal.
constantNotes.FIND_EXIT_TOP: Open tiles on the top edge (y = 0), as positions. Same number as TOP.
constantNotes.FIND_EXIT_RIGHT: Open tiles on the right edge (x = 49), as positions. Same number as RIGHT.
constantNotes.FIND_EXIT_BOTTOM: Open tiles on the bottom edge (y = 49), as positions. Same number as BOTTOM.
constantNotes.FIND_EXIT_LEFT: Open tiles on the left edge (x = 0), as positions. Same number as LEFT.
constantNotes.FIND_EXIT: All open edge tiles of the room, as positions.
constantNotes.FIND_CREEPS: All creeps in the room that have finished spawning.
constantNotes.FIND_MY_CREEPS: Your creeps in the room that have finished spawning.
constantNotes.FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS: Every creep that is not yours: enemies, allies, invaders, source keepers.
constantNotes.FIND_DROPPED_RESOURCES: Piles lying on the ground, of any resource.
constantNotes.FIND_STRUCTURES: Every structure, with or without an owner.
constantNotes.FIND_MY_STRUCTURES: Structures you own. Roads, containers and walls have no owner and are not in it.
constantNotes.FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES: Structures with an owner other than you. Roads, containers and walls are not in it.
constantNotes.FIND_NUKES: Nukes on their way to this room.
constantNotes.FIND_HOSTILE_POWER_CREEPS: Power creeps that are not yours.
constantNotes.LOOK_ENERGY: Dropped resources of any kind; the same list as LOOK_RESOURCES.
constantNotes.LOOK_STRUCTURES: All structures on the tile; a road, a rampart and a building can share one.
constantNotes.LOOK_TERRAIN: The terrain of the tile as the string "plain", "swamp" or "wall".
constantNotes.COLORS_ALL: List of the ten COLOR_* values; a flag color must be one of them.
constantNotes.OBSTACLE_OBJECT_TYPES: Object types a creep cannot walk onto. Roads, containers and ramparts are not in the list.
constantNotes.SPAWN_ENERGY_CAPACITY: Energy a spawn holds. Also the room total below which a spawn refills itself by 1 per tick.
constantNotes.WALL_HITS: Hits of a wall when it is built.
constantNotes.WALL_HITS_MAX: Hits a wall can be repaired up to, in a room at level 2 or more.
constantNotes.ROAD_HITS: Hits of a road on plain. On swamp and on a wall tile it is multiplied by the road ratio of that terrain.
constantNotes.STORAGE_CAPACITY: All resources together that a storage holds.
constantNotes.CONSTRUCTION_COST: Energy to build each structure type. Only the types listed here can be built, repaired, dismantled or destroyed with destroy().
constantNotes.CONSTRUCTION_COST_ROAD_SWAMP_RATIO: Factor on the cost, hits and decay of a road on swamp.
constantNotes.CONSTRUCTION_COST_ROAD_WALL_RATIO: Factor on the cost, hits and decay of a road on a wall tile (a tunnel).
constantNotes.OBSERVER_RANGE: Rooms an observer reaches in each direction.
constantNotes.MAX_CONSTRUCTION_SITES: Construction sites one player may have at a time, over all rooms.
constantNotes.CONTAINER_CAPACITY: All resources together that a container holds.
constantNotes.FACTORY_CAPACITY: All resources together that a factory holds.
constantNotes.RAMPART_HITS: Hits of a rampart when it is built.
constantNotes.RAMPART_HITS_MAX: Hits a rampart can be repaired up to, by the level of its owner's room. Below level 2 there is no entry: 0.
constantNotes.EXTENSION_ENERGY_CAPACITY: Energy one extension holds, by room level.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_LEVELS: Upgrade energy a controller needs at each level to reach the next one.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_STRUCTURES: How many structures of each type a room may have at each level; construction sites count too.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_DOWNGRADE: Full downgrade timer in ticks at each level. When it runs out the controller loses a level.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_DOWNGRADE_RESTORE: Ticks added to the downgrade timer in a tick with an upgrade. The level only rises while the timer is within this many ticks of full.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_DOWNGRADE_SAFEMODE_THRESHOLD: Safe mode cannot be activated once the downgrade timer is more than this many ticks below half of its maximum.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_CLAIM_DOWNGRADE: Ticks one CLAIM part takes off the downgrade timer of an owned controller per attackController.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_RESERVE: Reservation ticks one CLAIM part adds per reserveController, or takes off per attackController.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_MAX_UPGRADE_PER_TICK: Energy a level 8 controller takes per tick from all creeps together.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_ATTACK_BLOCKED_UPGRADE: Ticks after an attackController hit in which the controller cannot be upgraded, hit again, or put into safe mode.
constantNotes.CONTROLLER_NUKE_BLOCKED_UPGRADE: Ticks without upgrading after a nuke has landed in the room.
constantNotes.SAFE_MODE_COOLDOWN: Ticks before a controller can start safe mode again; counted from an activation, a lost level or an unclaim.
constantNotes.SAFE_MODE_COST: Ghodium a creep spends in generateSafeMode for one more safe mode in stock.
constantNotes.GCL_POW: Exponent of the GCL formula: level n needs GCL_MULTIPLY × (n − 1) ^ GCL_POW points in total.
constantNotes.GCL_NOVICE: A player who already owns this many rooms cannot claim another one inside a novice area.
constantNotes.TOWER_ENERGY_COST: Energy per tower action: attack, heal or repair.
constantNotes.TOWER_POWER_ATTACK: Damage of a tower shot at range 5 or less.
constantNotes.TOWER_POWER_HEAL: Hits a tower heals at range 5 or less.
constantNotes.TOWER_POWER_REPAIR: Hits a tower repairs at range 5 or less.
constantNotes.TOWER_OPTIMAL_RANGE: Up to this range a tower works at full power.
constantNotes.TOWER_FALLOFF_RANGE: From this range on a tower works at its lowest power.
constantNotes.TOWER_FALLOFF: Share of its power a tower loses at TOWER_FALLOFF_RANGE and beyond; in between the loss grows in a straight line.
constantNotes.BODYPART_COST: Energy each body part type costs to spawn.
constantNotes.HARVEST_POWER: Energy one WORK part takes from a source per tick.
constantNotes.HARVEST_MINERAL_POWER: Mineral one WORK part takes per harvest.
constantNotes.HARVEST_DEPOSIT_POWER: Deposit resource one WORK part takes per harvest.
constantNotes.REPAIR_POWER: Hits one WORK part repairs per tick.
constantNotes.DISMANTLE_POWER: Hits one WORK part takes off a structure per tick with dismantle.
constantNotes.BUILD_POWER: Energy one WORK part puts into a construction site per tick.
constantNotes.ATTACK_POWER: Damage of one ATTACK part per tick.
constantNotes.UPGRADE_CONTROLLER_POWER: Energy one WORK part puts into a controller per tick.
constantNotes.RANGED_ATTACK_POWER: Damage of one RANGED_ATTACK part per tick, and the base of rangedMassAttack.
constantNotes.HEAL_POWER: Hits one HEAL part restores per tick with heal (range 1).
constantNotes.RANGED_HEAL_POWER: Hits one HEAL part restores per tick with rangedHeal (range 3).
constantNotes.REPAIR_COST: Energy a creep pays per hit it repairs.
constantNotes.DISMANTLE_COST: Energy a creep gets per hit it dismantles.
constantNotes.MAX_CREEP_SIZE: Most body parts a creep can have.
constantNotes.BODYPARTS_ALL: Every body part type. A body with anything else is refused.
constantNotes.CREEP_LIFE_TIME: Ticks a creep lives after leaving the spawn. Also the ceiling for renewCreep.
constantNotes.CREEP_CLAIM_LIFE_TIME: Ticks a creep with a CLAIM part lives.
constantNotes.CREEP_CORPSE_RATE: Share of the body value a creep leaves when it dies or kills itself, before scaling by the life it had left. recycleCreep uses 1 instead.
constantNotes.CREEP_PART_MAX_ENERGY: Most energy one body part gives back when a creep dies or is recycled.
constantNotes.SPAWN_ENERGY_START: Energy in the first spawn a player places.
constantNotes.CREEP_SPAWN_TIME: Ticks of spawning per body part.
constantNotes.SPAWN_RENEW_RATIO: Factor of renewCreep against spawning: one call gives this many times the life, and costs this many times the energy, of one tick of spawning the same body.

lineSources.t: engine: full hits are only checked after the fee
wiki: Making your own console functions

engine creeps.js: attack, part check and safe mode check below it
engine: the check, first in withdraw, then in each blocked call
engine: a tower attack has no safe mode check

engine: range check, the same line in runReaction and reverseReaction

engine: created without an id (the same line is in spawnCreep)

glossary.means: A room you do not own whose sources you mine, usually with its controller reserved.
To upgrade a controller; a praiser is an upgrader creep.
A room kept only to pour energy into its controller for global control level.
Four creeps that move and fight as a 2 x 2 block.
Two creeps that fight as a pair, usually an attacker or dismantler with a healer.
To make towers spend their energy on a creep that heals more than they hit.
Healing a creep before it is hit, in the tick in which the damage is expected.
Shooting a melee creep from range while stepping away from it.
A creep that takes the fire for a group, usually behind boosted TOUGH parts.
A creep built on RANGED_ATTACK parts that fires rangedMassAttack every tick.
Short for rangedMassAttack.
A creep that hops back and forth between two rooms because it stays on an exit tile.
Source keeper; an SK room is one of the keeper rooms around the centre of a sector.
Room controller level, 1 to 8.
Global control level: how many rooms an account may own.
Global power level: how many power creep levels an account can hand out.
Non-coding player: an account that runs an open-source bot without changing it.
Nickname for the NPC invader creeps.
Keeping the parsed Memory object in the global scope to skip the JSON parse of each tick.
The global scope of your script, used as a cache that is lost on every global reset.
The server throws your isolate away; all variables and the module cache start empty.
Unused CPU saved up to a cap, which a later tick may spend.
A queued action: any call that changes the game and returns OK, at 0.2 CPU.
A bot built as processes with priorities that a kernel and scheduler run.
A fixed job per creep, stored in its memory, with one module of code per job.
A creep with a general body that takes whatever task a manager hands it.
Storing the id of a chosen target and checking it each tick instead of searching again.
A miner that stays at its source while haulers carry; drop, container and link mining are its forms.
Tier 3 boost: the catalysed compound of a boost, with the strongest effect; T1 and T2 are the weaker tiers.
Safe mode, written as one word.
League of Automated Nations: a community register of alliances and their members.
Public test realm: a copy of the world for testing.
A room on the border between sectors, without controller or sources.
Power bank.
Power creep; the only class so far is the operator.
Invader core: the NPC structure that reserves rooms and, at higher levels, heads a stronghold.
A room with far more roads than its traffic needs.
A spawn that kills a hostile creep on the last free tile next to it to place its new creep.
A walled start area for new players; also called novice area.
One of 100 strings of up to 100 KB kept beside Memory.
Cost matrix.

rows.label: Upgrade
rows.unit: energy (15 per tick cap at RCL 8)

entries.name: Harvest a source and haul the energy
entries.title: Harvest a source and haul the energy
entries.summary: A miner that stays at the source and haulers that carry: the standard income loop.

steps.text: Find the sources once (FIND_SOURCES) and keep their ids; pick the mining tile next to each.
Miner: 5 WORK drain a 3000 source (2 per WORK per tick, refill every 300 ticks). Add 1 CARRY if it should repair or fill a link.
Miner at range 1, every tick. Without free store the energy drops on its tile, into a container if it stands on one.
Optional container under the miner (5000 energy, holds 2000); the miner repairs it with its own energy.
Hauler takes from the container; or Creep.pickup for a pile on the ground.
Hauler fills spawn, extensions, towers, then storage. Check store.getFreeCapacity(RESOURCE_ENERGY) first.

tasks: mine a source and bring the energy home
pitfalls: Hauler size: energy per tick × round trip ticks ÷ 50 CARRY parts. A source gives 10 per tick.
A pile on the ground loses ceil(amount / 1000) per tick; a container loses nothing but needs repair.
Each harvest, withdraw, transfer and move costs 0.2 CPU; fewer, larger haulers are cheaper than many small ones.

entries.name: Reserve a neighbouring room and mine it
entries.title: Reserve a neighbouring room and mine it
entries.summary: Take energy from a room you do not own: reserve its controller, mine its sources, carry the energy home.

steps.text: Pick a neighbour with a controller that nobody owns or has reserved (needs vision: send a scout or use an observer).
Reserver with 2 CLAIM + 2 MOVE (1300 energy, lives 600 ticks, no renew). 2 CLAIM gain 1 tick per tick; stop calling near 5000.
Miner per source: 5 WORK once reserved (3000 per 300 ticks); unreserved it is only 1500.
Container at each source and roads on the haul path. Only roads and containers can be built there.
Keep them up: a remote container costs 0.5 energy per tick, a plain road tile 0.001.
Haulers take from the container and carry home to storage or a link.

tasks: harvest in a room I do not own
pitfalls: Harvest returns ERR_NOT_OWNER when another player or an invader core holds the reservation. Kill the core, then attackController or wait.
Harvesting feeds the invader counter: expect a raid about every 100,000 energy mined, unless all neighbours of the room are owned or reserved.
Remote containers decay five times faster than in your own room: 5000 ticks from full to gone.
No vision of the room without a creep in it: keep ids and positions in memory.

entries.name: Claim a new room and get it running
entries.title: Claim a new room and get it running
entries.summary: Claim the controller, then build the first spawn with creeps from an existing room.

steps.text: You need Game.gcl.level above the number of rooms you own.
Check the way there; the claimer has 600 ticks to arrive.
Claimer: 1 CLAIM + MOVE (650 energy), range 1. The controller must be level 0 and not reserved by someone else.
Place the spawn site (15,000 energy to build).
Send builders that harvest in the new room: 5 energy per WORK per tick.
Upgrade within 20,000 ticks or the level 1 controller downgrades and the room is lost.

tasks: build a spawn in a new room
pitfalls: Old structures of a previous owner stay and do not work for you; destroy() them or use what is in them first (withdraw works).
A claimed room starts with no safe mode in stock (check controller.safeModeAvailable); each level gained adds one.
Keep sending energy and creeps until the room has its own spawn and extensions.

entries.name: Tower logic: attack, heal, repair
entries.title: Tower logic: attack, heal, repair
entries.summary: One action per tower per tick, 10 energy each. Decide in this order.

steps.text: FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS once per room and tick; share the result between towers.
Shoot when the total damage of your towers at the target's range beats what its healers can restore; otherwise hold fire and keep the energy. All towers on one target.
Heal damaged creeps of yours in the room (400 close, 100 far).
Repair only what is urgent or close: a rampart about to fall, a road or container in range 5. Leave the rest to creeps, which get 100 hits per energy.
Keep towers filled; a hauler refills below a threshold so a raid does not start with empty towers.

tasks: what should towers do each tick
pitfalls: If the script calls several actions on one tower, only one runs: heal, else repair, else attack.
Damage at range: 600 up to 5, 150 from 20. Enemies at the edge of the room take a quarter.
A boosted healer restores 48 per HEAL part; count that before you spend energy.

entries.name: Link network
entries.title: Link network
entries.summary: Links carry energy across a room without haulers: source links send, a storage or controller link receives.

steps.text: Links from room level 5 (2), 6 (3), 7 (4), 8 (6); 5000 energy each. Put one within range 1 of each miner and one next to storage.
The miner (needs CARRY) puts its harvest into the source link.
When the source link is nearly full and has no cooldown, send to the receiver. 3% is lost; the sender waits 1 tick per tile of distance.
A filler at storage empties the receiving link, or upgraders take from a controller link.

pitfalls: A link holds 800. Sending small amounts wastes cooldown: wait until at least a few hundred are in.
The receiving link must have room. Without an amount only what fits is sent, and a full receiver gets nothing although the call returns OK; an amount above the free space returns ERR_FULL.
A miner with 5 WORK makes 10 per tick, so a source link fills in 80 ticks; across 30 tiles the cooldown is still shorter than that.

entries.name: Labs: reactions and boosting
entries.title: Labs: reactions and boosting
entries.summary: Two source labs feed the others; the product is either stored or used to boost creeps.

steps.text: Labs from room level 6 (3), 7 (6), 8 (10). Lay them out so every lab is within range 2 of the two source labs.
A hauler loads one reagent into each source lab (a lab holds 3000 of one mineral) and 2000 energy into labs that boost.
Each product lab calls runReaction(source1, source2) when its cooldown is 0: 5 + 5 → 5, then REACTION_TIME[product] ticks of cooldown.
Empty the product labs to terminal or storage; change reagents only when the labs are empty.
To boost: the creep stands next to a lab holding the compound; 30 compound + 20 energy per body part.
Before a boosted creep dies or is renewed: returns 15 compound per part on the ground.

pitfalls: Tier chain for one boost: base minerals → OH and the tier 1 compound → tier 2 (with OH) → tier 3 (with X). A full tier 3 boost of 10 parts needs 300 compound.
A boost lasts the creep's life. renewCreep removes all boosts.
Boost before the creep leaves: spawn it, walk it to the lab, boost, then send it out.
unboostCreep puts a long cooldown on the lab that does it, per removed part. Use a lab that runs no reactions.
A lab keeps its mineral type until the last unit is out; a leftover of fewer than 5 units has to be withdrawn by a creep.

entries.name: Terminal and market
entries.title: Terminal and market
entries.summary: Move resources between rooms and trade them for credits.

steps.text: Between rooms: send(resource, amount, roomName). The sender pays ceil(amount × (1 − e^(−distance/30))) energy; 10 ticks cooldown.
Read orders with a plain filter object, e.g. {type: ORDER_BUY, resourceType}; cache the result, the call is expensive.
Add the energy cost of the transfer to the price before choosing an order.
deal(orderId, amount, yourRoomName): instant, your terminal pays the energy, at most 10 deals per tick.
Or place your own order: 5% of price × amount in credits up front, then wait for a taker.

pitfalls: A terminal holds 300,000 in total; leave room for incoming deliveries.
Keep energy in the terminal for the fees: sending 1,000 over 10 rooms costs about 284.
A private server may have no other traders; the market can be empty.
send and deal return OK before anything has moved. The transfer is listed in Game.market.outgoingTransactions or incomingTransactions in the next tick if it happened.
A filled order stays in Game.market.orders as inactive and counts toward the limit of 300: cancel it.
An order ends after 30 days of real time.

entries.name: Safe mode: when and how
entries.title: Safe mode: when and how
entries.summary: A last line of defence: 20,000 ticks in which other players' creeps can do no harm in the room.

steps.text: Check the stock (and safeModeCooldown, which must be undefined).
Trigger on real damage to spawn, storage, terminal or towers, or on a rampart about to fall, not on any hostile in the room.
Activate. ERR_BUSY if another of your rooms is already in safe mode.
Restock later: a creep carrying 1000 ghodium next to the controller adds one.

pitfalls: Cooldown 50,000 ticks after use, and a controller downgrade empties the stock.
Not possible while upgradeBlocked (after attackController) or with a downgrade timer far below half.
Safe mode stops invaders too, but it is wasted on a normal raid: towers handle those.

entries.name: Observer and power banks
entries.title: Observer and power banks
entries.summary: From room level 8: watch highway rooms with an observer, break power banks, process the power into GPL.

steps.text: One room per tick, up to 10 rooms away; the room is visible in the next tick. Cycle through the highway rooms in range.
Next tick: FIND_STRUCTURES filtered by STRUCTURE_POWER_BANK (or FIND_DEPOSITS). Check power and ticksToDecay.
Attackers with healers: the bank has 2,000,000 hits and returns 50% of each hit. Start early enough to finish before it decays (5000 ticks).
When it breaks, its 500–10,000 power stays in a ruin for 10 ticks (Creep.withdraw), then drops as a pile; have haulers there by then.
At home: 1 power + 50 energy per tick → 1 GPL progress.

pitfalls: Travel time counts: creeps live 1500 ticks, and other players go for the same banks.
Free tiles around the bank limit how many attackers fit.
With a chance of 30 % a bank gets 5000 power on top of the roll, so a bank can hold close to 10,000. Read bank.power before you size the haulers.
A destroyed bank leaves a ruin that holds the power for 10 ticks: withdraw from the ruin. Only after that does the power lie on the ground.
A bank that runs out of time is removed with its power: nothing drops.
The hit-back is computed for any damage to the bank, ranged attacks included.
A highway room gets its next bank about 37,500 to 62,500 ticks after the last one appeared.
Withdraw does not work on a power bank; the power is only reachable by destroying it.
A power creep can renew next to a power bank, which makes banks stepping stones for long trips.
Under PWR_OPERATE_POWER a power spawn processes up to 6 power per tick instead of 1.

entries.name: Power creeps
entries.title: Power creeps
entries.summary: Spend GPL levels on a power creep and use its powers in your rooms.

steps.text: PowerCreep.create(name, POWER_CLASS.OPERATOR) uses one free GPL level.
Each further GPL level buys one power level; see POWER_INFO for what each power needs.
Game.powerCreeps[name].spawn(powerSpawn). It lives 5000 ticks.
Once per room, next to the controller, before any power works there.
PWR_GENERATE_OPS for ops, then the operate powers on spawn, tower, lab, storage or factory, or PWR_REGEN_SOURCE on a source, as needed.
Renew at the power spawn before ticksToLive runs out; a death costs 8 hours.

pitfalls: enableRoom is needed only in rooms that have a controller; in highway and centre rooms powers work at once.
One power per creep per tick, and each power has its own cooldown.
Renewing is free and works at any power bank and at any active power spawn, so there is no reason to let a power creep die of age.
suicide() counts as a death and starts the same cooldown.
Room.find(FIND_MY_CREEPS) and Game.creeps do not contain power creeps: loop over Game.powerCreeps.

entries.name: Spawn, renew, recycle
entries.title: Spawn, renew, recycle
entries.summary: Paying for creeps and deciding between a new creep, a renewed one and a recycled one.

steps.text: The body must cost no more than this: 300 per spawn plus the extensions.
Body cost is the sum of BODYPART_COST; spawning takes 3 ticks per part; at most 50 parts. dryRun tests without spending.
A free spawn can renew an adjacent creep: +floor(600 / parts) ticks per call. Not for CLAIM creeps; removes boosts.
A creep that is no longer needed walks to a spawn: refund by remaining life, up to 125 per part.

tasks: how long does it take to spawn a creep
pitfalls: One spawn can keep at most 500 body parts alive (1500 ticks of life ÷ 3 ticks per part).
Part order matters in a fight: damage starts at the front.
Replace a creep early enough: spawn time plus travel time before the old one dies.

constants.name: BODYPART_COST
constants.value: {move: 50, work: 100, attack: 80, carry: 50, heal: 250, ranged_attack: 150, tough: 10, claim: 600}

entries.name: Deal with invaders and invader cores
entries.title: Deal with invaders and invader cores
entries.summary: Raids come with the energy you mine. In your own room towers handle them; in remote rooms you need a guard or you leave for a while.

steps.text: FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS and check creep.owner.username === "Invader"; FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES for an invader core.
Own room: focus all towers on one invader, healers first.
Remote room: a guard with ATTACK or RANGED_ATTACK and HEAL. Small invaders have 10 parts; boosted ones heal or hit for two to four times that.
Invader core (level 0): 100,000 hits, no defence. A few ATTACK parts for a few hundred ticks.
After the core is dead its reservation remains; wear it down with CLAIM parts or wait until it runs out, then reserve again.

tasks: get rid of an invader core
pitfalls: An invader lives 1500 ticks and never leaves its room. Pulling miners out and waiting is a valid answer for a weak room.
Raids stop when every neighbour of the room is owned or reserved, or when the sector has no stronghold.

entries.name: Build and keep roads and containers
entries.title: Build and keep roads and containers
entries.summary: What roads and containers cost to build and to keep, and who repairs them.

steps.text: Plan the path once with plainCost 2, swampCost 10 and existing roads at 1; store it.
Place sites along it: 300 energy per plain tile, 1500 on swamp. Mind the limit of 100 sites.
Range 3, 5 energy per WORK per tick.
A hauler with one WORK repairs the tile it walks on, or a repairer walks the road when hits fall below a threshold. Range 3.

pitfalls: A road halves the MOVE parts a loaded hauler needs. It pays when enough weight crosses it; it costs 1 energy per 1000 ticks per plain tile plus wear from traffic.
Traffic wears roads: every step moves the next decay closer by 1 tick per body part.
repair on a full road still costs 0.2 CPU: check hits first.

entries.name: Mine a mineral
entries.title: Mine a mineral
entries.summary: From room level 6: an extractor on the mineral, a miner with many WORK parts that harvests every 6 ticks, and a hauler that takes the mineral to the terminal or storage.

steps.text: room.find(FIND_MINERALS)[0] is the mineral of the room. Read mineralType and mineralAmount and keep its id.
STRUCTURE_EXTRACTOR on the mineral's position: 5000 energy, one per room from room level 6. A container on a free tile next to the mineral gives the miner a place to stand and drop.
Miner: mostly WORK. Each WORK takes 1 unit per harvest and a harvest is possible every 6 ticks, so 30 WORK bring 5 units per tick.
harvest(mineral) at range 1 in the ticks where extractor.cooldown is 0; skip the call otherwise.
A hauler empties the container (or picks up the pile) and carries the mineral to the terminal or storage.
At mineralAmount 0 the mineral refills after 50,000 ticks: recycle the miner and spawn the next one shortly before the timer ends.

pitfalls: Mine the mineral down to 0: the refill timer starts only then.
Two miners must harvest in the same tick. If they alternate, each one's harvest puts the extractor on cooldown for the other.
A miner without free capacity drops the mineral on its tile, where it shrinks every tick unless a container is under the miner.
The harvest boosts work on minerals too: UO ×3, UHO2 ×5, XUHO2 ×7 units per WORK part.
A full mineral holds 15,000 to 100,000 units; with 30 WORK that is 3000 to 20,000 ticks of mining.

entries.name: Make a tier 3 boost from base minerals
entries.title: Make a tier 3 boost from base minerals
entries.summary: Four reactions lead to a tier 3 compound based on U, K, L or Z (tier 1, OH, tier 2, tier 3); the ghodium ones need three more to make G. Run them step by step in a lab group where every producing lab is within range 2 of the two source labs.

steps.text: Pick the compound and write down its chain. XLHO2 (heal): L + O → LO, H + O → OH, LO + OH → LHO2, LHO2 + X → XLHO2. One unit takes 1 L, 2 O, 1 H and 1 X.
Bring in the base minerals your room does not have: from your other rooms by terminal, or from the market with Game.market.deal.
Lab layout: two source labs in the middle and every other lab within range 2 of both. 3 labs at room level 6 are two sources and 1 producing lab; 10 at level 8 are two sources and 8 producing labs.
A hauler loads one reagent into each source lab. A lab takes a mineral only when it is empty or already holds that mineral; it holds 3000.
Every producing lab whose cooldown is 0 calls runReaction(sourceA, sourceB): 5 units per run, then REACTION_TIME[product] ticks of cooldown.
When the batch is done, empty the producing labs completely and store the product. It is the reagent of the next step.
Repeat for each step of the chain. For a ghodium compound first make ZK and UL, then G from them.
To use it: one lab holds the compound and energy, the creep stands next to it. 30 compound and 20 energy per part.

tasks: what do I need to make XGHO2
which reactions for a catalyzed compound
how long does it take to make a tier 3 compound
pitfalls: Work in batches that are multiples of 5. A leftover below 5 cannot react and keeps the lab on its old mineral until a creep takes it out.
One producing lab makes 5 units per REACTION_TIME. The four steps to XLHO2 add up to 95 ticks per 5 units; enough for 10 parts (300 units) is 60 runs of each step.
The last step is the slow one, and it differs a lot between compounds: XZH2O 160, XGHO2 150, XGH2O 80 ticks, most others 60.
A source lab that feeds several producing labs in one tick needs 5 for each of them; reactions that find it empty are skipped although they returned OK.
A wrong product can be split again with reverseReaction, at the same cooldown and without loss.

entries.name: Run a factory
entries.title: Run a factory
entries.summary: From room level 7: load the components into the factory, call produce when its cooldown is 0, take the product out. Recipes with a level also need an operator that keeps PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY on the factory.

steps.text: STRUCTURE_FACTORY: 100,000 energy, one per room from room level 7. Next to storage and terminal one hauler serves all three.
Load the components of the recipe (COMMODITIES[type].components) for a few batches. The factory holds 50,000 in all.
When factory.cooldown is 0: produce(type). One batch per call; the cooldown is COMMODITIES[type].cooldown.
Take the product out before the factory is full.
For recipes of level 1 to 5: an operator uses PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY of that level on the factory, range 3, 100 ops, and again every 1000 ticks. The first use fixes the factory level.
Without an operator the factory still compresses minerals into bars (500 → 100) and energy into batteries (600 → 50), and makes wire, cell, alloy and condensate from deposit resources.

tasks: what do I need for higher commodities
pitfalls: Choose the level before the first PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY: it sets the factory level for good, and a power of another level does nothing afterwards.
ERR_BUSY means the effect has run out; ERR_INVALID_TARGET means the recipe level is not the factory level.
ERR_FULL when the product does not fit; keep free space in the factory.
Batteries are storage, not profit: 600 energy go in and 500 come back out.
A higher commodity needs parts from lower levels, and a factory makes only its own level: plan one room per level, or buy the parts.

entries.name: Harvest a highway deposit
entries.title: Harvest a highway deposit
entries.summary: Find a deposit in a highway room, send creeps with WORK and CARRY, harvest whenever its cooldown is 0 and carry the load home. Stop when the cooldown has grown too long for the trip.

steps.text: Look into the highway rooms in range, one room per tick; the room is visible in the next tick.
room.find(FIND_DEPOSITS): note depositType, lastCooldown and ticksToDecay of each.
Check the way. A creep lives 1500 ticks, and the walk there and back comes off its working time.
Body: WORK for the yield (1 unit per WORK per harvest), CARRY to hold it, MOVE for a trip without roads.
At range 1 whenever deposit.cooldown is 0. Creeps that harvest in the same tick all get their share.
A full creep walks home or hands over to a hauler; the resource goes to the factory or the terminal.
At home: 100 of the raw resource + 20 bars + 40 energy make 20 wire, cell, alloy or condensate.

tasks: get silicon metal biomass or mist
when to stop harvesting a deposit
pitfalls: The cooldown grows with everything ever harvested there: 64 ticks after 10,000 units, 436 after 50,000. Skip deposits whose lastCooldown is already high.
A deposit disappears 50,000 ticks after its last harvest; one harvest resets the timer.
Whatever does not fit in the creep drops on its tile and decays.
The harvest boosts multiply the yield per WORK part: UO ×3, UHO2 ×5, XUHO2 ×7.
Other players can harvest the same deposit, and their harvests lengthen your cooldown too.

entries.name: Balance resources between your rooms
entries.title: Balance resources between your rooms
entries.summary: Moving a surplus from one of your rooms to another is one terminal send: the sender pays the energy and waits 10 ticks. Compare the stocks, check the space in the target terminal, send, and confirm in the next tick.

steps.text: Per room and resource add up storage.store[r] and terminal.store[r] to see which room has a surplus and which is short.
A hauler moves the amount to send, and the energy for the cost, from storage into the terminal: a terminal sends only what it holds itself.
Cost of a route: 96 energy per 1000 units at 3 rooms, 284 at 10. Of several rooms that are short, the nearest is the cheapest to serve.
send(resource, amount, roomName) from a terminal whose cooldown is 0, with no more than the free space of the target terminal.
Next tick: the transfer is listed here if it happened.
What none of your rooms has can be bought on the market, and a surplus in all of them sold.

tasks: send minerals to the room that needs them
supply a new room by terminal
pitfalls: One send per terminal per tick, then 10 ticks of cooldown: a room cannot supply several rooms at once.
The amount is cut to the free space of the receiving terminal, so keep space free in every terminal.
Sending energy burns energy: per 1000 sent, 154 more at 5 rooms and 487 more at 20.
A send to a room without an active terminal of a player returns OK and does nothing.
A terminal that sent this tick cannot also deal: the deal is dropped.

entries.name: Mine a source keeper room
entries.title: Mine a source keeper room
entries.summary: Kill the keeper at a source, mine while its lair counts down 300 ticks, and have the guard back when the next keeper appears. Sources there hold 4000 and need no reservation.

steps.text: With vision of the room: FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES filtered by STRUCTURE_KEEPER_LAIR gives the lairs, FIND_SOURCES and FIND_MINERALS what they guard: a keeper takes the source or mineral within 5 tiles of its lair.
Guard: the keeper has 5,000 hits and deals 300 melee plus 100 ranged per tick to a creep next to it. A ranged guard at range 2 or 3 takes only the 100, which 9 HEAL parts cover.

Fight from range 3 and heal yourself in the same tick: rangedAttack and heal do not exclude each other. The keeper does not follow; it walks to its source and stays beside it. The kill takes 5,000 ÷ (10 × your RANGED_ATTACK parts) ticks.
The lair has been counting 300 ticks since your first hit. Send the guard to the next lair and bring it back before ticksToSpawn reaches 0: the new keeper appears on the lair tile.
Miner per source: 7 WORK parts drain 4000 per 300 ticks. The room has no controller, so nothing has to be reserved.
Containers (up to 5 in the room) and roads can be built; keepers do not attack structures.
Haul home. The tombstone of a killed keeper holds up to 624 energy as well.
Minerals: harvesting needs an extractor on the mineral. You cannot build one in a room without a controller; an extractor without an owner works for everybody.

tasks: how many heal parts against a source keeper
when to step back from a keeper lair
pitfalls: A living keeper shoots every player creep within 3 tiles and hits those next to it for 400 per tick. Pull miners and haulers back before ticksToSpawn runs out.
The lair timer starts with the first damage. A keeper you hurt but do not kill is replaced by a fresh one when it ends.
When the creeps around it score above 13 (10 per creep in range 1, 4 at range 2, 1 at range 3) the keeper uses rangedMassAttack and hits all of them.
Energy harvested here counts toward raids, and a raid in these rooms is always a group of 2 to 5 small invaders, each boosted with tier-3 compounds half of the time.
Strongholds deploy in these rooms. When the deploy ends, a creep standing on a tile of the layout dies: keep off the marker ramparts around a core that shows ticksToDeploy.
Keepers and invaders do not fight each other, so neither clears the room for you.

entries.name: Clear a stronghold and take its loot
entries.title: Clear a stronghold and take its loot
entries.summary: Break the rampart over the invader core and destroy the core (100,000 hits): towers and defenders stop, the ruin of the core holds commodities, and each container can be emptied once the rampart on it is down.

steps.text: FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES with structureType STRUCTURE_INVADER_CORE finds the core. core.level (1 to 5) tells the strength. While core.ticksToDeploy is set it cannot be hurt.
The effect EFFECT_COLLAPSE_TIMER on the core gives the ticks the stronghold has left. At 0 everything is removed, loot included, so plan the trip inside that time.
Size the force by level: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 towers of 600 damage each at close range, ramparts of 100,000 to 2,000,000 hits, defenders from level 2 (tables in mechanic:strongholds).
Levels 1 to 3 refill a tower only by chance once it is down to 20 energy (1%, 10%, 30% per tick), and each shot costs it 10 of 1000: towers there can be run dry. Levels 4 and 5 refill at once.
Defenders move on rampart tiles only: melee reaches 1 tile beyond the ramparts, rangers 3. Towers reach the whole room.
Every structure stands under a rampart, which takes the damage first. Ramparts, towers and containers can also be dismantled; the core only takes attack and rangedAttack.
With the core destroyed the towers and defenders no longer act. Take the commodities from the ruin of the core.
For each container: break the rampart on its tile, then withdraw.

tasks: stop invader raids in my sector
pitfalls: withdraw on a container under an Invader rampart returns OK and moves nothing.
Towers and defenders are driven by the core. Destroying a tower first costs time under fire; destroying the core stops all of them.
A fortifier (level 5 always, level 4 sometimes) repairs one rampart per tick by 3000 hits. Damage on a single rampart must stay above that.
At levels 4 and 5 all towers shoot the creep that takes the most raw damage from towers and defenders together. Your healing is not part of that sum.
Level 5 strengthens its ramparts against incoming nukes: their repair target rises by the nuke damage.
The ruin of the core stays until the time the stronghold would have collapsed. Until then no new stronghold appears in the sector and no raids come.
What is left in the containers at the collapse time is removed with them.

entries.name: Get vision of a room
entries.title: Get vision of a room
entries.summary: A room is visible in a tick when something of yours is in it, or when one of your observers looked at it the tick before. Terrain, exits and room status can be read without vision.

steps.text: Game.rooms[name] exists only in a tick in which you have vision of the room. Everything read through room.find needs it.
Without vision you still get the status (normal, closed, novice, respawn), the neighbours from Game.map.describeExits and walls and swamps from Game.map.getRoomTerrain.
Scout creep: one MOVE part (50 energy) is enough. The room is visible while the creep is in it. Step off the exit tile at once, or the creep is back in the old room one tick later.
Observer (from room level 8): one room per call, up to 10 rooms away on each axis. The room is visible in the next tick only; call every tick to keep watching.
While PWR_OPERATE_OBSERVER is active on the observer, the range limit does not apply.
In the visible tick write down what you need: sources, mineral, controller owner and reservation, hostile structures, FIND_NUKES, power banks and deposits with their ticksToDecay.
Keep positions and room names, not only ids: getObjectById returns null for an object in a room you cannot see.

tasks: see into a room I am not in
why is Game.rooms undefined for a room
check a room before claiming it
what can I know about a room without vision
pitfalls: Flags and construction sites give no vision of their room.
Every other object that carries your user id does: creeps, power creeps, structures, and also your tombstones and the ruins of your structures while they last.
A reservation gives no vision: the reserved controller is not an object of yours.
An observer keeps its target for one tick: the room it was told to watch is cleared at the start of each tick.
observeRoom returns ERR_NOT_IN_RANGE beyond 10 rooms on either axis unless PWR_OPERATE_OBSERVER is active.

entries.name: Upload code from outside the client, and manage branches
entries.title: Upload code from outside the client, and manage branches
entries.summary: One HTTP request replaces all modules of a branch: `POST /api/user/code` with your auth token and a JSON body of branch and modules. Further endpoints list, copy, switch and delete branches. The open backend takes up to 5 MB of modules and 30 branches.

steps.text: Official server: make an auth token in your account settings. Keep it in a file that is not committed.
Collect the modules as one object: name → source text. The name is what `require` takes. A binary module is `{binary: "<base64>"}` instead of text.

Send `POST /api/user/code` with the header `X-Token` and the JSON body `{"branch": "default", "modules": {"main": "…"}}`. On `screeps.com` the paths are `/api/user/code` (main world), `/ptr/api/user/code` (PTR) and `/season/api/user/code` (season).
Read the answer: `ok: 1` means the branch now holds exactly the modules you sent. The next tick starts with a fresh global scope.

For other branches: `GET /api/user/branches` lists them, `POST /api/user/clone-branch` copies or creates one, `POST /api/user/set-active-branch` picks the one that runs, `POST /api/user/delete-branch` removes one.
Or let grunt-screeps do the request: options `token` and `branch`, plus `ptr: true` or `server: "season"` for those servers, the files under `src`, then `grunt screeps`.

tasks: how big can my code be
pitfalls: Open backend: uploading to a branch that does not exist fails with "branch does not exist"; create it first with `clone-branch`.
grunt-screeps takes only the file name: `a/util.js` and `b/util.js` both become the module `util`, and the later one wins. Flatten folders into names such as `a_util` before uploading.
Keep the token out of the repository: the contributed grunt article reads credentials from a separate file listed in `.gitignore`.
notes: The docs name two ways: the grunt-screeps task, or a direct request to `/api/user/code`, where `POST` writes and `GET` reads. External upload needs an auth token.
grunt-screeps sends the `token` option as the `X-Token` header and posts to `screeps.com` under `/api/user/code`, `/ptr/api/user/code` or `/season/api/user/code`.
The body is `{branch, modules}`. grunt-screeps leaves `branch` out when the option is not set.
Lines marked "open backend" are read from the public private-server code (screeps/backend-local); the code of the official server is not public.
Open backend: without `branch` the upload goes to `$activeWorld`, the branch that runs in the world; `$activeSim` names the one active in the simulation. `GET /api/user/code` takes the same names.
Open backend: the upload replaces the whole module set of the branch, so a module you leave out is gone.
Open backend: the `modules` object as JSON may not be longer than 5 MB; the answer is then "code length exceeds 5 MB limit".
Open backend: a module `main` is added empty when it is missing. A module whose name starts with `$`, `.`, `/` or `\` is dropped.
Open backend: at most 30 branches per account, a further one answers "too many branches". Copying onto an existing name overwrites that branch.
Open backend: `clone-branch` takes `branch` (the source, at most 30 characters), `newName`, and `defaultModules` for a new branch without a source; with neither the new branch has an empty `main`.
Open backend: `set-active-branch` takes `branch` and `activeName`, which is `activeWorld` or `activeSim`. `delete-branch` takes `branch` and leaves it alone while it is active for either.
Open private server: after an upload the runner sees a newer code timestamp and discards your isolate, so the next tick has an empty global scope and loads every module again.
Official limits for token requests: `POST /api/user/code` 240 per day, `GET /api/user/code` 60 per hour, `POST /api/user/set-active-branch` 240 per day.
Code on the PTR is wiped every Monday with the rest of the PTR data.

entries.name: Operator routine in a room
entries.title: Operator routine in a room
entries.summary: What one operator does over and over in a base: make ops, keep the timed effects running, renew before 5000 ticks are up. It can use one power per tick, and every power has its own cooldown.

steps.text: Not in a room (powerCreep.room is undefined): spawn it at your power spawn once spawnCooldownTime has passed. It appears on the power spawn tile; move it off.
Once per room: step next to the controller and enable powers, unless controller.isPowerEnabled is true already.
Next to the power spawn (range 1): renew. It is free and sets the life back to 5000 ticks, so do it on every pass, and start the walk back before ticksToLive is shorter than the way.
PWR_GENERATE_OPS whenever powers[PWR_GENERATE_OPS].cooldown is 0: every 50 ticks, + 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 ops by power level. It needs no target, so it fits any tick in which no other power is due.

Keep the timed effects up. Look at target.effects for the power: when it is missing or about to end, the power is off cooldown and the ops are in the store, go within range 3 and use it. Only one power per tick, so serve the effect that ends first.
Spawns: PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN costs 100 ops, lasts 1000 ticks, cooldown 300: one creep keeps 3 spawns covered. Put it on before a large creep is started.
Labs: PWR_OPERATE_LAB costs 10 ops per lab for 1000 ticks, cooldown 50. Put it on the labs that call runReaction, not on the two reagent labs.
Sources: PWR_REGEN_SOURCE is free, lasts 300 ticks, cooldown 100: both sources of a room stay covered. Each use adds up to 1000 / 2000 / 3000 / 4000 / 5000 energy to a source that is being harvested.
Towers under attack: PWR_OPERATE_TOWER costs 10 ops per tower for 100 ticks, cooldown 10: all 6 towers fit in one cycle.
Extensions empty and a spawn waiting: PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION on the storage, 2 ops, at most every 50 ticks. It moves up to 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 % of the total extension capacity.
Too few ops for the next power: take ops from the storage or terminal one tick before it is due.
Store nearly full: put surplus ops into the storage. PWR_GENERATE_OPS drops on the ground what does not fit.

tasks: what should my operator do each tick
how often to renew a power creep
how many ops does a base need
how many spawns can one operator boost
pitfalls: One power per creep per tick: a second usePower call in the tick replaces the first one. Decide which power is due before you call.
usePower runs before withdraw inside a tick, and the call checks the store from the start of the tick: withdraw the ops one tick ahead.
PWR_GENERATE_OPS at level 5 brings 160 ops per 1000 ticks; the table shows what each effect takes. Add up what you keep running and bring in the rest.
PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN shortens only creeps whose spawning starts while the effect is on.
PWR_REGEN_SOURCE adds nothing to a full source: use it where harvesters keep the source below its capacity.
A death stops the routine for at least 8 hours of real time while the effects run out: keep the operator behind ramparts and renew early.
Refreshing an effect early does not add time: the new effect replaces the old one and lasts the normal duration from now.

entries.name: Level a power creep: what opens when
entries.title: Level a power creep: what opens when
entries.summary: Every Global Power Level is one point: the first creates the creep, each further one adds a level to one of its powers. Higher power levels, and some powers, need a minimum creep level; a creep ends at level 25.

steps.text: Earn Global Power Levels: level n needs 1000 × n^2 processed power in total, and each power takes 50 energy.
First free level: PowerCreep.create(name, POWER_CLASS.OPERATOR). The creep is level 0 with 1,000 hits and a store of 100.
Each further free level: upgrade(power) adds one level to one power, and 1,000 hits and 100 capacity to the creep. Free levels = Game.gpl.level − number of power creeps − sum of their levels.

From creep level 0 the first level of these is open: PWR_GENERATE_OPS, PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN, PWR_OPERATE_TOWER, PWR_OPERATE_STORAGE, PWR_OPERATE_LAB, PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION, PWR_OPERATE_OBSERVER, PWR_OPERATE_TERMINAL, PWR_DISRUPT_SPAWN, PWR_DISRUPT_TOWER, PWR_DISRUPT_SOURCE, PWR_SHIELD, PWR_FORTIFY, PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY.
Take PWR_GENERATE_OPS early: it is the only source of ops, and most other powers are paid in ops.
Power levels 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 of those powers need creep level 2 / 7 / 14 / 22.
Creep level 10 opens PWR_REGEN_SOURCE, PWR_REGEN_MINERAL, PWR_OPERATE_POWER; their levels 2–5 need creep level 11 / 12 / 14 / 22.
Creep level 20 opens PWR_DISRUPT_TERMINAL, PWR_OPERATE_CONTROLLER; their levels 2–5 need creep level 21 / 22 / 23 / 24.
Level 25 is the end: a full creep uses 26 GPL levels, which is 676,000 power and 33,800,000 energy.

tasks: which power can I take at which level
when can I take regen source
what creep level for operate controller
how many powers can reach level 5
how many GPL levels for a max power creep
plan the build of an operator
pitfalls: Power level 5 needs the creep at level 22 before the upgrade, and the creep stops at 25: at most 3 powers reach level 5 on one creep.
ERR_FULL from upgrade means: creep level too low for the next level of that power, the power is at 5, or the creep is at 25. Take another power meanwhile.
A level cannot be moved to another power later. The only reset is deleting the creep: 24 hours and one GPL level, unless an experimentation period is active.
The level of PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY is the factory level the creep can set and operate, and it must match exactly. Raising the power later leaves the factories it set before without an operator.
An upgrade shows in the next tick; it works on a spawned creep, so there is no need to wait for a death.
