entries.name: Decay: what disappears on its own, and how fast
entries.title: Decay: what disappears on its own, and how fast
entries.summary: Roads, containers and ramparts lose hits on a timer; dropped resources shrink every tick; tombstones and ruins vanish after a fixed time. Walls and construction sites do not decay.
tasks: how long does a road last
how fast do containers decay in unowned rooms
how fast does dropped energy decay
upkeep cost of roads and containers
how long does a tombstone last
how long does a ruin last
facts: Road: −100 hits every 1000 ticks; 5000 hits, so 50,000 ticks without traffic. Swamp roads have ×5 hits and decay, tunnels ×150. Each creep step brings the next decay closer by 1 tick per body part.
Container: −5000 hits every 100 ticks in a room without owner (reserved rooms included), every 500 ticks in an owned room; 250,000 hits, so 5000 or 25,000 ticks. Its contents drop when it goes.
Rampart: −300 hits every 100 ticks. A fresh rampart has 1 hit.
Dropped resource: −ceil(amount / 1000) every tick. Small piles lose 1 per tick; a pile of 5,000 loses 5.
Tombstone: 5 ticks per body part of the dead creep (power creeps 500), then the contents drop.
Ruin: 500 ticks (10 for the ruin of a power bank), then the contents drop.
Repair cost is 0.01 energy per hit, so upkeep per tick: road 0.001, swamp road 0.005, remote container 0.5, owned-room container 0.1, rampart 0.03.
No decay: walls, construction sites, and all owned structures other than ramparts. Power banks (5000 ticks), deposits (50,000 after the last harvest) and portals have their own timers.

entries.name: Reserving a room
entries.title: Reserving a room
entries.summary: A creep with CLAIM parts reserves a neutral controller. The reservation is a countdown of at most 5000 ticks that each reserve call pushes up.
tasks: how long does a reservation last per CLAIM part
find the cheapest way to reserve a room
what does reserving a room do
how many CLAIM parts to keep a room reserved
facts: Each reserveController call adds 1 tick per CLAIM part. The countdown loses 1 per tick, so the net gain is parts − 1 per tick while the creep works.
Maximum 5000 ticks. A call that would go above it does nothing, although it returned OK.
A CLAIM creep lives 600 ticks and cannot be renewed; a CLAIM part costs 600.

Over a cycle, a creep with N CLAIM parts that works W ticks covers N × W ticks of reservation. To hold a room for 1500 ticks with 2-CLAIM creeps working ~500 ticks each you need 1.5 creeps: 1950 energy, about 1.3 per tick.
What it buys: sources hold 3000 instead of 1500; other players cannot harvest or place sites there; invaders cannot enter the neighbouring rooms through the exits that face it.
It does not change container decay (a reserved room still counts as unowned) and gives no vision.
attackController takes 1 tick per CLAIM part off someone else's reservation; an invader core adds or removes 2 per tick.

entries.name: Controller levels, downgrade and GCL
entries.title: Controller levels, downgrade and GCL
entries.summary: Upgrading a controller raises the room level, which unlocks structures. Without upgrades the level counts down and is lost.
tasks: what does each room level unlock
how much energy for the next room level
how long until a controller downgrades
how many rooms can I own
what happens when a controller downgrades
how many towers, links, labs, extensions or spawns at each RCL
how many towers at room level 5
why does my controller not level up
does controller progress carry over to the next level
facts: Downgrade timer per level 1–8: 20,000, 10,000, 20,000, 40,000, 80,000, 120,000, 150,000, 200,000 ticks. A tick with an upgrade adds 100 ticks, up to that maximum.
After a level-up the timer starts at half of the new maximum.

On a downgrade the level drops by one, progress grows by 90% of the lower level's requirement, the stock of safe modes is set to 0 and the safe mode cooldown starts. At level 0 the room is no longer yours.
Structures above the allowance of the new level stop working (isActive() false); those nearest to the controller keep working.
At level 8 upgrading is capped at 15 energy per tick.
GCL: the number of rooms you may own. Level n needs 1,000,000 × (n − 1)^2.4 upgrade energy in total; every energy spent on any controller counts.
A level-up needs two things in the same tick: enough progress, and a downgrade timer within 100 ticks of its maximum. Until the timer is full, progress just keeps growing.
Progress above the requirement is carried into the next level.
The timer gains its 100 ticks once per tick with an upgrade, whatever the energy: 1 energy every 100 ticks holds it level.
A newly claimed controller starts with a full timer: 20,000 ticks at level 1.
Falling to level 0 clears the owner, the progress, a running safe mode and its stock, and switches powers off. The structures stay.
The level 8 cap of 15 is on the energy spent by all creeps together. Boosts add progress on top; PWR_OPERATE_CONTROLLER raises the cap by 10 to 50.
GCL counts the boosted amount, at every level.
A player who already owns 3 rooms cannot claim another one inside a novice area (ERR_FULL).

entries.name: Safe mode
entries.title: Safe mode
entries.summary: For 20,000 ticks other players' creeps can do no harm in the room.
tasks: how long does safe mode last
how do I get safe modes
when can safe mode be activated
can enemies still enter in safe mode
does my first room start in safe mode
what stops me from activating safe mode
facts: Blocked for creeps of other players in the room: attack, rangedAttack, rangedMassAttack, dismantle, heal, rangedHeal, attackController, claimController and withdraw. Towers of the owner keep firing.
Hostile creeps can still enter and move, but they no longer block your creeps: yours walk through them.
One room at a time. After activation the controller cannot activate again for 50,000 ticks.
Not possible while the controller is upgrade-blocked, or when its downgrade timer is more than 5000 ticks below half of the maximum.
Stock: +1 for every room level gained, +1 per generateSafeMode (1000 ghodium). A downgrade sets it to 0.
A nuke that lands ends a running safe mode and clears its cooldown.
Your first room starts in safe mode: placing the first spawn switches it on for 20000 ticks, without using the stock and without a cooldown.
An activation takes effect with the next tick; the stock drops by one at the same moment.
attackController blocks activation for 1000 ticks: an attacker who reaches the controller first takes safe mode away.
The owner's melee creeps take no hit-back in their room while it is in safe mode.
Other players' creeps no longer remove construction sites by walking on them.
The owner can build non-walkable structures on tiles where hostile creeps stand.
The blocked calls return ERR_NO_BODYPART; withdraw returns ERR_NOT_OWNER.
Power creeps of other players cannot use enableRoom or usePower in the room.
The cooldown also starts when the controller loses a level or the room is unclaimed. There is none in novice areas.
Of several activateSafeMode calls in one tick only the last one is kept.

entries.name: What a creep can do in one tick
entries.title: What a creep can do in one tick
entries.summary: A creep may call many methods in a tick, but some exclude each other. Of the excluded ones only the highest in the list runs; all calls still return OK and cost CPU.
tasks: which actions can a creep do in the same tick
can a creep harvest and transfer in one tick
can a creep attack and heal in the same tick
why did my creep action not happen
can a creep move and work in the same tick
facts: Work group, one per tick, highest first: heal, rangedHeal, attackController, dismantle, repair, build, attack, harvest.
Ranged group: rangedHeal, then build or repair, then rangedMassAttack, then rangedAttack. So rangedAttack runs next to attack, harvest, dismantle or heal, but not next to build, repair or rangedHeal.
Always independent: move, transfer, withdraw, pickup, drop, upgradeController, claimController, reserveController, signController, generateSafeMode, say, suicide, pull.
So a creep can, in one tick: move + harvest + transfer, or move + withdraw + upgradeController + build, or move + heal + rangedAttack.
The same method twice in a tick: the later call replaces the earlier one.
Return codes are checked against the state at the start of the tick. Energy that arrives this tick cannot be spent this tick by a creep that had none.
Inside one creep the engine runs: drop, transfer, withdraw, pickup, then the work actions, move, repair, build, the ranged actions, and the controller actions.
The 0.2 CPU is charged per object and method name: the same method twice in a tick costs it once, and an action that is dropped later still cost its own.
The dropping happens in the processor, after your script has ended: no return code shows it.
A tower runs one of heal, repair, attack per tick, preferred in that order.
A spawn takes spawnCreep, renewCreep, recycleCreep, setDirections and cancel in that order within one tick. recycleCreep works while it spawns, renewCreep does not.

groups.title: Work actions
groups.note: one per tick: the highest one called runs, the others are dropped

groups.title: Ranged actions
groups.note: one per tick; build and repair also drop the two attacks

groups.title: Independent
groups.note: always run next to anything else

entries.name: Order of events inside a tick
entries.title: Order of events inside a tick
entries.summary: All scripts run on the same snapshot. The engine then applies every intent, resolves movement, and last runs each object's own tick (damage, healing, ageing, decay). You see the result next tick.
tasks: in which order are intents processed
does a creep that dies this tick still act
facts: Your script never sees its own changes in the same tick: a store, a position or hits only change in the next tick's objects.

Stage 1, intents: for each room, user by user, the room-level intents (place site, destroy structure, flags) and each object's intents. Transfers and withdrawals change stores at once inside this stage, so a later intent can find a store already full or empty.
Stage 2, movement: all move intents of the room are resolved together after the intents.
Stage 3, object ticks, one pass over all objects of the room: a creep moves, ages, and gets the tick's damage and healing applied together; structures decay, cool down, finish spawning.
A creep that receives lethal damage this tick still carries out all its intents of this tick.
New objects (a placed site, a spawned creep, a built structure) have no usable id until the next tick.

The whole tick: all player scripts run, then all rooms are processed, then one global step moves creeps that stood on an exit into the next room and settles power creep account actions and market deals. Then Game.time goes up.
Inside a room, before any player intent, landing nukes are prepared and the NPCs (source keepers, invaders, invader cores) choose their actions, which join the intent list.
Players are handled one after another: all intents of one player in the room, then those of the next.
The room-level intents of a player run in a fixed order: remove flag, create flag, create construction site, remove construction site, destroy structure.
A creep that ends the tick on an exit tile changes room in the global step, if the room on the other side is open. Otherwise it stays where it is.

engine.label: engine: damage and healing at the end

entries.name: Movement, fatigue and what blocks a tile
entries.title: Movement, fatigue and what blocks a tile
entries.summary: Every step makes fatigue from the creep's weight and the terrain; MOVE parts remove it. A creep with fatigue cannot move.
tasks: how many MOVE parts does a creep need
can a creep walk through a rampart
can a creep walk through another creep
why is my creep stuck or not moving
do empty CARRY parts slow a creep
how many ticks per tile does my creep need
facts: Weight: every body part except MOVE counts 1; a CARRY part counts only while it holds something.
A step makes weight × 1 fatigue on a road, × 2 on plain, × 10 on swamp. Each MOVE part removes 2 per tick (boosted: ZO ×2, ZHO2 ×3, XZHO2 ×4).
Full speed needs: 1 MOVE per 2 weight on roads, 1 per 1 on plain, 5 per 1 on swamp.

Blocked tiles: walls without a road, non-walkable structures, a creep that is not moving away this tick, a closed rampart of another player, and your own construction site for a non-walkable structure.
Walkable structures: roads, containers, ramparts (your own or public ones). Portals move the creep.
Two creeps moving onto each other's tiles swap. In your own safe mode your creeps walk through hostile creeps.
Stepping onto another player's construction site destroys it (half of its progress drops as energy).
Stepping onto an exit tile moves the creep to the next room in the following tick; arriving on the exit tile clears fatigue.
A pulled creep needs no MOVE; its fatigue goes to the puller.
To move at all a creep needs fatigue 0 and at least one MOVE part with hits, or a creep that pulls it.
CARRY parts weigh one per 50 carried: a half-loaded hauler weighs half.
The tile stepped onto sets the factor, and a road on it wins: a swamp road and a tunnel cost 1 per weight.
MOVE parts take fatigue off in the tick of the step too, so ticks per tile = weight × factor ÷ (2 × MOVE parts), rounded up.
Another player's construction site never blocks a tile, whatever it is for; only your own does.
In a room under safe mode only the owner's creeps remove foreign construction sites by stepping on them.
A move toward a tile with a non-walkable structure or a closed foreign rampart is dropped at once and makes no fatigue.

entries.name: Damage, healing, ramparts and boosts in a fight
entries.title: Damage, healing, ramparts and boosts in a fight
entries.summary: All damage and healing a creep receives in a tick is added up and applied once at the end of the tick. Damage removes body parts from the front.
tasks: how is damage applied to a creep
what does a boosted HEAL part heal
how much damage does TOUGH absorb
does a rampart protect a creep
how much damage per ATTACK part
why does my creep stop working when damaged
facts: Per part and tick: ATTACK 30, RANGED_ATTACK 10 (mass attack 10 / 4 / 1 at range 1 / 2 / 3), HEAL 12 adjacent or 4 at range, dismantle 50 against structures.
Boosted HEAL: LO ×2, LHO2 ×3, XLHO2 ×4, so 24 / 36 / 48 adjacent and 8 / 12 / 16 at range, per part.
A creep has 100 hits per part. Parts lose hits from the front of the body, and a part at 0 hits does nothing. Put TOUGH first, HEAL and MOVE last.
Boosted TOUGH takes less damage while it has hits: GO ×0.7, GHO2 ×0.5, XGHO2 ×0.3. One XGHO2 part absorbs 333 damage.
The creep survives the tick if hits − damage + healing is above 0. Healing cannot exceed hitsMax.
A rampart takes all damage aimed at its tile, for creeps and structures under it, until it is destroyed.
Melee attack: the target hits back with its own ATTACK parts, unless the attacker stands on a rampart.
Tower: 600 damage or 400 healing up to range 5, a quarter of that at range 20.
The rampart redirect asks neither whose rampart it is nor whose creep: an enemy standing on your public rampart is covered by it.
Damage beyond a rampart's hits is lost in that tick; only a nuke passes the rest on to the tile.
The rampart that spares a melee attacker the hit-back can be anyone's. There is no hit-back either for a creep that attacks in its own room during safe mode.
Boosted TOUGH is worked off part by part from the front: unboosted parts in front of it take their damage in full first.
Destroyed parts still weigh, and destroyed MOVE parts remove no fatigue: a damaged creep slows down on both counts.
Destroyed CARRY parts lose their capacity at once; what no longer fits falls on the tile.
A creep still inside a spawn can be neither attacked nor healed.
Walls and ramparts under PWR_FORTIFY take no damage except from a nuke.
A structure brought to 0 hits leaves a ruin holding its contents, unless a nuke destroyed it.

entries.name: Tower numbers by range
entries.title: Tower numbers by range
entries.summary: A tower reaches the whole room. Its effect is full up to range 5 and falls in a straight line to 25% at range 20. Every action costs 10 energy.
tasks: how much does a tower heal at range 20
how much damage does a tower do at range 10
how much damage do six towers do
facts: Formula for range r between 5 and 20: base × (1 − 0.75 × (r − 5) / 15), rounded down. Range is the larger of dx and dy.
One action per tower per tick: heal beats repair, repair beats attack.
A full tower (1000 energy) has 100 shots.
PWR_OPERATE_TOWER raises and PWR_DISRUPT_TOWER lowers the effect.
A target on a rampart tile is replaced by the rampart: the shot damages the rampart, whoever owns it and whatever was aimed at.
attack takes creeps, power creeps and structures; heal only creeps and power creeps; repair only structures that have a build cost.
A creep still inside a spawn can be neither shot nor healed.
repair on a structure at full hits spends no energy, and neither does an action whose amount comes to 0.
Below 10 energy the three calls return ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_ENERGY.
attack, heal and repair are three intents: every call that returns OK costs 0.2 CPU, although one runs.
Power effects multiply the amount before it is rounded down: PWR_OPERATE_TOWER ×1.1 to ×1.5, PWR_DISRUPT_TOWER ×0.9 to ×0.5 by power level.

entries.name: What a dead creep leaves behind
entries.title: What a dead creep leaves behind
entries.summary: A creep that dies leaves a tombstone with its cargo and a share of its body energy. How large the share is depends on how it died and how much life it had left.
tasks: what happens when a creep dies
how much energy does recycling return
do boosts come back when a creep dies
facts: Share of the body: rate × remaining life ÷ full life, per part at most 125 energy. Rate is 0.2 for death and suicide, 1 for recycleCreep.
Boosted parts return 30 compound and 20 energy times the same share.
Death of old age returns almost nothing from the body, since only one tick of life is left; the cargo is still there.
If the creep stands on a container, the resources go into the container first.
The tombstone lasts 5 ticks per body part; then what is left drops on the ground.
A nuke leaves no tombstone.
"Full life" in the formula is 600 for a body with a CLAIM part and 1500 otherwise.
Every part counts with its full price, damaged or destroyed alike. Each resource is rounded down.
Parts priced above 125 never return more than that: RANGED_ATTACK, HEAL and CLAIM are capped.
A creep killed by a spawn that needed its tile dies like any killed creep and leaves a tombstone.
A creep still inside a spawn leaves nothing when the spawning is cancelled or the spawn is destroyed.

entries.name: Invader raids, invader cores and strongholds
entries.title: Invader raids, invader cores and strongholds
entries.summary: NPC creeps (user "Invader") appear in rooms where energy is harvested. Raids start from the amount harvested; cores and strongholds are structures that spread through a sector.
tasks: how to stop invaders from spawning
how much damage does an invader do
how much does an invader healer heal
why did the invaders kill themselves
how many invaders in a raid
facts: Every room counts the energy harvested from its sources. A raid is due when the count passes the room's goal: 100,000 at first, then re-rolled after each raid to 70–130% of that (one time in twenty, twice as much).
A raid needs an active stronghold (invader core of level 1 or more) somewhere in the same sector. No stronghold, no raids.
Invaders enter through an exit whose neighbouring room is neither owned nor reserved. If every neighbour is owned or reserved, no raid comes.
No new raid while an invader is still alive in the room. The counter restarts after a raid.

Size: small bodies (10 parts) in unowned rooms and below room level 4; big bodies (50 parts) from level 4. Nine times in ten it is a single creep; otherwise a group of 2 to 5 (big bodies: at most 2 at levels 4–5, 3 at levels 6–7).
A single raider is boosted half of the time. The first creep is a melee type, the others ranged or healers.
Invaders live 1500 ticks and do not leave the room. They hunt creeps and only break structures that are in the way.
A level 0 invader core in a neutral or reserved room reserves the controller as "Invader" at 2 ticks per tick; while that holds you cannot harvest there. It has 100,000 hits and does not fight back.
Strongholds (core level 1–5) have towers and ramparts, defender creeps from level 2, hold loot, and collapse after about 75,000 ticks (±10%).
The room where a player or a bot places its first spawn gets a goal of 1,000,000 instead, so the first raid there comes ten times later.
On a private server the raid job leaves out every room that is in the set of rooms waiting to be processed at the moment it runs, so a raid that is due can come several runs late.
On a private server the raid check runs every five minutes of real time, so the delay after reaching the goal varies with tick speed.
Invader bodies have 100 hits per part: 1,000 for the small ones, 5,000 for the big ones.
In a group each creep rolls for a boost on its own: 50% for small bodies; 0% for big bodies, except 40% in the larger groups at room level 7 and 8.

A boost covers every HEAL, RANGED_ATTACK, WORK, ATTACK and TOUGH part of the creep: LO, KO, ZH, UH, GO. In the centre block of a sector (both room numbers ending in 4, 5 or 6) the tier-3 compounds are used instead.
Four groups out of five are pairs; only the fifth draws its size from the full range. A group is never larger than the number of exit tiles on its side.
In the centre block every raid is a group of 2 to 5 small invaders and its first creep is ranged.
Elsewhere the second creep of a group is ranged or a healer at even odds and the rest are healers; only in a group of 5 the third may be ranged too.
All creeps of a raid come in on the same side of the room, on exit tiles next to each other.
The count includes what other players harvest from the sources of the room. Minerals do not count.
One time in twenty the new goal comes out as 0, which the server reads as 100,000 again.
The room of your first spawn starts with a goal of 1,000,000.
Targets are the creeps and power creeps of players. Invaders ignore Source Keepers, and keepers ignore them.
A melee invader walks to the nearest player creep it can reach and attacks it at range 1. Every invader with RANGED_ATTACK parts also shoots the creep with the fewest hits within range 3, each tick.
A ranged invader keeps its distance: it steps away when a player creep is within 2 tiles and comes closer only while its target is more than 3 away.
Below half of its hits a ranged invader walks to the nearest healer of its group.

A healer heals the most damaged invader within 3 tiles, itself included (heal at range 1, rangedHeal beyond), and walks to the nearest damaged one. With nobody damaged it backs off from player creeps within 3 tiles, or else follows a non-healer.
If no open path leads to a player creep, the invader plans one through walls and ramparts, then through any destructible structure.

An invader with ATTACK or WORK parts checks the first tile of its path: a structure there (any buildable type except a spawn, roads and containers included) is dismantled if the invader has WORK, attacked otherwise, and shot with RANGED_ATTACK parts.
With no player creep to go for, an invader in an owned room kills itself, unless a spawn is walled in: then it digs toward that spawn. In a room without owner it waits.
A healer with nobody to heal and no non-healer left to follow kills itself.
A dead invader leaves a tombstone with energy for its body and, if boosted, some of the compound: per boosted part 30 × 0.2 × the share of life it had left.

entries.name: Sources: capacity and regeneration
entries.title: Sources: capacity and regeneration
entries.summary: A source refills to its capacity every 300 ticks. The capacity depends on the room.
tasks: how much energy does a source give per tick
source capacity in a reserved room
how many WORK parts per source
energy income of a remote room
facts: Capacity: 3000 in owned and reserved rooms, 1500 in neutral rooms, 4000 in rooms without a controller (source keeper and centre rooms).
That is 10, 5 and 13.3 energy per tick, needing 5, 3 and 7 WORK parts.
The 300-tick timer starts when the source first drops below full and refills it completely when it ends. Energy not harvested by then is lost.
The capacity switches in the tick the room becomes reserved or loses the reservation.
More WORK than needed only helps to cover walking time and gaps between miners.

entries.name: CPU: limit, bucket and the cost of intents
entries.title: CPU: limit, bucket and the cost of intents
entries.summary: Each tick you may use your limit; unused CPU is saved in a bucket of up to 10,000 that lets a tick use up to 500. Every state-changing call that returns OK costs a fixed 0.2 CPU on top of its run time.
tasks: how does the cpu bucket work
what happens when I run out of cpu
facts: The 0.2 CPU fee applies to methods the reference marks as actions (kind "intent" here) and only when they return OK. A call that returns an error costs only its own run time.
So check cheap conditions yourself before calling: range, fatigue, full store, hits < hitsMax, reservation below the cap.
No fee: say, pull, cancelOrder, all find/look/range methods, PathFinder (it costs its own run time, which can be far more).
moveTo is not an action itself, but it issues a move (0.2) and may run a path search.
Typical floor: one intent per creep per tick. A creep that moves and works costs 0.4.
Script over tickLimit: it is stopped in the middle of the tick. Bucket at 0: only the limit is available.
Memory is parsed on first access each tick; the larger it is, the more CPU that access takes.
Game.cpu.getUsed() around a block measures it; in the simulation room it returns 0.
tickLimit = limit + bucket, at most 500. The cap is cpuMaxPerTick in the driver.
After the tick: bucket = bucket + limit − CPU used, at most 10,000 (cpuBucketSize in the driver).
CPU used = run time + 0.2 per intent, rounded up to a whole number. So every tick costs at least 1 CPU.
The intent fee lives in the runtime: 0.2 is added to the running total when an intent is queued, and the bucket is charged 0.2 for each intent in the final list.
The clock starts when your loop is called and stops after Memory has been turned back into a string. Building the Game object before the loop is not charged; the Memory save after it is.
What is measured is the CPU time of your isolate.
A bucket below 0 after an overrun means the script is not run: "Script execution has been terminated: CPU bucket is empty". Each skipped tick adds the limit back.

entries.name: Memory, segments and the global scope
entries.title: Memory, segments and the global scope
entries.summary: Three places to keep data: Memory (2 MB of JSON, parsed every tick), segments (100 × 100 KB strings, loaded on request), and the global scope (free, but lost on every reset).
tasks: how many memory segments can be active
how to share data with another player
facts: Memory: at most 2 MB as JSON. Parsed on first access in a tick and written back at the end; both cost CPU in proportion to its size.
Segments: ids 0–99, 100 KB each. At most 10 active at a time. Ask with setActiveSegments; they are in RawMemory.segments from the next tick. Write by assigning a string.
Reading another player: they call setPublicSegments, you call setActiveForeignSegment and read RawMemory.foreignSegment next tick. One foreign segment at a time.

Global scope (variables outside the loop, properties on global): kept between ticks at no cost, but wiped whenever the server restarts your isolate or you upload code. Treat it as a cache and rebuild it when empty.
Game objects are new every tick. Keep ids and look them up with Game.getObjectById.
InterShardMemory: one 100 KB string per shard, readable from your code on the other shards.
Memory limit: 2 × 1024 × 1024 characters of JSON, checked when the tick is saved. Above it the save is refused and the stored Memory stays unchanged.
Memory is parsed by the first read of the global Memory in a tick, and written back after the loop only if it was parsed.
Segment limits: ids 0 to 99, 100 × 1024 characters each, at most 10 requested and at most 10 saved per tick.
The list given to setActiveSegments is stored with the account: those segments are loaded every tick from the next one on, until the list changes.
Breaking a segment rule (too long, not a string, more than 10 keys) fails the whole tick: its intents, Memory changes and segments are all lost.

Foreign segment: you request a user name and an id (or that user's default). One tick later RawMemory.foreignSegment holds {username, id, data}, but only if the owner lists that id as public at that moment.
A public segment with id 0 cannot be read by others: the loader skips id 0.
Inter-shard memory: a shard can write only its own string; the other shards read it.

entries.name: Nukes
entries.title: Nukes
entries.summary: A nuke lands 50,000 ticks after launch on a position up to 10 rooms away.
tasks: how to see an incoming nuke
how much damage does a nuke do
can I nuke a room without vision
facts: Damage to structures: 10,000,000 on the target tile, 5,000,000 within range 2. A rampart takes the hit first; what is under it gets only the damage above the rampart's hits.
Every creep in the room dies, without a tombstone. Construction sites, dropped resources, tombstones and ruins are removed.
Safe mode ends and the controller cannot be upgraded for 200 ticks.
Incoming nukes are in room.find(FIND_NUKES) with timeToLand. Ramparts above 5,000,000 hits (or 10,000,000 on the centre) save what is under them.
Launching costs 300,000 energy and 5000 ghodium, then 100,000 ticks of cooldown.
The nuke strikes in the tick in which timeToLand reads 1; one tick later the Nuke object is gone.
A structure destroyed by a nuke leaves no ruin, so what it held is lost.
Power creeps in the room die as well. Spawns lose the creep they are making, and spawn orders given in the landing tick are dropped.
When a nuke ends a safe mode, the safe mode cooldown is cleared as well; still, a new safe mode does not start while the controller is blocked from upgrading.
PWR_FORTIFY does not protect walls and ramparts from a nuke.
The range is counted on each axis: the target room lies in the square of 21 × 21 rooms around the nuker.
The target is any RoomPosition; the call does not ask for vision of that room.
A new nuker starts with the full cooldown of 100,000 ticks.
A launched nuke cannot be stopped. Several nukes may be aimed at one tile.
No nuke can be launched from or into a novice or respawn area.

entries.name: Room types in a sector
entries.title: Room types in a sector
entries.summary: The world is made of 10×10 room sectors. Rooms whose number ends in 0 are highways; the 3×3 block in the middle of a sector holds source keeper rooms around a centre room.
tasks: what is a source keeper room
where are power banks and deposits
what can I build in a room without a controller
facts: Highway rooms (x or y ending in 0): no controller, no sources. Power banks and deposits appear there.
Source keeper rooms (x and y ending in 4–6, except 5/5): no controller, sources of 4000, a mineral, keeper lairs that respawn a keeper.
Centre room (x and y ending in 5): no controller and no keepers; portals appear there.
All other rooms have a controller and can be reserved or claimed.
Rooms without a controller cannot be reserved; roads and containers can still be built there.
The server tells a highway by the room number alone: x or y ending in 0.
Sources hold 4000 in every room that has no controller.
The allowance in a room without a controller is that of room level 0: 5 containers, roads, and no other structure.
Strongholds deploy in the eight rooms around the centre room. Raids in the whole centre block always come as groups, boosted with tier-3 compounds.
The highway crossings between sectors (W0N0, W10N0, W10N10 and so on) hold NPC terminals that trade on the market.
The reference places the portals that appear at random in the centre room of a sector.

entries.name: Minerals and extractors
entries.title: Minerals and extractors
entries.summary: A room holds one mineral of one type. With an extractor on it each WORK part takes 1 unit per harvest, and a harvest is possible once every 6 ticks. An emptied mineral is full again after 50,000 ticks.
tasks: how fast can I mine a mineral
how many WORK parts for mineral mining
how much mineral is in a room
why can I not harvest the mineral
how often can I harvest a mineral
pitfalls: A mineral left with a few units never refills: harvest it down to 0.
Call harvest only when extractor.cooldown is 0; in between the call returns ERR_TIRED.
An extractor in a room whose level dropped below the required one is inactive, and the mineral cannot be harvested until the level is back.
facts: There are seven base minerals: H, O, U, L, K, Z, X. A room has one mineral, of one type.
Harvesting needs an extractor on the mineral tile. It is allowed from room level 6, costs 5000 energy and can be placed only on a mineral.
A harvest takes 1 unit per working WORK part, at most what is left. The harvest boosts multiply it: UO ×3, UHO2 ×5, XUHO2 ×7.
A harvest puts a cooldown of 5 on the extractor. It counts down by 1 per tick, so the mineral can be harvested once every 6 ticks: 0.167 unit per WORK part per tick.
The cooldown is written at the end of the tick, so every creep that harvests in that same tick gets its share. Several miners must harvest in the same tick.
What does not fit in the creep falls on its tile, into a container if it stands on one.
A full mineral holds 15,000, 35,000, 70,000 or 100,000 units, by its density (low, moderate, high, ultra).
The refill timer of 50,000 ticks starts when the amount reaches 0, not earlier.

At the refill the mineral gets the amount of the density it has. After that the density is drawn again for the next refill: always when it was low or ultra, otherwise with a 5% chance. A new draw never keeps the old density.
A draw gives low 10%, moderate 40%, high 40%, ultra 10%.

harvest returns ERR_NOT_FOUND without an extractor, ERR_NOT_OWNER when the extractor belongs to another player, ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH when it is inactive, ERR_TIRED during the cooldown and ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES when the mineral is empty.
The mineral itself blocks movement; the miner stands next to it.
PWR_REGEN_MINERAL adds 2 to 10 units (power level 1 to 5) every 10 ticks to a mineral that is not empty.
The room generator of the private server picks the mineral type from a weighted list: H and O 6 of 25 each, Z, K, U and L 3 of 25 each, X 1 of 25.

entries.name: Labs and reactions
entries.title: Labs and reactions
entries.summary: A lab holds 2000 energy and 3000 of one mineral or compound. A reaction takes 5 units from each of two labs within range 2 and makes 5 units of the product; the producing lab then waits REACTION_TIME[product] ticks.
tasks: reaction chain from base minerals to tier 3
how is the mineral type of a lab set
empty a lab to change its mineral
how much compound does a lab make per tick
pitfalls: Checks use the amounts at the start of the tick and run again when the tick is processed. A source lab that feeds several producing labs must hold 5 for each of them, or the later reactions are skipped although they returned OK.
To switch a lab to another compound, empty it completely first: one leftover unit keeps the old type.
LAB_COOLDOWN is not used anywhere; the cooldown is REACTION_TIME.
facts: First steps: H + O → OH; Z + K → ZK; U + L → UL; ZK + UL → G. G is not mined, it is made this way.
Tier 1: U, K, L, Z or G with H or O, for example U + H → UH. Tier 2: tier 1 + OH, for example UH + OH → UH2O. Tier 3: tier 2 + X, for example UH2O + X → XUH2O.
Each run takes 5 from each source lab and adds 5 to the producing lab: one unit of product uses one unit of each reagent.
So one unit of a tier 3 compound from U, K, L or Z uses 1 of that mineral, 1 X and 3 of H and O together; one from G uses 1 each of Z, K, U, L and X and 3 of H and O.
Both source labs must be within range 2 of the producing lab. The two sources need not be near each other.
After a run the producing lab waits REACTION_TIME of the product, between 5 and 160 ticks. Source labs get no cooldown and can feed several labs.
Output of one producing lab: 5 units per REACTION_TIME ticks. OH at 20 ticks is 250 per 1000 ticks; XGHO2 at 150 is 33.
How a lab gets its mineral type: the first resource other than energy that enters an empty lab, by transfer or as a reaction product, takes the mineral slot.
How it is cleared: when the amount reaches 0, by withdraw, by a reaction that uses it up or by boosting. Then the lab accepts any resource again.
A lab that holds one mineral refuses every other one: transfer returns ERR_INVALID_TARGET.
The producing lab must be empty or already hold the product (ERR_INVALID_ARGS otherwise) and have room for one more run (ERR_FULL).
reverseReaction splits 5 units of the compound in the lab into 5 of each reagent, put into two labs within range 2. Nothing is lost, and the cooldown is the same as for making the compound.
In one tick a lab can boost, unboost and run one reaction; runReaction wins over reverseReaction.
PWR_OPERATE_LAB adds 2 to 10 units per run (power level 1 to 5) on the lab it is used on, for 1000 ticks. Inputs and output grow alike; the cooldown stays.
Labs allowed: 3 at room level 6, 6 at 7, 10 at 8, for 50,000 energy each. A lab above the allowance of the current level returns ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH.

entries.name: Boosts: how they are applied and what they change
entries.title: Boosts: how they are applied and what they change
entries.summary: A lab puts its compound on the matching body parts of an adjacent creep for 30 compound and 20 energy per part. A boosted part multiplies the actions its compound is listed for, until the creep dies, is renewed or is unboosted.
tasks: which body parts does a compound boost
how much does it cost to boost a whole creep
how long does a boost last
get compound back from a boosted creep
pitfalls: If the lab runs short it boosts only the parts it can pay for, and boostCreep has already returned OK. Check creep.body before sending the creep out.
Unboosting a creep with many tier 3 parts blocks that lab for thousands of ticks. Use a lab that runs no reactions.
Renew a boosted creep and the boosts are gone; cargo above the smaller capacity drops on the ground.
facts: boostCreep takes 30 compound and 20 energy from the lab for every part it boosts. The lab must be yours; the creep must be adjacent and done spawning.
Which parts: those without a boost whose type is listed for the compound in BOOSTS. One compound per part; a boosted part is skipped.
Order: TOUGH parts are taken from the front of the body, all other types from the back. bodyPartsCount limits how many are boosted.
A full lab (3000 compound, 2000 energy) boosts 100 parts. Ten parts cost 300 compound and 200 energy.

Where the power is computed: each action adds up the working parts of its type, and a part multiplies its base value by BOOSTS[type][compound][action] when that action is listed for the compound. Every other action of the part stays at ×1.
So a WORK part with UO harvests ×3 but builds, repairs, dismantles and upgrades at the normal rate.
The harvest boost works on sources, minerals and deposits alike.
build, repair and upgradeController: the boost adds output; the energy spent is the same as without a boost.
CARRY: a boosted part holds 50 × 2, 3 or 4, and it still counts as one part of weight when loaded.
MOVE: a boosted part removes 2 fatigue × 2, 3 or 4 per tick.
TOUGH: damage that lands on a boosted TOUGH part with hits left is multiplied by 0.7, 0.5 or 0.3.
A part at 0 hits adds nothing, boosted or not.
A boost has no timer. renewCreep removes every boost of the creep and gives nothing back.
unboostCreep (own creep, adjacent, lab off cooldown) removes all boosts at once and drops 15 compound per part on the creep's tile, 50% of what went in, and 0 energy.
The unboosting lab then cools down: per part, the reaction times of the whole chain of the compound × 3. One XLHO2 part: 285 ticks; one XGHO2 part: 675.
Death: each boosted part leaves 30 compound and 20 energy × rate × remaining life ÷ full life in the tombstone. The rate is 0.2, or 1 for recycleCreep.

entries.name: Factory, commodities and factory levels
entries.title: Factory, commodities and factory levels
entries.summary: A factory turns resources from its own store into commodities, one batch per call, with a cooldown per recipe. Recipes without a level run in any factory; recipes of level 1 to 5 need a factory of exactly that level with an active PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY effect.
tasks: which commodities need no factory level
can a factory level be changed
pitfalls: Decide the level before the first usePower: an operator whose PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY has another level can never operate that factory.
The product must fit: ERR_FULL when the store minus the components plus the product would exceed the capacity.
A factory in a room that is no longer yours, or below the needed level, has capacity 0 and produces nothing.
facts: One factory per room from room level 7, for 100,000 energy. It holds 50,000 units of any mix.
produce(type) takes the components of COMMODITIES[type] out of the factory store, adds COMMODITIES[type].amount units of the product and sets a cooldown of COMMODITIES[type].cooldown ticks.
Compression, in any factory: 500 of a mineral + 200 energy → 100 bar, cooldown 20. Back: 100 bar + 200 energy → 500 mineral.
The bars: utrium_bar, lemergium_bar, zynthium_bar, keanium_bar, ghodium_melt (G), oxidant (O), reductant (H), purifier (X).
Battery: 600 energy → 50 battery; 50 battery → 500 energy, cooldown 10 each way. A round trip loses 100 energy per batch.
Four chains start from the deposit resources, in any factory: 100 silicon + 20 utrium_bar → 20 wire; biomass + lemergium_bar → cell; metal + zynthium_bar → alloy; mist + keanium_bar → condensate.

Each chain then rises one factory level per step: wire → switch → transistor → microchip → circuit → device; cell → phlegm → tissue → muscle → organoid → organism; alloy → tube → fixtures → frame → hydraulics → machine; condensate → concentrate → extract → spirit → emanation → essence.
Shared components made from bars: composite (level 1), crystal (level 2), liquid (level 3).
A new factory has no level. The first PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY used on it sets its level to the level of the power, for good. Later uses must have the same level and only renew the effect.
The effect lasts 1000 ticks and costs 100 ops, at range 3; the power itself has a cooldown of 800 ticks.
A recipe with a level needs a factory of exactly that level (ERR_INVALID_TARGET otherwise) and the effect active (ERR_BUSY otherwise).
Without the effect a levelled factory still runs every recipe that has no level.
The power changes nothing else: batch size and cooldown stay those of COMMODITIES.
A factory makes only its own level and the recipes without level, so a chain up to level 5 needs factories of several levels, each in its own room.
The level cannot be changed afterwards; only a rebuilt factory can get another one.

entries.name: Deposits in highway rooms
entries.title: Deposits in highway rooms
entries.summary: Deposits appear in highway rooms and give silicon, metal, biomass or mist: 1 unit per WORK part per harvest. Every harvest makes the next cooldown longer, and a deposit nobody harvests for 50,000 ticks disappears.
tasks: when does a new deposit spawn
how much can I get from a deposit
pitfalls: Once the cooldown is long a creep mostly waits: with W WORK parts it gets W units once per cooldown. Decide by lastCooldown and the travel time whether the trip still pays.
The wear is shared: a deposit other players have used starts slow for you too.
What does not fit in the creep drops on its tile and decays; bring enough CARRY.
facts: Four types: silicon, metal, biomass, mist.
One type per quadrant of the world map; deposits lie in the highway rooms between the sectors.
Any creep with WORK harvests it at range 1. No extractor, no ownership and no reservation is checked.
A harvest gives 1 unit per working WORK part, times the harvest boost. A deposit has no amount that runs out.
After a harvest the cooldown is ceil(0.001 × total harvested ^ 1.2) ticks. The total counts everything ever taken from this deposit, by anyone.
There is no cooldown while that value is 1 or less: about the first 316 units.
Later it grows fast: 64 ticks after 10,000 units, 436 after 50,000, 1000 after 100,000.
All creeps that harvest in the same tick succeed; the cooldown is set at the end of the tick from the new total.
Every harvest sets the decay timer back to 50,000 ticks, and a new deposit starts with that timer. When it runs out the deposit is removed.
Deposit.lastCooldown is the current value of the formula; the total itself is not shown.
The server job that places deposits runs every five minutes of real time. Per sector it puts one into a highway room of that sector that has no deposit yet.

A sector gets a new one only while its deposits are worn: each counts 20 ÷ max(1, its cooldown value) and the sum must be below 2.5. A fresh deposit counts 20 and blocks new ones; a single deposit must be past a cooldown of 8, about 1789 units harvested.
It is placed on a wall tile with at least one open neighbour, between 5 and 44 on both axes, with no other object within 2 tiles.
A deposit blocks movement; creeps harvest from a neighbouring tile.

entries.name: Market: orders, deals, fees and credits
entries.title: Market: orders, deals, fees and credits
entries.summary: Players trade through buy and sell orders tied to a terminal. Creating an order costs 5% of its value in credits. A deal against an order moves the resource between the two terminals at the end of the tick, and the side that makes the deal pays the energy.
tasks: how long does a market order last
how many market orders can I have
do I get the fee back when I cancel an order
pitfalls: OK from createOrder, deal, extendOrder or changeOrderPrice only means the request was queued. Whether it took effect shows next tick in Game.market.orders, credits and the transaction lists.
A filled order stays in Game.market.orders as inactive and still counts toward the limit: cancel it.
When you buy energy, the transfer fee must already be in your terminal; the energy that arrives cannot pay for it.
If the owner changes the price of an order in the tick you deal on it, your deal is either dropped or runs at the new price, depending on which player is processed first.
Each market call that returns OK costs 0.2 CPU like any other intent.
facts: Two order types. ORDER_SELL offers a resource out of your terminal; ORDER_BUY asks for a resource to be delivered to it. An order names a room where you own a terminal.
Fee: 5% of price × amount in credits, rounded up to 0.001, taken when the order is created. extendOrder charges it on the added amount, changeOrderPrice on the increase × remaining amount.
cancelOrder returns no fee. An order that expires gets the fee of its unfilled part back.
Life time: 30 days of real time from creation. Extending the order or changing its price does not restart it.
At most 300 orders per player; inactive and filled ones count.

A sell order is active while its terminal holds the resource. A buy order is active while you have credits for at least one unit and its terminal has free space. This is checked again every tick, and a new order starts inactive.
order.amount is what can trade right now (limited by stock, credits and space), remainingAmount what is left of the order, totalAmount what was ordered.
Only active orders are visible in getAllOrders and can be dealt with.
deal(orderId, amount, yourRoomName) trades against an order through your terminal in that room; at most 10 deals per tick.
Deals and terminal sends run once per tick, after all rooms have been processed. The result is visible in the next tick.
The traded amount is the smallest of: the amount asked, what is left in the order, the stock of the selling terminal, the free space of the buying terminal, and what the buyer can pay.
The price is the order's price per unit. The buyer pays amount × price and the seller receives exactly that; a deal has no credit fee.
Energy: the terminal of the player who makes the deal pays the transfer cost for the distance between the two rooms, whether buying or selling. The order owner pays no energy.
Only the dealing terminal gets the cooldown of 10 ticks, so each terminal makes at most one deal per tick.
When several players deal on the same order in one tick, the terminal nearest to the order is served first.
Credits belong to the account. Balance and prices have a resolution of 0.001 credit.
First credits: sell to an existing buy order with deal. That needs no credits; only buying from a sell order is checked against your balance.
Account resources (INTERSHARD_RESOURCES: token, cpuUnlock, pixel, accessKey) trade without terminals: no room, no energy, no cooldown; the items move between the two accounts.
NPC terminals stand in the highway crossroads rooms. Their orders have no owner: they are limited only by their remaining amount, never by stock, space or credits.
On the private server a job renews the orders of each NPC terminal about every 5,000 ticks: one sell order for a base mineral, sometimes one for energy and one buy order for a base mineral.
getHistory gives, per resource and day, the transactions, volume, avgPrice and stddevPrice of the sales by players in the last 14 days. It is rebuilt hourly and cached for three hours in the runtime.
Every send and deal that was carried out is logged; the last 100 in each direction are in incomingTransactions and outgoingTransactions.

entries.name: Terminal transfers: energy cost, cooldown, limits
entries.title: Terminal transfers: energy cost, cooldown, limits
entries.summary: A terminal sends any resource to a player's terminal in any other room. The sender pays ceil(amount × (1 − e^(−distance / 30))) energy on top and then waits 10 ticks; the resource arrives at the end of the same tick.
tasks: how far can a terminal send
who pays for a terminal transfer
how long is the terminal cooldown
is there a minimum amount for terminal send
pitfalls: send returns OK for a room without a terminal, for a full terminal and for a terminal in a room that is no longer active. Check Game.market.outgoingTransactions in the next tick.
Under PWR_OPERATE_TERMINAL send() and deal() still compare the terminal's energy with the full cost, so keep the undiscounted fee in the terminal.
A send and a deal from the same terminal in one tick: the send runs first and the deal is dropped.
If creeps take the resource or the fee energy out of the terminal in the tick of the send, the send is dropped.
facts: Energy cost: ceil(amount × (1 − e^(−distance / 30))). It depends only on amount and distance, not on the resource.
Distance is counted in rooms: the larger of the two axis differences, wrapping around the edge of the world.
Per 1000 units that is 33 energy at 1 room, 154 at 5, 284 at 10, 487 at 20, 633 at 30 and 865 at 60. There is no distance limit; far away the cost comes close to the amount itself.
The sender pays. To send energy the terminal needs the amount plus the cost.
The sending terminal then cools down 10 ticks, if the send went through. The receiver gets no cooldown and can take any number of transfers.
Sends run once per tick after all rooms have been processed; both stores show the result in the next tick.
The target room must hold a terminal that belongs to a player. If not, nothing happens and nothing is charged.
The amount is cut to the free space of the target terminal and the cost is counted on what is really sent. A full target receives nothing.
A terminal holds 300,000 in all. Its capacity is 0 while the room is not the owner's at a level that allows a terminal, so such a terminal receives nothing.
send() only checks your side at the start of the tick: resource and fee in the terminal, no cooldown, a well-formed room name. It cannot see the target.
There is no minimum amount. TERMINAL_MIN_SEND and TERMINAL_SEND_COST are not read by the engine.

PWR_OPERATE_TERMINAL multiplies the energy cost (rounded up) and the cooldown (rounded) of that terminal by 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6 or 0.5 (power level 1 to 5) for 1000 ticks. At level 5 the cooldown is 5 ticks. It applies to sends from the terminal and to deals made through it.

PWR_DISRUPT_TERMINAL lasts 10 ticks and reaches the whole room (range 50). While it lasts creeps cannot withdraw from the terminal (ERR_INVALID_TARGET) and PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION cannot take energy from it.
The engine code for send and deal looks only at PWR_OPERATE_TERMINAL; it has no check for the disrupt effect.

entries.name: Source keepers and keeper lairs
entries.title: Source keepers and keeper lairs
entries.summary: A keeper lair keeps one Source Keeper beside a source or mineral. The keeper has 5,000 hits and deals 400 damage per tick to a creep next to it. Its lair replaces it 300 ticks after it was first hurt.
tasks: how strong is a source keeper
how much damage does a source keeper do
how does a source keeper behave
how much energy is in a source keeper room source
pitfalls: Hurting a keeper without killing it gains nothing: the lair replaces it with a fresh one when the timer ends.
The quiet time after a kill is 300 ticks minus the length of the fight. Kill fast.
Keepers attack creeps only. Containers and roads next to a source are safe from them.
facts: Body: 17 TOUGH, 13 MOVE, 10 ATTACK, 10 RANGED_ATTACK, in that order with ATTACK and RANGED_ATTACK alternating; 5,000 hits.
To a creep in range 1 it does attack (300) and a ranged action (100) in the same tick. At range 2 or 3 only the ranged damage arrives.
Targets are creeps and power creeps of players, always the one with the fewest hits in reach. Invaders and other keepers are never targets.

With several creeps near it uses rangedMassAttack instead of rangedAttack: it scores 10 per creep in range 1, 4 at range 2, 1 at range 3 and switches above 13. That hits every creep for 100 / 40 / 10 at range 1 / 2 / 3.
It takes the source or mineral within 5 tiles of where it appears, walks next to it and stays. It does not chase and it never leaves the room.
The lair starts a timer of 300 ticks as soon as its keeper is missing or below full hits, so the count begins with the first damage, not with the death.
When the timer ends a keeper that is still alive is removed, and a new one with full hits appears on the lair tile.
lair.ticksToSpawn is the rest of that timer and undefined while none runs.
A keeper ages like any creep: after 1500 ticks it dies and the lair counts 300 ticks again.
A killed keeper leaves a tombstone with energy for its body: up to 624, less the older it was.
Sources in a room without a controller hold 4000: 13.3 energy per tick, 7 WORK parts to drain one.
Lairs belong to the map: a room has keepers where the map has lairs. The lair cannot be destroyed.
lair.owner.username is "Source Keeper" and lair.my is false. Keepers are creeps of that user, so FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS returns them and FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES returns the lairs.
A mineral there needs an extractor on it like any mineral. One without an owner works for everybody; you cannot build one where there is no controller.
Energy harvested there counts toward invader raids. In the centre block of a sector (both room numbers ending in 4, 5 or 6) a raid is always a group of 2 to 5 small invaders.

entries.name: Strongholds: levels, defences, loot and lesser cores
entries.title: Strongholds: levels, defences, loot and lesser cores
entries.summary: A stronghold is an invader core of level 1 to 5 with towers, ramparts, loot containers and, from level 2, defenders. It deploys for 5,000 ticks, lives about 75,000 ticks, and sends level 0 cores into nearby rooms to take their controllers.
tasks: how many towers does a stronghold have
what does an invader core do to a controller
how long does a stronghold take to deploy
what is in a stronghold container
when does a new stronghold appear
pitfalls: withdraw from a stronghold container returns OK but moves nothing while the Invader rampart on its tile stands. Break the rampart first.
During the deploy stage attack, rangedAttack and dismantle on the core return ERR_INVALID_TARGET.
Loot that is still in the containers at the collapse time is gone: the containers are removed, not destroyed.
facts: A sector gets a new stronghold when it holds no invader core of any level and no ruin of one.
The room is drawn from the eight rooms around the centre room of the sector, leaving out rooms whose controller is owned or reserved.
The layout (bunker1 to bunker5; its number is the level) and its place are drawn from those that fit between the walls of the room.
Deploy stage, 5,000 ticks: the core shows ticksToDeploy, is invulnerable and does nothing; public ramparts with 1 hit mark the tiles of the layout.
When the deploy ends the real structures are put down. A creep or power creep standing on a layout tile dies; structures there are destroyed and construction sites removed.
From then the stronghold lives 75,000 ticks ±10%. Each of its structures carries EFFECT_COLLAPSE_TIMER with the ticks that remain.
Towers and ramparts belong to user "Invader"; containers and roads have no owner. Towers start with 1000 energy and shoot like player towers, 10 energy a shot.
Every tile of the layout has a rampart, the core tile included. Ramparts start with STRONGHOLD_RAMPART_HITS of the level and do not decay before the collapse.
The core has 100,000 hits at every level. attack and rangedAttack work on it; dismantle does not, since it has no build cost.

The core refills a tower that is down to 20 energy or less and still under a rampart, one tower per tick, with a chance per tick of 1% at level 1, 10% at level 2, 30% at level 3 and always at levels 4 and 5.
Levels 1 to 3: all towers shoot the player creep nearest to the core. Levels 4 and 5: towers and defenders pick the creep on which their combined damage is highest.
The core spawns its defenders itself and replaces dead ones: none at level 1, one at level 2, two at level 3, four at level 4, nine at level 5. A body part takes 6 / 3 / 2 / 1 ticks at levels 2 to 5.
While player creeps are in the room, defenders walk on rampart tiles only. Melee defenders go for creeps next to a rampart, rangers for creeps within 3 tiles of one.
Level 5 always has a fortifier, level 4 only if it was drawn: it repairs one rampart per tick by 3000 hits, back up to the level value, with energy the core hands it.
At levels 4 and 5 one tower per tick heals a damaged defender that stands on a rampart instead of shooting.
Level 5 raises the repair target of every rampart an incoming nuke will hit by the damage of that nuke (ramparts over containers excepted).
Defenders live until the collapse and leave an empty tombstone.

Container loot: each container gets up to three kinds out of utrium, lemergium, zynthium and keanium bars, oxidant, reductant, purifier, ghodium melt, battery, composite, crystal and liquid. The budget per container is 500 / 4,000 / 10,000 / 50,000 / 360,000 points at levels 1 to 5; a unit costs 5 points (the four bars, oxidant, reductant, purifier), 10 (battery, composite), 15 (crystal), 20 (ghodium melt) or 30 (liquid).

Core loot: when the core is destroyed its ruin holds commodities of one chain (silicon, metal, biomass or mist, fixed when the stronghold appears), from the first product up to the one of factory level equal to the stronghold level. Budget: 1,000 / 16,000 / 60,000 / 400,000 / 3,000,000 points; a unit costs 10, 220, 1,400, 5,100, 14,000 or 31,500 points by tier.
Towers and defenders get their orders from the core each tick. Once the core is destroyed they stop acting.
The other structures stay until the collapse time, and the ruin of the core lasts at least that long. While it lies there the sector gets no new stronghold, and without a stronghold no raids.
At the collapse time everything that carries the timer is removed without a ruin: towers, ramparts, roads, containers with what is still in them, the core and its lesser cores.

An active stronghold places a level 0 core (a "lesser core") every INVADER_CORE_EXPAND_TIME ticks of its level: 4000 at level 1 down to 2000 at level 5. The reference gives 42 as the most one stronghold can place.

The room is found by walking outward from the stronghold through room exits. The first room with a controller that nobody owns and without a core gets one; a reserved room qualifies. The walk goes on through rooms without a controller and rooms that already have a core, never through highways, owned rooms, novice or respawn areas.
A lesser core stands on a free tile within 5 tiles of the controller, has 100,000 hits, no structures and no creeps.
Each tick a lesser core adds 2 ticks to a reservation for "Invader", up to 5000.
If a player holds the reservation, it takes 2 ticks per tick off it instead, on top of the normal countdown, and reserves for itself once it is gone.
On a private server new strongholds are checked every 5 minutes and lesser cores every 15 minutes of real time, so both come somewhat later than their timers.

entries.name: Power banks
entries.title: Power banks
entries.summary: A power bank appears on a wall tile of a highway room with 500 to nearly 10,000 power and 2,000,000 hits. It returns 50% of every hit to the attacker and vanishes after 5000 ticks.
tasks: how much power is in a power bank
how long does a power bank last
what is left when a power bank is destroyed
how many attack parts for a power bank
does a power bank hit back ranged attackers
how many heal parts for a power bank
pitfalls: Ranged attackers are not safe: the bank returns half of ranged damage as well.
The power is in a ruin first. Use withdraw during its 10 ticks and pickup afterwards.
The bank sits in a wall: count the walkable tiles around it before you size the group, since melee attackers need range 1.
facts: Banks are created only in highway rooms (rooms the map marks as "bus"), each room on its own timer.
When a bank appears, the next one in that room is set 37,500 to 62,500 ticks ahead, whatever happens to the first.
It stands on a natural wall tile, at least 5 tiles from the room border, that touches at least one tile that is not a wall.
Power: a random amount from 500 to 5000; with a chance of 30% another 5000 is added.
It has 2,000,000 hits and 5000 ticks from the moment it appears.
Every hit sends 50% of its damage back to the creep that dealt it, for attack, rangedAttack and rangedMassAttack alike.
The returned damage is applied like any damage, so boosted TOUGH parts reduce it.
Per tick an ATTACK part does 30 and takes 15; a HEAL part restores 12. Unboosted, every ATTACK part needs 1.25 HEAL parts beside it.
With N ATTACK parts hitting every tick the bank falls in 66,667 ÷ N ticks. Finishing inside its 5000 ticks takes at least 14 parts, before travel time.
It cannot be dismantled, and withdraw does not work on it.
Destroyed, it leaves a ruin that holds the power for 10 ticks. After that the power lies on the tile as a dropped resource and decays like one.
When its timer runs out the bank is removed and nothing is left.
Carrying a full bank home takes up to 200 CARRY parts.
bank.owner.username is "Power Bank" and bank.my is false, so FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES returns it.
A power creep next to a power bank can renew itself there.

entries.name: Portals and shards
entries.title: Portals and shards
entries.summary: A portal moves every creep that ends its move on it to its destination: a fixed position in another room, or another shard. A stable portal has no timer; an unstable one disappears after 30,000 ticks.
tasks: what happens to a creep in a portal
how long does a portal last
can a power creep use a portal
does creep memory survive a shard change
send a creep through a portal
pitfalls: PathFinder.search gets only the cost matrices you give it and knows nothing of portals. A path of your own may cross a portal tile and send the creep away: write 255 on portal tiles.
Check portal.ticksToDecay before a round trip: an unstable portal may be gone when the creep wants to come back.
facts: Two kinds: portal.destination is a RoomPosition for a portal inside the shard, and an object {shard, room} for a portal to another shard.

A creep that stands on a portal tile after its move is sent on. Inside the shard it is at the destination position in the next tick; only its room and position change, so body, cargo and remaining life stay.
No call is needed: the portal acts like an exit tile.
Through a portal to another shard the creep arrives on some free tile of the destination room; the position is not fixed.
Your script runs on each shard separately with a Memory of its own. A creep that changes shard has no Memory.creeps entry there; hand over what it needs through InterShardMemory.
A power creep uses portals inside the shard only: it cannot step onto a portal that leads to another shard.
A portal does not block movement, but Room.findPath and moveTo treat its tile as blocked and walk around it, unless the portal tile itself is the target.
A portal with an expiry date turns unstable when that date passes: from then it has ticksToDecay, starting at 30,000, and is removed when the count ends.
The reference gives a stable time of 10 days for the portals that appear at random in the centre room of a sector.
StructurePortal is a plain Structure without owner: FIND_STRUCTURES returns it, FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES does not.
If the destination room is closed the creep is not moved.
The world consists of several shards, each a map of its own, connected by such portals.

entries.name: First spawn, respawn, novice and respawn areas
entries.title: First spawn, respawn, novice and respawn areas
entries.summary: The first spawn goes into any open room with a free controller; novice and respawn areas are walled-off sectors made for it. A respawn wipes everything you have in the world so that you can place a spawn again; your GCL stays.
tasks: do I keep my GCL after a respawn
how many rooms can I claim in a novice area
can I nuke a novice area
when do novice area walls come down
where can I place my first spawn
what does room status novice mean
will my room become a novice area
what happens to my structures when I respawn
pitfalls: A respawn gives nothing back and cannot be undone: creeps are gone, and what your storage and terminal held lies in ruins for whoever comes first.
With GCL above 3 a novice area is closed to you. Use a respawn area or any free room.
facts: The first spawn needs a room that is not closed, with a controller that nobody owns or has reserved, and you must have nothing else in the world.
Placing it makes the controller yours at level 1 with 20,000 ticks of safe mode. The spawn starts with 300 energy.
What other players left in that room is cleared: their creeps and construction sites are removed, their structures become ruins that last 100,000 ticks.
A respawn removes your creeps and construction sites, turns every structure of yours into a ruin, deletes your flags and sets your controllers back to level 0 without owner.
Those ruins keep what the structures held and last 500,000 ticks. They belong to the game, not to you: anyone who gets there can empty them.
GCL is kept, so after a respawn you may claim as many rooms as before.
After a respawn the new spawn can be placed 180 seconds later at the earliest.

You count as lost when you still have objects in the world but no spawn in a room whose controller is yours. With a claimed room and a creep that can build you can raise a new spawn instead of respawning.
A novice area is a sector shut off by walls that cannot be destroyed. The only way in is to place your first spawn there, and only with GCL 3 or lower.
In a novice room claimController returns ERR_FULL once you own 3 rooms. Reserving is not limited.
In a novice room safe mode leaves no cooldown.
Nukes: launchNuke returns ERR_INVALID_TARGET when the nuker or the target room is in a novice or respawn area. A nuke on its way into a room that has become such an area is removed without effect.
An area ends at a date in real time: the walls vanish and the rooms are normal rooms. Most novice sectors are also split into quarters by inner walls that vanish earlier than the outer wall.
A respawn area is walled off in the same way but open to any GCL and without the claim limit; only the nuke rule applies.
Strongholds send no lesser cores into novice or respawn areas.
Game.map.getRoomStatus(name) returns {status, timestamp}: status is "normal", "novice", "respawn" or "closed"; for an area the timestamp is the date in milliseconds at which it ends.
A closed room cannot be entered: a creep on the exit tile towards it stays where it is.

Before an area is made in a settled part of the world, the game signs the controllers of the free rooms in the sector: sign.username is SYSTEM_USERNAME ("Screeps") and sign.text is SIGN_PLANNED_AREA. Rooms you reserve are left out.

constants.name: SIGN_PLANNED_AREA
constants.value: A new Novice or Respawn Area is being planned somewhere in this sector. Please make sure all important rooms are reserved.

entries.name: The world map: room names, exits, sectors, terrain
entries.title: The world map: room names, exits, sectors, terrain
entries.summary: The world is a grid of rooms of 50 × 50 tiles, named by quadrant and number like W12N34. Rooms connect through the exit tiles on their borders; highways, the centre block and the centre room repeat every 10 rooms.
tasks: which room is north of mine
what is the centre room of a sector
why does my creep bounce between two rooms
facts: A room name is W or E with a number, then N or S with a number. E0 is x = 0 and W0 is x = −1; S0 is y = 0 and N0 is y = −1. The four rooms E0S0, W0S0, E0N0 and W0N0 meet at the origin of the map.
North is up and x grows to the right: above W5N5 lies W5N6, right of it W4N5. In the E and S halves the numbers grow to the right and downward.
A room has 50 × 50 tiles, x and y from 0 to 49, y = 0 being the top row. The tiles with x or y equal to 0 or 49 are the border: exit tiles or walls.

A side of a room has an exit when at least one of its border tiles is open ground. Game.map.describeExits names the neighbour on each such side without vision, and returns null for a room that is not open.
A creep that ends its move on an exit tile is in the next tick on the opposite border of the neighbouring room, at the same place along the edge (x 0 ↔ 49, y 0 ↔ 49).
It arrives on an exit tile again, so a creep that does not step off the border is sent back one tick later.
Creeps of Invader and Source Keeper never change rooms.
A room has from 1 to 4 exits.
Game.map.getWorldSize() is the number of rooms from one edge of the world to the other, the larger of width and height. WORLD_WIDTH and WORLD_HEIGHT are deprecated.
Game.map.getRoomLinearDistance is the larger of the two coordinate differences; with continuous = true it wraps around the edge of the world.
Game.map.findRoute looks at most about 30 rooms away from the start room in each direction.
Rooms whose x or y number ends in 0 are highways. They frame sectors of 9 × 9 rooms, so the pattern repeats every 10 rooms.
The server treats the 3 × 3 rooms whose two numbers end in 4, 5 or 6 as the centre block of a sector, and the room where both end in 5 as the centre room.

What the server ties to the kind of room: power banks and deposits are created in highway rooms; strongholds in the centre block except the centre room; raids in the centre block are always groups; lesser cores skip highways.
Terrain is fixed for each tile: wall (TERRAIN_MASK_WALL, 1), swamp (TERRAIN_MASK_SWAMP, 2) or plain (0). Room.Terrain.get returns one of the three; a tile with both bits reads as wall.
The terrain of every room of the shard is available without vision through Game.map.getRoomTerrain.

entries.name: Web API: auth tokens, endpoints and rate limits
entries.title: Web API: auth tokens, endpoints and rate limits
entries.summary: Your own tools talk to the server over HTTP under `/api/` and over a socket, signed with an auth token from your account settings. On the official server token requests are limited to 120 per minute, with lower limits on some endpoints.
tasks: call the server from a script
where does the auth token go in a request
read memory from outside the game
pitfalls: Give a tool a token, never the account password: the docs warn against handing a password to third-party programs.
On the official server read `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and, at 0, wait until `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` answer names the wait.
`POST /api/user/memory` changes nothing until your script has run another tick; read the value back after that.
Community API clients are built on these endpoints and may stop working when the server changes.
facts: The HTTP endpoints are the ones the game client itself uses. The docs call them undocumented, and they can change without notice.
Official server: create a token on the auth tokens page of your account settings. It never expires. It gives full access, or only the endpoints, websocket events and memory segments chosen for it.
Send the token as the `X-Token` request header or as the `_token` query parameter; both count the same.
Official server: requests from the browser and Steam clients are not rate limited; every request signed with a token is.
Official server: 120 token requests per minute in total, plus a lower limit on the endpoints in the table.
Over a limit the answer is HTTP `429`, and its text gives the wait in milliseconds.
Three answer headers tell where you stand: `X-RateLimit-Limit` (requests per window), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (left in this window) and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (end of the window in UTC epoch seconds).

Official server: the limit of one token can be lifted for 2 hours. The account owner opens the `noratelimit` page of the auth tokens settings for that token and presses Proceed. The page has a CAPTCHA, so a person has to do it.
Official server: `GET /api/auth/query-token` with the token tells what it may do and how long its unlimited period still runs.
Lines marked "open backend" are read from the public private-server code (screeps/backend-local). The official server lists the same paths in its limits table, but its code is not public.
Answers are JSON; a request that worked carries `ok: 1`.
Private server: a request without a valid token gets HTTP 401 and `{error: "unauthorized"}`.
Private server: a token comes from the Steam sign-in (`POST /api/auth/steam-ticket`) and is good for 60 seconds; every authenticated answer carries a fresh one in its `X-Token` header.
Open backend: `GET /api/user/memory` with `path` (dots between keys) returns that part of Memory as `gz:` followed by base64 of the gzipped JSON.

Open backend: `POST /api/user/memory` with `path` and `value` (at most 1 MB as JSON) does not write at once: it queues a hidden console command that assigns the value in your next tick. Without `path` it replaces all of Memory; without `value` it deletes the path.
Open backend: `GET /api/user/memory-segment` with `segment` and `POST /api/user/memory-segment` with `segment` and `data` read and write one segment directly: ids 0 to 99, at most 100 KB.

Open backend: `GET /api/game/room-terrain` with `room` returns the wall and swamp tiles as a list of `{room, x, y, type}`. With `encoded` set it returns one string of 2,500 digits instead: index y × 50 + x, bit 1 wall, bit 2 swamp.
Open backend: `POST /api/game/map-stats` with `rooms` (a list of names) and `statName` (a name ending in a number) returns for each room its status, owner and level, sign, safe mode and mineral.
Open backend: the socket is SockJS under `/socket`. On connect the server sends `time <ms>` and `protocol <n>`. Sign in with `auth <token>`; the answer is `auth ok <new token>` or `auth failed`.

Open backend: `subscribe <channel>` and `unsubscribe <channel>` pick the events. An event is a JSON array `[channel, data]`. After `gzip on`, an event that gets shorter that way arrives as `gz:` plus base64 of the deflated text.
Open backend: `user:<id>/…` channels are served only to the signed-in owner of that id.
Open backend: `room:<name>` sends the objects of a room after each tick: all of them first, then only what changed. It serves 2 rooms per account at a time; a third gets `subscribe limit reached`.
