entries.name: Account resources: CPU limit, CPU unlocks, pixels, access keys
entries.title: Account resources: CPU limit, CPU unlocks, pixels, access keys
entries.summary: On the official server the CPU limit is 20, or with full CPU unlocked it grows by 10 per GCL level up to 300. CPU unlocks, pixels and access keys belong to the account, show in `Game.resources`, and trade on the market without a terminal.
tasks: how much cpu do I get
what does a cpu unlock do
pitfalls: `Game.cpu.unlock`, `generatePixel` and `setShardLimits` are undefined on a private server, so calling them throws. Check `typeof Game.cpu.generatePixel == "function"` first.
`Game.cpu.unlockedTime` and `Game.shard.accessTime` are clock times, not ticks: compare them with `Date.now()`.
`generatePixel` spends the bucket: with the bucket full at 10,000 one pixel leaves no reserve for a heavy tick.
facts: Official server: the CPU limit is 20 without full CPU. With full CPU unlocked it grows by 10 for each GCL level until it reaches 300.
GCL is never lost, so the CPU it gives stays after a respawn.
Official server: full CPU comes from a subscription or, 24 hours at a time, from CPU unlock items: `Game.cpu.unlock()` uses up one `cpuUnlock` of the account.
Official server: if full CPU was not on before, an unlock can take up to 5 minutes to apply. With a subscription `Game.cpu.unlock()` returns ERR_FULL.

Official server: `Game.cpu.unlocked` says whether full CPU is on. `Game.cpu.unlockedTime` is when the unlock ends, in milliseconds since 1970; it is undefined without an unlock and with a subscription.
Official server: a pixel is an account resource made from spare CPU. `Game.cpu.generatePixel()` takes 10,000 CPU from the bucket for 1 pixel, or 9,000 with the Pixelization Deluxe upgrade.
`Game.resources` lists the account resources by name with their amounts: `token`, `cpuUnlock`, `pixel`, `accessKey`.
They trade on the market without rooms: `createOrder` for one needs no terminal and no `roomName`, and `deal` needs no room and pays no energy.
Selling into a buy order needs the amount in `Game.resources`; your own sell order is only active for the amount the account holds.
Official server: an access key opens a restricted shard for 30 days: `Game.shard.activateAccess()` uses up one `accessKey`. `Game.shard.access` and `Game.shard.accessTime` show the state.

Official server: `Game.cpu.setShardLimits({shard0: 20, shard1: 10})` divides the limit between shards. The values must add up to the total in `Game.cpu.shardLimits`. Once per 12 hours, otherwise ERR_BUSY.
Official server: on the PTR the CPU subscription is off after each copy; its order page turns on a free one until the next reset.

Private server: `Game.cpu` has only `limit`, `tickLimit`, `bucket`, `getUsed`, `getHeapStatistics` and `halt`. `unlock`, `generatePixel`, `setShardLimits`, `shardLimits`, `unlocked` and `unlockedTime` are not in the open engine.
Private server: a new account gets a CPU limit of 100, whatever its GCL.
Private server: `Game.shard` has `name` (the host name of the machine), `type` "normal" and `ptr` false, and nothing about access.

entries.name: Real time: what runs on the clock instead of on ticks
entries.title: Real time: what runs on the clock instead of on ticks
entries.summary: Game timers count ticks, and a tick has no fixed length. A few things follow the wall clock instead: the 180-second respawn wait, power creep cooldowns of 8 and 24 hours, market orders that end after 30 days, CPU unlocks, shard limits, novice areas and the weekly PTR copy.
tasks: which timers are in real time
does a cooldown count ticks or hours
how long is the respawn timeout
tick length on a private server
pitfalls: Do not turn ticks into hours with a fixed factor: the docs themselves give two different estimates for the same 20,000 ticks of safe mode.
For a clock timer compare with `Date.now()`, not with `Game.time`.
facts: A tick has no fixed length: it ends when the scripts of all players have run. How `Game.time` relates to real time depends on the load of the servers.
Private server: a tick lasts at least 1,000 ms by default; a tick that took longer is followed by the next at once.
Private server: `GET /api/game/tick` returns the shortest of the last 30 tick lengths in milliseconds.
Official server: after a respawn a new first spawn can be placed only 180 seconds later.
Private server: the open backend has the same 180,000 ms check against the date of the last respawn, but no code in the open repositories sets that date.
Power creeps: a dead one can be spawned again 8 hours later, deleting one takes 24 hours, and an experimentation period lasts 24 hours.
Market orders: an order is removed 30 days after it was created, and the fee for the unfilled rest is paid back.
Novice and respawn areas end at a date, not at a tick; `Game.map.getRoomStatus` gives it as `timestamp` in milliseconds. The area walls carry their own end date and go when it has passed.
A portal with an unstable date starts its 30,000-tick countdown once that date has passed.
Official server: a CPU unlock lasts 24 hours, shard access from a key 30 days, and `setShardLimits` works once per 12 hours.
Official server: the PTR gets a new copy of the world every Monday at 0:00 UTC.
Official server: API rate limits count per minute, hour or day, and a lifted limit lasts 2 hours.
Notifications: the `groupInterval` of `Game.notify` and the mail interval of the account are in minutes.
A controller sign stores the clock time it was written.

Private server: NPC events are looked at on the clock, while the timers they look at count ticks. Every 5 minutes the server checks for due power banks, invaders, deposits, strongholds and NPC market orders; every 15 minutes for strongholds that expand.

entries.name: E-mail notifications
entries.title: E-mail notifications
entries.summary: `Game.notify` queues up to 20 messages per tick for the e-mail address of your account. The game queues its own for attacks, controller level changes and script errors. Equal messages are merged, and the mail goes out in batches.
tasks: send myself an email from code
why do I get no notification mail
pitfalls: `Game.notify` in every tick of a lasting problem queues the same text again and again. Pass a `groupInterval`, or note in Memory that it was sent.
Invader creeps never mail you: detect them in code.
Put the important part first: on a private server everything after 500 characters is lost.
facts: `Game.notify(message, groupInterval)` queues one message. At most 20 per tick: the next call returns ERR_FULL. Each queued message costs the 0.2 CPU of an intent.
The message is cut at 1,000 characters. The open private server then stores only the first 500.

`groupInterval` is in minutes; 0 sends without waiting. Open private server: it is held between 0 and 1,440, the message waits for the next full interval mark of the clock, and the same text queued again before that mark is counted, not repeated.
Not available in the simulation room.

Attack: when a creep, power creep or structure with the attack notification on is hit, its owner gets "Your … in room … is under attack!". For a road, wall or container the owner of the room controller gets it.
The attack notification is on for every new creep, power creep and built structure. `notifyWhenAttacked(false)` turns it off for one object, and only issues an intent when the value changes.
Hits by Invader and Source Keeper creeps queue no attack message. A tower shot queues one whoever owns the tower.
The game also queues a message 3,000 ticks before a controller loses a level, when it has lost one, and when it gains one.
Open private server: an uncaught error of your script is queued as an error message, merged per text over the error interval of the account (30 minutes unless set).
Open backend: a private message from another player queues one too, unless you were online in the last 10 minutes or switched that off.
Open backend: the account settings are `POST /api/user/notify-prefs` with `disabled`, `disabledOnMessages`, `sendOnline`, `interval` (5 to 4,320 minutes) and `errorsInterval` (0 to 100,000 minutes).

Private server: once a minute the backend gathers the due messages of each account, at most one batch per interval (60 minutes unless set), and hands them to the `sendUserNotifications` event. The open backend sends no mail itself.
Private server: with notifications disabled in the account, queued messages are deleted unsent.

entries.name: The console: output, commands and limits
entries.title: The console: output, commands and limits
entries.summary: Text from console.log is collected during your tick and sent to the client after it. A console command runs once, right after your loop in the same tick, and its CPU counts toward that tick. The open backend takes commands of up to 1,024 characters over HTTP.
tasks: when does a console command run
does a console command cost cpu
send a console command from a script
pitfalls: A heavy command can push the tick over its CPU limit like the same code in `loop` would.
The open backend refuses a command over 1,024 characters: put the code in a module, put a function on `global`, and call that.
Helpers on `global` are gone after a global reset until your code sets them again; define them at the top of `main`, outside `loop`.
facts: A console command runs in the next tick of your script, after `loop` has returned, as if it stood at the end of `main`.
It is part of the same script run: its CPU time is added to that tick, and its intents go out with the tick.
The command is passed to `eval` in the global scope of your script; its value, turned into a string, is the result line.
So anything your code puts on `global` is a console helper: set `global.stats = function() {…}`, then type `stats()`.
Each command runs once: the runner takes all waiting commands for the tick and deletes them.
From outside the client: `POST /api/user/console` with `expression`. Open backend: as JSON the expression may be at most 1,024 characters. Official server: 360 such requests per hour for a token.
`console.log` joins its arguments with spaces after calling `toString()` on each: an object prints as `[object Object]` unless you pass `JSON.stringify(obj)`.
`console.log` text is HTML-escaped before it reaches the client. The open engine also defines `console.logUnsafe`, which is sent as it is; the API reference does not list it.
Open private server: after the tick, log lines and command results go to the socket channel `user:<id>/console` as `{messages: {log, results}}`; an uncaught error goes there as `{error}`.
Private server: console output is only published, not kept. A client that subscribes later does not get earlier lines.
In the web client the output also goes to the browser console.
Open backend: `POST /api/user/memory` uses the same queue, with a hidden command that assigns to `Memory` and prints no result.
Private server: no script run, no command. An account with no object in the world is not run, and its commands wait.

entries.name: Public Test Realm (PTR)
entries.title: Public Test Realm (PTR)
entries.summary: A separate official server that gets a fresh copy of the main world every Monday at 0:00 UTC. Building costs 1 energy and a controller level 1,000, so a test setup is quick. Everything on it, your code included, is wiped at the next copy.
pitfalls: Do not keep code only on the PTR: it is gone with the next Monday copy.
Energy budgets measured on the PTR say nothing about the main world: building and upgrading are almost free there.
facts: The PTR is a server of its own, with its own world data, scripts, memory and settings.
Every Monday at 0:00 UTC the main world and all accounts are copied to it, and the old PTR data is wiped, scripts included.
No account can be registered on the PTR; yours arrives with the copy.
The CPU subscription is off after each copy. The order page of the PTR turns on a free one until the next reset.
World mode and simulation mode both exist on it.
A construction site of any structure costs 1 energy.
Each controller level below 8 costs 1,000 energy instead of 200 to 10,935,000.
In the PTR mode of the open engine a new nuker holds 1 energy and 1 ghodium instead of 300,000 and 5000, and nuker cooldown and nuke flight take 100 ticks instead of 100,000 and 50,000.
The open engine is in PTR mode when the environment variable `PTR` is `true`.
Engine changes from the PTR are published under the `ptr` tag of the private server package: `npm install screeps@ptr`.
Upload code to the path `/ptr/api/user/code`, or with grunt-screeps and the option `ptr: true`.
`Game.shard.ptr` tells a script that it runs on the PTR. The open private server sets it to false.
The PTR has its own API reference at docs-ptr.screeps.com.

entries.name: Client tools for testing: test invaders, memory watch, console
entries.title: Client tools for testing: test invaders, memory watch, console
entries.summary: The client can drop NPC invaders into a room you own or reserved (at most 5 at a time, and only while no creep of another player is there), watch Memory paths tick by tick, and show console output in the browser console.
tasks: spawn test invaders in my room
why can I not create an invader
upload code from a local folder
pitfalls: A test invader fights for real: it hunts your creeps and breaks structures in its way.
A watch on an object shows `[object Object]`: watch a path that ends in a number or a string.
facts: The room side panel has Invasion controls that create NPC invaders by hand, to test defences.
Open backend: creating one is refused with "too many invaders exist" when the room already holds 5 Invader creeps.
Open backend: refused with "hostiles present" while a creep of any other player is in the room.
Open backend: refused with "not owned" unless you own the room controller or hold its reservation.

Open backend: the request names the size (small or big), the type (Melee, Ranged or Healer), the tile and whether it is boosted. The six bodies are those of raid invaders; the creep lives 1,500 ticks.
Open backend: boosted means LO on its HEAL parts, KO on RANGED_ATTACK, ZH on WORK and UH on ATTACK.
Open backend: only the player who created a test invader can remove it again.
It is an ordinary Invader creep, so its hits send no attack notification.
Memory inspector: add a watch on a Memory path and the panel shows its value, refreshed every tick.
Open backend: a watch is the socket channel `user:<id>/memory/<path>`. The value arrives as text, so an object shows as `[object Object]`; at most 50 paths per account are served.
In the web client all console output also goes to the browser console.
Open backend: the client switches the attack notification of a single object with `POST /api/game/set-notify-when-attacked`.
The in-game editor marks a module as binary with a switch and takes a file as its content.
The Steam client can upload code from a local folder; the contributed grunt article uses that for private servers.
Private server: room history is gathered in chunks of 20 ticks, but the open backend answers `/room-history` with "not implemented".

entries.name: The simulation room
entries.title: The simulation room
entries.summary: In simulation mode your script runs in your browser, not on the server, in a room named `sim`. Run time is not limited and `Game.cpu.getUsed()` returns 0, so it shows whether code works, not what it costs.
tasks: is cpu measured in the simulation
what can I not test in the simulation
does the simulation run while I am offline
pitfalls: CPU use cannot be measured there. To test cost or several rooms, the docs point to the PTR.
`debugger` pauses only in the simulation: in the world the script does not run in your browser.
facts: The engine has two variants. In simulation mode the script runs in your browser and the server takes no part in the calculation; the game API is the same.
Script run time is not limited there.
`Game.cpu.getUsed()` always returns 0.
`Game.notify` is not available.
The simulation does not run while you are away; scripts in the world do.
In Chrome the `debugger` keyword pauses the script at that line, and objects logged to the browser console can be opened and walked through.
The room is named `sim`: `Game.rooms.sim`.
A tower site costs 100 energy there instead of 5000.
Open backend: a branch is made active for the simulation apart from the world, as `activeSim` next to `activeWorld`.
The tutorial runs in the simulation.
The PTR has a simulation mode too.

entries.name: Binary modules and WebAssembly
entries.title: Binary modules and WebAssembly
entries.summary: A module can hold binary data instead of source text. `require` then returns its bytes, which `WebAssembly.Module` compiles: this is how C, C++ or Rust code runs inside a script.
tasks: send a binary module over the api
pitfalls: `require` caches only the bytes. Compile and instantiate outside `loop` and keep the instance, or the module is compiled again every tick.
facts: `require` of a binary module returns the raw bytes, not an exports object.
In the open engine the value is a `Buffer` decoded from the stored base64 text.
Run it with the WebAssembly API: `new WebAssembly.Module(bytes)`, then `new WebAssembly.Instance(module, imports)`, then call the functions in its `exports`.
The docs example compiles C with Emscripten as a side module (`emcc -s WASM=1 -s SIDE_MODULE=1`) and passes a `memory` and a `table` in `imports.env`.
In the in-game editor a module is made binary with a switch, and a file is uploaded as its content.
Over the API a binary module is `{binary: "<base64>"}` in the `modules` object. grunt-screeps sends every file that does not end in `.js` this way, named after the file without its extension.
The bytes are loaded once and kept in the module cache like any module, until the global scope is reset.
Open backend: the base64 text counts toward the 5 MB code limit.
The docs list starter kits for Rust, Kotlin, Python and TypeScript.

entries.name: Account rules: what the terms of service forbid
entries.title: Account rules: what the terms of service forbid
entries.summary: The terms of service allow one account per player. They forbid using bugs, using game mechanics or server resources for something they were not meant for, and disturbing the servers. Breaking them can end the account.
tasks: what do the terms of service forbid
facts: Each player may register one account only.
Bugs, flaws and vulnerabilities may not be used to your advantage.
Server resources and game mechanics may not be used for something the game does not intend them for.
Nothing may be done that could break, damage or disturb the game or its servers, and no illegal, harassing or defamatory material may be published through it.
Breaking one of these rules can end the account at once, with the deposits in it lost.

entries.name: Power creeps: life cycle, levels, limits
entries.title: Power creeps: life cycle, levels, limits
entries.summary: A power creep belongs to the account, not to a room. It costs one Global Power Level to create and one per level, lives 5000 ticks until renewed, and after a death cannot be spawned for 8 hours.
tasks: how does a power creep work
what happens when a power creep dies
how many hits does a power creep have
how much can a power creep carry
can a power creep attack or harvest
how many GPL levels does a power creep cost
what does deleting a power creep cost
pitfalls: FIND_CREEPS, FIND_MY_CREEPS and FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS do not return power creeps. Use FIND_POWER_CREEPS, FIND_MY_POWER_CREEPS and FIND_HOSTILE_POWER_CREEPS, or defence code never sees an enemy operator.
spawnCooldownTime and deleteTime are timestamps in milliseconds of real time: compare them with Date.now(), not with Game.time.
An unspawned power creep has no room and no pos, and its ticksToLive is NaN (the docs say undefined). Check powerCreep.room before you use it.
moveTo plans for creeps by default: road 1, plain 2, swamp 10. A power creep spends one tick on any tile, so pass {plainCost: 1, swampCost: 1} to get the shortest way.
It respawns with an empty store: what it carried is in the tombstone where it died.
facts: Global Power Level = floor((processed power / 1000) ^ (1/2)). Level n needs 1000 × n^2 power in total: 1000, 4000, 9000 for levels 1 to 3.
Free levels = GPL level − number of power creeps − sum of their levels. PowerCreep.create and upgrade each take one free level.
A new power creep is level 0 with 1,000 hits and a store of 100. Every level adds 1,000 hits and 100 capacity; level 25 is the last (26,000 hits, 2600 capacity).
Each level goes into one power. A power has 5 levels, and level k of it needs the creep to be at POWER_INFO[power].level[k − 1] before the upgrade.
create, upgrade, spawn, rename, delete and suicide are account intents. They run after all rooms of the tick, so the result shows in the next tick.

spawn(powerSpawn) needs your own active power spawn and a creep that is not on cooldown. The creep appears on the tile of the power spawn with full hits and 5000 ticks to live. Spawning takes no energy and no power.
One spawn per power spawn per tick, and none while another power creep stands on the power spawn tile. The call returns OK either way.
renew(target) from range 1 of a power bank or an active power spawn sets the life back to 5000 ticks. It is free, has no cooldown, and the code does not ask whose power spawn it is.
It dies when its hits reach 0, or at the end of the tick in which ticksToLive is 1. Rooms are processed before that check, so a renew in the same tick still saves it.
A death leaves a tombstone for 500 ticks that holds everything the creep carried.
After any death, suicide included, the creep is back on the account and cannot be spawned for 8 hours of real time. Its level and powers stay.
A nuke kills every power creep in the room it lands in.
delete() on an unspawned creep starts a 24-hour timer in real time; delete(true) or a spawn stops it.
When the timer ends the creep is removed and the account drops one GPL level, keeping the same share of progress inside the lower level. The levels the creep used are free again.
During an experimentation period (started in the game client, 24 hours) delete() removes the creep at once and no GPL is lost.
No body parts and no fatigue: it moves one tile per tick on road, plain and swamp alike.
Its actions are move, usePower, withdraw, transfer, say, drop, pickup, enableRoom and renew: one of each per tick, processed in this order.
It cannot harvest, build, repair, upgrade, attack, heal, claim or pull, and a creep cannot pull it.
It takes damage from attack, rangedAttack, rangedMassAttack and towers, and is healed by heal, rangedHeal and towers. Nothing else changes its hits: they do not come back on their own.
Invaders, source keepers and stronghold defenders treat it as a hostile.
It blocks a tile like a creep, crosses room edges like one and uses portals inside the shard. It cannot step onto a portal that leads to another shard.
Each step on a road brings the next decay of that road 100 ticks closer.
Game.powerCreeps holds every power creep of the account by name, spawned or not; its memory is Memory.powerCreeps[name].

entries.name: Powers: what each one does
entries.title: Powers: what each one does
entries.summary: An operator has 19 powers with up to 5 levels each. usePower spends ops, starts the cooldown of that power and, for most powers, puts a timed effect on the target that the rest of the engine reads.
tasks: how much faster is a spawn with operate spawn
how much energy does regen source give
how long does a power effect last
which factory level does operate factory set
can I use powers in another player's room
pitfalls: usePower does not check the type of the target. On a wrong target it returns OK and the processor drops the intent: no ops spent, no cooldown, no effect.
PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN counts when spawnCreep is processed, not while the creep is being built: put the effect on before you start a large creep.
Under PWR_OPERATE_LAB a reaction needs the raised amount of both reagents and that much room in the lab, or nothing happens (ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES, ERR_FULL). There is no partial run.
Under PWR_OPERATE_POWER processPower returns ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES unless the power spawn holds the full raised amount of power and the energy for it. A smaller rest waits until the effect ends.
PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY cannot be undone: the first use fixes the factory level, and a power creep with another level of the power can never operate that factory.

PWR_SHIELD needs a tile where a rampart may stand: not one that already has a rampart, not the room edge, not the tile next to an exit. A construction site under the creep is removed first, your own included, even when the shield then fails.
The docs give PWR_SHIELD an energy cost of 100, and POWER_INFO has that field, but the engine code of the power takes no energy.
PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION with nothing to move (target without energy, extensions full) spends nothing and starts no cooldown.
attack, rangedAttack and dismantle return ERR_INVALID_TARGET on a wall or rampart under PWR_FORTIFY; pick another target instead of repeating the call.
Dismantling a rampart made by PWR_SHIELD, or one under PWR_FORTIFY, gives no energy back.
facts: usePower works in a room without a controller, or with a controller that has isPowerEnabled. It does not work in another player's room that is in safe mode.
It also needs the power at level 1 or more, its cooldown over, enough ops in the creep, and for a power with a range a target within that range.
The effect is stored on the target with the power id, the power level and an end time. Scripts read it in target.effects as {power, effect, level, ticksRemaining}.
The same power used again on a target at the same or a higher level replaces the old effect and its time starts over. Against a higher active level the call returns ERR_FULL.
Effects of different powers sit side by side on one target: a tower under PWR_OPERATE_TOWER and PWR_DISRUPT_TOWER gets both factors.
Only the type of the target is checked, not its owner, PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION excepted: operate powers work on an ally's structures and disrupt powers on an enemy's.
PWR_GENERATE_OPS (no target; no ops; instant; cooldown 50): adds 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 ops to the creep's own store. What does not fit drops on its tile.

PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN (spawn; range 3; 100 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 300): a creep whose spawning starts under the effect takes × 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.35 / 0.2 of the normal time, rounded up. A creep already being spawned keeps its time.
PWR_OPERATE_TOWER (tower; range 3; 10 ops; lasts 100; cooldown 10): attack, heal and repair of the tower × 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 / 1.5, applied after the range falloff and rounded down.

PWR_OPERATE_STORAGE (storage; range 3; 100 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 800): capacity + 0.5M / 1M / 2M / 4M / 7M while it lasts. Afterwards the capacity is 1,000,000 again; the contents stay, but nothing more fits until the storage is below that.
PWR_OPERATE_LAB (lab; range 3; 10 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 50): runReaction and reverseReaction called on this lab handle 5 + 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 units per call. The lab cooldown does not change.

PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION (storage, terminal, factory or container; range 3; 2 ops; instant; cooldown 50): moves energy from the target into the room owner's extensions, nearest to the target first, until 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 % of their total capacity has been moved or the target is empty. Spawns get nothing.
PWR_OPERATE_OBSERVER (observer; range 3; 10 ops; lasts 200 / 400 / 600 / 800 / 1000; cooldown 400): observeRoom accepts a room at any distance. The range check sits in the API call.

PWR_OPERATE_TERMINAL (terminal; range 3; 100 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 500): the energy this terminal pays for a send or a deal × 0.9 / 0.8 / 0.7 / 0.6 / 0.5 (rounded up), and its cooldown becomes 9 / 8 / 7 / 6 / 5 instead of 10 ticks.
PWR_DISRUPT_SPAWN (spawn; range 20; 10 ops; lasts 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5; cooldown 5): while it lasts, the creep being spawned makes no progress: its finish time moves back one tick per tick.
PWR_DISRUPT_TOWER (tower; range 50; 10 ops; lasts 5; cooldown 0): attack, heal and repair of the tower × 0.9 / 0.8 / 0.7 / 0.6 / 0.5.
PWR_DISRUPT_SOURCE (source; range 3; 100 ops; lasts 100 / 200 / 300 / 400 / 500; cooldown 100): while it lasts and the source is not full, its regeneration timer stands still.

PWR_SHIELD (no target; no ops; lasts 50; cooldown 20): puts a rampart of 5000 / 10000 / 15000 / 20000 / 25000 hits on the creep's tile, owned by the creep's owner. It is removed when the time is up, does not decay before, and cannot be repaired (hitsMax 0).

PWR_REGEN_SOURCE (source; range 3; no ops; lasts 300; cooldown 100): every 15 ticks the source gains 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 / 250 energy, up to its capacity: at most 1000 / 2000 / 3000 / 4000 / 5000 per use. A full source gains nothing.

PWR_REGEN_MINERAL (mineral; range 3; no ops; lasts 100; cooldown 100): every 10 ticks the mineral gains 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 units: 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 per use. It does nothing on a depleted mineral.

PWR_DISRUPT_TERMINAL (terminal; range 50; 50 / 40 / 30 / 20 / 10 ops; lasts 10; cooldown 8): nobody can withdraw from the terminal, its owner included, and PWR_OPERATE_EXTENSION cannot draw from it. The engine code reads the effect in these two places only.
PWR_OPERATE_POWER (power spawn; range 3; 200 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 800): one processPower call handles 1 + 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 power, each with 50 energy.

PWR_FORTIFY (wall or rampart; range 3; 5 ops; lasts 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5; cooldown 5): the target takes no damage from attack, rangedAttack, rangedMassAttack, dismantle or towers. A nuke still damages it.
PWR_OPERATE_CONTROLLER (controller; range 3; 200 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 800): the level 8 limit of 15 upgrade energy per tick rises by 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 / 50. Below level 8 it changes nothing.

PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY (factory; range 3; 100 ops; lasts 1000; cooldown 800): on a factory without a level it sets the level to the level of the power, for good. After that only a power of exactly that level works on it. Commodities that have a level can only be produced while the effect is active.

effects can also hold two entries no power creep makes: EFFECT_INVULNERABILITY (stronghold core before it deploys, controller of a stronghold room: attacks are refused) and EFFECT_COLLAPSE_TIMER (stronghold structures: removed when it ends).

entries.name: Ops: what powers are paid with
entries.title: Ops: what powers are paid with
entries.summary: Ops is a resource that only PWR_GENERATE_OPS makes. A power takes its ops from the store of the power creep that uses it; apart from that ops can be stored, moved and traded like any resource.
tasks: how many ops does a power cost
how fast can I generate ops
can I buy ops on the market
pitfalls: PWR_GENERATE_OPS at level 5 brings 160 ops per 1000 ticks. Keeping PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN on one spawn takes 100 of them and PWR_OPERATE_POWER 200: an operator that runs several effects needs ops from outside, from a second operator or the market.
Ops are taken when the power is applied, whether the effect is then used or not: PWR_OPERATE_TOWER on a tower that never fires costs the same.
facts: PWR_GENERATE_OPS adds 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 ops per use at power levels 1–5, with a cooldown of 50 ticks: 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.08 / 0.12 / 0.16 ops per tick.
It needs no target and costs nothing, but the room rule holds for it too: no controller, or a controller with isPowerEnabled.
Ops beyond the free space of the creep fall on its tile as a dropped resource.
A power is paid from the store of the creep that uses it. Ops in a storage or terminal count only after a withdraw.
usePower is processed before withdraw in the same tick, and the API call checks the store as it was at the start of the tick: ops you take out now pay for a power next tick.
PWR_GENERATE_OPS, PWR_SHIELD, PWR_REGEN_SOURCE and PWR_REGEN_MINERAL cost no ops: POWER_INFO has no ops field for them.
PWR_DISRUPT_TERMINAL is the one power whose cost depends on the level: 50 / 40 / 30 / 20 / 10 ops.
ops is in RESOURCES_ALL: transfer, withdraw, drop, storage, terminal, container and market orders take it like any other resource.
A power creep holds 100 units per level plus 100, ops and everything else together.
Ops a power creep carries when it dies stay in its tombstone for 500 ticks.

entries.name: Processing power into Global Power Level
entries.title: Processing power into Global Power Level
entries.summary: A power spawn burns 1 power and 50 energy per processPower call, one call per tick, and adds 1 to the account's power total. Global Power Level n needs 1000 × n^2 in total.
tasks: how much power for the next GPL level
how fast can I process power
how much power does a power spawn hold
pitfalls: Each level costs more than the one before: level n alone takes (2n − 1) × 1000 power, and every power takes 50 energy. Plan the energy before you buy the power.
processPower returns ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES when the power spawn has power but less than 50 energy: keep both filled.
facts: processPower takes 1 power and 50 energy out of the power spawn and adds 1 to the power total of the account.
One call per power spawn per tick; a room has one power spawn, at room level 8.
The power spawn holds 100 power and 5000 energy: 100 ticks of work per fill, and both run out together.
Under PWR_OPERATE_POWER one call handles 1 + 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 power at the same energy rate: up to 6 power and 300 energy per tick, so a full power spawn lasts 16 ticks.
The power spawn must be active: in your room, at a level that allows it. Otherwise nothing is processed (ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH).
Game.gpl.level = floor((total / 1000) ^ (1/2)). progress is the total minus what the current level needed; progressTotal is the size of the step to the next level, (2 × level + 1) × 1000.
Each GPL level is one point for power creeps: creating one takes a point, and so does every level of it.
Power comes from power banks in highway rooms and from the market.
The total can go down: when a deleted power creep is removed, the account drops one GPL level.

entries.name: Hard limits: text lengths, counts, per-tick caps and sizes
entries.title: Hard limits: text lengths, counts, per-tick caps and sizes
entries.summary: Every fixed cap in one place. Text is counted in characters, not bytes. Most caps answer with an error code; a few cut the text or drop the call without telling you.
tasks: how long can a creep name be
how long can a controller sign be
how many construction sites can I have
how many flags can I place
how big can a memory segment be
list of all limits and caps
pitfalls: The calls with a cap of 50 per tick give no sign when you are over it. Count them yourself when you issue many.
Nothing throws inside your code when the Memory object grows past 2 MB: the save fails after the tick. Watch the size yourself.
A sign or say text that is too long is not refused, only cut. Check the length before you rely on the end of the text.
facts: Creep name: 100 characters. A longer one makes spawnCreep return ERR_INVALID_ARGS.
Spawn name given to createConstructionSite: 100 characters, else ERR_INVALID_ARGS.
Power creep name: 100 characters, else ERR_INVALID_ARGS from PowerCreep.create and rename.
Flag name: 100 characters from a script, else ERR_INVALID_ARGS. The server request that places a flag from outside a script accepts 60.
Behind those checks, every name and sign inside an intent is cut to 100 characters when the intent is stored.
Creep.say: only the first 10 characters are shown. No error.
Controller sign: cut to 100 characters. signController does not check the length and returns OK.
Terminal send description: 100 characters, else ERR_INVALID_ARGS.
Game.notify: 20 calls per tick, the next returns ERR_FULL. The text is cut to 1000 characters, and to 500 when the server stores it. The group interval is capped at 1440 minutes.
Body: 50 parts, else ERR_INVALID_ARGS.
Construction sites: 100 for the whole account, those placed earlier in the same tick included. Then ERR_FULL.
Flags: 10,000, then ERR_FULL.
Structures per room: the number CONTROLLER_STRUCTURES gives for the type and the room level, sites included; then ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH. Roads 2500, walls 2500, ramparts 2500, containers 5.
Rooms: as many as your GCL level, else ERR_GCL_NOT_ENOUGH. Inside a novice area 3 at most, else ERR_FULL.
Power creep level: 25, then upgrade returns ERR_FULL.
Market orders: 300, then createOrder returns ERR_FULL.
Game.market.deal: 10 per tick, the next returns ERR_FULL.
cancelOrder, changeOrderPrice and extendOrder: 50 each per tick. Calls above that still return OK and are dropped.
PowerCreep.create and a power creep's rename, upgrade, delete, spawn and suicide: 50 each per tick, dropped in the same silent way.
Memory: 2 MB, counted as 2 × 1024 × 1024 characters of JSON. RawMemory.set throws above that. A Memory object that serialises longer is not saved: the Memory of the tick before stays.
Memory segments: ids 0 to 99, 100 × 1024 characters each, 10 active at a time. RawMemory.segments may hold 10 entries at the end of a tick, the loaded ones included.
A segment that is too long or not a string, or an eleventh entry, makes the runtime throw after your code has run. The Memory changes and the intents of that tick are then not saved.
Room visuals: 500 KB per room and tick; the map visual 1000 KB. The drawing call that passes the limit throws.
Code: all modules of one upload together 5 MB as JSON. The server rejects more.
Console command sent through the server API: 1024 characters.
CPU: a tick gets at most 500, however full the bucket is. The bucket holds 10,000.
Heap: 256 MB plus the size of the terrain data.
PathFinder.search: 64 rooms at most (16 unless you set maxRooms), and 2000 operations unless you set maxOps.
Transactions: the last 100 incoming and the last 100 outgoing are loaded for Game.market.
Every text limit compares the length of the JavaScript string, so it counts characters and not bytes.

entries.name: Stores: which structure holds what, and how much
entries.title: Stores: which structure holds what, and how much
entries.summary: A store has either one shared capacity for any resource (creep, container, storage, terminal, factory) or a fixed capacity per resource and nothing else (spawn, extension, tower, link, lab, nuker, power spawn). A transfer only works into a store that has capacity for that resource.
tasks: which resources can a structure hold
capacity of storage terminal and factory
how much does an extension hold at each level
what happens to the cargo when carry parts are destroyed
can I withdraw from a nuker
what happens when a store is over capacity
pitfalls: On a spawn, extension, tower, link or lab, ask with the resource: store.getFreeCapacity(RESOURCE_ENERGY). Without it you get null, and null > 0 is false.
A lab that still holds one unit of a mineral refuses every other mineral. Empty it completely before you change what it holds.
A transfer with an explicit amount larger than the free space returns ERR_FULL and moves nothing. Leave the amount out to move what fits.
facts: Per-resource stores: spawn 300 energy, tower 1000, link 800, nuker 300,000 energy and 5000 ghodium, power spawn 5000 energy and 100 power. They hold nothing else.
Shared stores, any mix of resources up to the total: container 2000, storage 1,000,000, terminal 300,000, factory 50,000.
The capacity for one resource is its own entry if the store has one, else what is left of the shared total. Zero means the store cannot take that resource.
transfer into a store without capacity for the resource returns ERR_INVALID_TARGET; into a full one, ERR_FULL.
Lab: 2000 energy plus 3000 of one other resource. An empty lab takes any resource that is not energy; the first unit fixes the type until the lab holds none of it again.
Extension: 50 energy up to room level 6, 100 at level 7, 200 at level 8. It is set every tick from the room level.
Storage, terminal and factory have capacity 0 while the room is not owned by their owner or the level does not allow them. Nothing goes in then; withdrawing what is inside still works.
PWR_OPERATE_STORAGE adds 500,000 to 7,000,000 to the storage capacity, by power level, while it lasts.
Creep: 50 per CARRY part that still has hits; a boosted part counts ×2 (KH), ×3 (KH2O) or ×4 (XKH2O).
When damage takes out CARRY parts, the cargo above the new capacity drops on the creep's tile, energy first, then the other resources in the order of RESOURCES_ALL.
Power creep: 100 at level 0, plus 100 per level.

A structure's store is never trimmed. When its capacity falls (an extension after a downgrade, a storage in a lost room) the contents stay and it counts as full until it is emptied below the new capacity.
getCapacity() without a resource is null on a per-resource store, and getCapacity(resource) is null for a resource the store cannot hold. getFreeCapacity follows the same rule.
store[RESOURCE] reads 0, not undefined, for a resource that is not there.
withdraw is refused on nukers and power banks (ERR_INVALID_TARGET). Other structures, tombstones and ruins give up what they hold.
Tombstones and ruins only give: transfer accepts creeps, power creeps and structures as target, nothing else.

entries.name: Losing or giving up a room: what resets and what stays
entries.title: Losing or giving up a room: what resets and what stays
entries.summary: A room stops being yours through unclaim() or when its controller counts down to level 0. The controller is reset. Your structures stay where they are and stay yours, but they stop working.
tasks: what happens to my structures when I unclaim
what happens when a controller reaches level 0
how long until an abandoned room is lost
who can destroy structures in an abandoned room
clean up a room I took over
old structures of the previous owner
can I claim a room again after unclaim
pitfalls: unclaim() asks no question and cannot be undone: level and progress are gone at once.
Empty storage and terminal before you give a room up. Afterwards they take nothing in, and anyone standing next to them can take out.
A reservation is not enough to destroy() leftovers: the controller must be yours. In a room you only reserve, dismantle them.
facts: unclaim() takes effect when the tick it is called in is processed: the controller loses its owner, goes to level 0 and progress 0, its downgrade timer is cleared, a running safe mode ends, the safe mode stock is 0 and power is switched off.
It also starts the safe mode cooldown of 50,000 ticks on that controller, except in a novice area. A later claim does not clear it: claiming only sets owner, level, progress, timer and reservation.

Downgrade: when the timer runs out the level drops by one and the timer restarts at half of the lower level's maximum. From level 1 the room becomes neutral, with the same reset as unclaim; the upgrade block is cleared as well.
A level 8 room with a full timer that nobody upgrades is lost after about 420,000 ticks: the full level 8 timer, then half a timer for each level below. A level 1 room lasts 20,000.
You get a notification 3000 ticks before each downgrade and one when it happens.
The room leaves your list of rooms, so its GCL slot is free again.
Structures are not touched. Nothing is removed or refunded, and they keep their owner: structure.my stays true and you keep vision of the room while they stand.
Every owned structure there becomes inactive: isActive() is false and its methods return ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH.
Spawns and extensions no longer count for energyAvailable. Storage, terminal and factory drop to capacity 0. Ramparts get hitsMax 0, so they cannot be repaired and decay away.
Walls in a room with a controller below level 2 also have hitsMax 0 and cannot be repaired.
While the room has no owner, destroy() works for nobody. Anyone can dismantle or attack what stands there, and withdraw from it unless a closed rampart of the old owner covers it.
A new owner can destroy() every structure in the room, the old owner's included, as long as no creep of another user is in the room.
Leftover structures count against the new owner's limits: a new site is allowed by the number of structures and sites of that type in the room, whoever owns them.
For the new owner the old structures stay inactive, and the old owner's closed ramparts still block the new owner's creeps.
If you claim the room again, your old structures work again as far as the level allows: the check only asks for the controller's owner and the allowance.
A newly claimed controller is level 1 and gets no safe mode with the claim. The stock grows by one for each level gained by upgrading.

entries.name: What a destroyed structure leaves behind
entries.title: What a destroyed structure leaves behind
entries.summary: A structure destroyed by damage or by destroy() becomes a ruin that keeps its contents for 500 ticks. None of the build cost comes back. A nuke leaves no ruin at all.
tasks: what happens when a structure is destroyed
how long does a ruin stay
what happens to the storage contents when it is destroyed
pitfalls: destroy() refunds nothing, and dismantle little: a full spawn has 5000 hits and returns at most 25 of the 15,000 energy it cost.
Take the contents out of a ruin with withdraw within 500 ticks. After that they lie on the ground and shrink every tick.
facts: A ruin appears when a structure reaches 0 hits by attack, dismantle or tower fire, and when it is removed with destroy().
The ruin holds exactly the store of the structure. Nothing of the build cost is added.
It stays 500 ticks, the ruin of a power bank 10. Then the contents drop on the tile.
The ruin of a structure with a collapse timer (a stronghold) stays at least until that timer ends.
ruin.structure tells what it was: id, type, hitsMax and owner of the destroyed structure, with hits 0.
A ruin of your structure is your object: the room stays visible to you until it is gone.
A structure destroyed by a nuke leaves no ruin: its contents are lost. A landing nuke also removes the ruins already in the room.
Decay makes no ruin: a road or rampart at 0 hits just disappears, a container drops its contents on the tile.

dismantle pays the dismantling creep 0.005 energy per hit removed, rounded down for each call. One WORK part removes 50 hits, so an unboosted creep needs 4 WORK parts to get 1 energy per tick and gets nothing with fewer. attack, tower fire and destroy() pay nothing.
A destroyed spawn takes the creep it was spawning with it.
Damage that destroys a structure writes EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED into the room's event log. destroy() writes no event.
A ruin cannot be removed by a script: destroy() only acts on types that can be built. It goes when its timer ends, also when it is already empty, or when a nuke lands. It does not block movement.

entries.name: Season 1: score containers and collectors
entries.title: Season 1: score containers and collectors
entries.summary: Season 1 rules as the public server mod states them: a resource called score appears in containers all over the map and counts when a creep carries it into a collector in a highway crossing room.
tasks: how does scoring work in season 1
how often do score containers spawn
how much does a score collector take
can terminals send to other players in a season
pitfalls: This is the public mod. The official season server loaded one more file that is not public, so details there may have differed.

The room left in a collector is its capacity for score: read collector.store.getFreeCapacity(RESOURCE_SCORE) before you walk there. At zero that call gives null and transfer returns ERR_INVALID_TARGET.
facts: Score is a resource (RESOURCE_SCORE, "score") that creeps and stores hold like any other.
Score containers: every 250 ticks each room has a 1% chance to get one on a free tile.
A container holds 500 to 2500 score (53 of 100), 3500 to 6500 (29 of 100) or 8500 to 11,500 (18 of 100).
It disappears when it is empty or when its timer ends. The timer is a random number from the same band as the amount, at most 5000 ticks.
The map runs in cycles of 50,000 ticks. From tick 10,000 to 15,000 of a cycle no containers appear; from 45,000 to 50,000 they hold double.
In a script: room.find(FIND_SCORE_CONTAINERS); a container has store, decayTime and ticksToDecay. Take the score with withdraw.
Score collectors stand in highway crossing rooms (both room coordinates end in 0), one per room, placed once.
Every tile up to 5 tiles around a collector is a wall, an 11 by 11 block with the collector in the middle. A wall has 70 to 130 million hits; about one in five has 300 million.
Scoring: transfer score into a collector. Every unit adds 1 to the score of the creep's owner.
A collector starts with room for 20,000. Each tick it loses the room that was filled and gains 20, never above 20,000. Over time one collector takes 20 score per tick from all players together.
A collector blocks movement. Find it with room.find(FIND_SCORE_COLLECTORS).
Terminals: a send to a room whose terminal belongs to another player is cancelled.
Stronghold loot includes score.
Ranking: by score, ties by GCL points. It is recalculated every 60 seconds.

entries.name: Season 2: symbols and decoders
entries.title: Season 2: symbols and decoders
entries.summary: Season 2 rules as the public server mod states them: 22 symbol resources appear in containers, every room with a controller has a decoder for one symbol, and decoding there counts more the higher the room level.
tasks: how does scoring work in season 2
how is the season 2 score calculated
pitfalls: Each decoder takes one symbol only. Any other symbol has to be carried to a room whose decoder is made for it.
The multiplier is that of the room where the decoder stands, at the moment of the transfer. The same symbols are worth 243 times more in a level 8 room than in a level 3 room.
This is the public mod. The official season server loaded one more file that is not public, so details there may have differed.
facts: There are 22 symbol resources, symbol_aleph to symbol_taw, listed in the constant SYMBOLS. Creeps and stores hold them like any resource.
Symbol containers: every 250 ticks each room has a 1% chance to get one. It holds one random symbol: 500 to 2500 units (53 of 100), 3500 to 6500 (29 of 100) or 8500 to 11,500 (18 of 100).
A container disappears when empty or after its timer, at most 5000 ticks.
Every room with a controller has one symbol decoder for one random symbol. It stands on a wall tile with an open tile next to it, at least 5 tiles from the sources, the mineral and the controller.

Decoding: transfer the decoder's own symbol into it. You are credited the amount times the multiplier of the room's controller level: 1 at levels 1 to 3, then 3, 9, 27, 81 and 243 at levels 4 to 8. In a room at level 0 nothing is credited.
The credit goes to the owner of the creep that transfers, whoever owns the room.
A decoder has room for 1,000,000 of its symbol and is emptied every tick. It has no capacity for anything else.
Score: your decoded amounts per symbol are put in order and the n-th is multiplied by n, then all are added. The order comes from the default JavaScript sort, which compares the numbers as text.

In a script: Game.symbols gives the decoded amount per symbol, Game.score the score. A decoder has resourceType and scoreMultiplier; a container has resourceType, store and ticksToDecay. Find them with FIND_SYMBOL_DECODERS and FIND_SYMBOL_CONTAINERS.
Terminals: a send to a room whose terminal belongs to another player is cancelled.
Stronghold cores hold symbols as loot.
Ranking: by score, ties by GCL points, recalculated every 60 seconds.

entries.name: Season 5: thorium and reactors
entries.title: Season 5: thorium and reactors
entries.summary: Season 5 rules as the public server mod states them: every room with a controller has a thorium deposit, thorium shortens the life of whatever shares its tile, and burning it in a reactor in a sector centre room gives score.
tasks: how does scoring work in season 5
what does thorium do to a creep
how do I claim a reactor
how much score does a reactor give
pitfalls: The penalty counts the whole tile. A hauler standing on a container that holds thorium ages by the sum of both loads, and the container decays faster too.
Carry thorium in loads below 100 where you can: 99 costs one tick per tick, 100 costs two.
Keep a reactor from running empty: the score per tick only grows with unbroken work, and one empty tick puts it back to 1.
This is the public mod. The official season server loaded one more file that is not public, so details there may have differed.
facts: Thorium is a resource with the name "T" (RESOURCE_THORIUM).
Every room with a controller gets one thorium mineral, on a wall tile with an open tile next to it, at least 5 tiles from the sources, the other mineral and the controller.
It holds 10,000, 22,000, 45,000 or 67,000 thorium, with chances of 10, 40, 40 and 10 in 100. It does not refill: the empty mineral is removed.

Thorium penalty: each tick the thorium in the stores of all objects on one tile is added up, and floor(log10(total)) ticks are taken from every object on that tile. A creep loses life; other objects lose time on their decay timers.
So 1 to 9 thorium costs nothing, 10 to 99 one extra tick per tick, 100 to 999 two, 1000 to 9999 three. Only thorium inside a store counts, not a pile on the ground.
Reactors stand in the centre room of each sector (both room coordinates end in 5), one per room, with room for 1000 thorium.
creep.claimReactor(reactor) makes you the owner. It needs a CLAIM part with hits and range 1, nothing else, so it also takes a reactor from another player.

An owned reactor that holds thorium burns 1 per tick and gives its owner 1 + floor(log10(1 + ticks of continuous work)) score that tick: 1 at first, 2 from tick 9, 3 from tick 99, 4 from tick 999, 5 from tick 9999.
The count of continuous work starts when an owned reactor first holds thorium and goes back to zero when the reactor is empty. A change of owner does not reset it.
Thorium cannot be withdrawn from a reactor.
In a script: room.find(FIND_REACTORS); a reactor has owner, my, store and continuousWork.
A respawn gives up your reactors and their work count.
Terminals: a send to a room whose terminal belongs to another player is cancelled.
Stronghold loot includes thorium.
Ranking: by score, ties by GCL points, recalculated every 60 seconds.

entries.name: How your code runs each tick
entries.title: How your code runs each tick
entries.summary: Each tick the server calls the loop function that your main module exports, once, inside your own V8 isolate. The isolate and its global scope stay alive between ticks until a reset; the Game object is built new every tick.
tasks: how does my code run each tick
what happens when my script throws an error
does code outside the loop run every tick
pitfalls: A value kept in the global scope can be gone on any tick. Always write the rebuild path: if the cache is missing, compute it again.
The first tick after a reset compiles and runs every module again and finds all caches empty. It is the most expensive tick; do not start other heavy work in it.
The built-in lodash is version 3.10.1, not 4. Functions that came with lodash 4 are missing: go by the lodash 3 documentation.
facts: A tick has two stages: first every player script runs, then every room is processed. Game.time goes up after both.
Each player has one isolate: a separate V8 heap with a limit of 256 MB plus the size of the world terrain data. It is kept from tick to tick.
Each tick the runtime calls require("main") and then the loop function main exports.
require runs a module once and keeps its exports. Code outside functions therefore runs only when the module is first loaded, which is after a reset.
If main exports no loop function, the module cache is dropped every tick and all modules run again from the top each tick.
An unknown module name throws "Unknown module". A module that is required again while it is still loading throws "Circular reference to module".
require("lodash") returns the built-in lodash, the same object as the global _. It is version 3.10.1.
A binary module comes back from require as a buffer with its bytes.
Game is made new every tick. Global variables, module-level variables and the module cache stay as they are.
The classes (Room, Creep, RoomPosition and the rest) are created once per isolate, so methods you add to their prototypes stay until the next reset.
The constants (OK, FIND_*, BODYPART_COST and so on) are written onto global again every tick, as fresh copies.

Global reset: the isolate is thrown away, and with it every variable and the module cache, when you upload new code, when the heap limit is hit, when the hard timeout fires, when you call Game.cpu.halt(), when the script has not run for 3 minutes, and when the server restarts its runners.
A reset does not touch Memory, memory segments or anything in the game world.
An error that your code does not catch ends the loop for this tick only. The intents queued before it, Memory and the segments are still saved, and the next tick runs in the same isolate.
The loop is stopped when it runs longer than Game.cpu.tickLimit (plus 5 ms of slack). That counts as an error of the same kind: "Script execution timed out: CPU time limit reached".
If the script cannot be stopped that way, the run is aborted after 5 seconds: nothing of the tick is saved and the isolate is restarted.
Console commands run in the same tick right after your loop, with the same globals, and their CPU counts as yours.
A player with no object left in the world (no creep, structure or construction site) is set inactive and the script is no longer run.

entries.name: Intents: how a call becomes an action
entries.title: Intents: how a call becomes an action
entries.summary: A method that changes the game does not act at once. It checks the state from the start of the tick, queues an intent and returns OK; the intent is carried out after all scripts have run. Each queued intent costs 0.2 CPU.
tasks: what if I call the same method twice in a tick
does a failed call cost cpu
are intents kept when the script crashes
what happens to my actions when I run out of cpu
why did a call return OK but nothing happened
pitfalls: One creep, the same method, two targets (two transfers, two attacks): only the last call happens.
The fee is taken when the intent is queued. If the processor drops it later, the 0.2 CPU is still spent.
Game.cpu.halt() discards the intents of the tick in which it is called.
facts: An action method first checks its conditions against the objects as they were when the tick started. On an error code nothing is queued and no fee is charged.
The fee is 0.2 CPU per intent. It is added to Game.cpu.getUsed() at the moment the call returns OK.
Most actions are stored per object and method name. Calling the same method again on the same object replaces the earlier call and is not charged again.
say and pull are free.

Some calls are lists: every call adds an entry and costs 0.2 CPU. These are createConstructionSite, createFlag, Flag.remove, ConstructionSite.remove, Structure.destroy, Game.notify, and the market and power creep account calls.
Caps per tick on the lists: 20 notifications, 10 market deals, 50 order cancellations.
Flag.setPosition and Flag.setColor queue two entries each, a remove and a create: 0.4 CPU.
Creep.cancelOrder(name) takes a queued intent of that creep back and returns the 0.2 CPU.
What the bucket is charged is counted from the final list after the loop: 0.2 for every stored intent, list entries one by one.
Values in an intent are cleaned before it is stored: numbers go through parseInt (a fraction is cut off), names and signs are cut to 100 characters.
OK means queued, not done. When the intent is applied the processor checks range, amounts and ownership again and drops the intent silently if they no longer hold.
An intent for an object that is not yours is ignored by the processor.
Script error or CPU stop: the intents queued up to that point are still saved and carried out.
The whole tick is lost, intents included, in four cases: Game.cpu.halt(), a full heap, the hard timeout, and a broken segment rule at the end of the tick.

entries.name: Pathfinding: PathFinder.search, findPath and moveTo
entries.title: Pathfinding: PathFinder.search, findPath and moveTo
entries.summary: PathFinder.search finds the cheapest path over terrain and your cost matrices, through up to 64 rooms. Room.findPath, findClosestByPath and moveTo call it with a ready-made cost matrix that knows structures, creeps and roads.
tasks: what does moveTo add to the pathfinder
pitfalls: A goal with range 0 on a tile nobody can stand on (a source, a controller, a wall) uses up all maxOps and comes back incomplete. Give such goals a range of at least 1.
incomplete: true still comes with a path, to the nearest point reached. Following it without a check walks the creep into a dead end.
The default matrix treats every creep as a wall, also one that will have moved away next tick. For long routes use ignoreCreeps and solve blocking near the creep.
moveTo returns ERR_TIRED before it does any path work, and OK without any intent when the creep already stands on the target.
facts: PathFinder.search defaults: plainCost 1, swampCost 5, maxOps 2000, maxRooms 16, heuristicWeight 1.2, no cost limit, flee off.
Out-of-range values are clamped: plainCost and swampCost to 1..254, maxRooms to 1..64, heuristicWeight to 1..9.
A goal is a position (range 0) or {pos, range}. With a list of goals the search ends at the one that is cheapest to reach.
By itself the search knows terrain only: plain and swamp at the given costs, walls blocked. Structures, creeps and roads exist for it only through a cost matrix.
Cost matrix value of a tile: 0 = use the terrain cost, 1 to 254 = that cost, 255 = blocked. A value from 1 to 254 also opens a wall tile.
roomCallback(roomName) is called once for each room the search enters. Return a CostMatrix, nothing (terrain only), or false to keep the search out of that room.
Rooms beyond maxRooms count as walls.
The search gives up after maxOps steps, or when a node would cost more than maxCost. It then returns the path to the nearest point it reached, with incomplete: true.
Result: {path, ops, cost, incomplete}. path is a list of RoomPosition from the first step to the goal, without the start tile.
flee: true turns the goals around: the search ends on the cheapest tile that is at least range away from every goal.
Room.findPath, RoomPosition.findPathTo, findClosestByPath and moveTo all end in PathFinder.search, with a cost matrix made for each visible room.
That matrix blocks: structures you cannot walk on, portals, creeps and power creeps, ramparts of others that are not public, and your own construction sites for blocking structures. Roads get cost 1.
The wrappers search with plain 2 and swamp 10, so that roads (1) are preferred. With ignoreRoads the costs are 1 and 5 and road tiles get no cost of their own.

ignoreCreeps takes creeps out of the matrix. ignoreDestructibleStructures takes out walls, spawns, extensions, links, storages, observers, towers, power banks, power spawns, labs, terminals and foreign ramparts.
costCallback(roomName, costMatrix) receives a copy of that matrix for each room; change it, or return another CostMatrix.
The wrappers pass on maxOps, maxRooms, plainCost and swampCost. heuristicWeight is not passed on; avoid and ignore are dropped with a deprecation message.
maxOps of findPath: 2000 inside one room, 20000 when the target lies in another room.
findPath searches to range 1 of the target and then adds the target tile as the last step, unless you give a range.
findPath returns only the steps inside the starting room, as {x, y, dx, dy, direction}.
The matrix is built once per room, tick and set of ignore options, then shared by every findPath and moveTo of the tick.
For a room without vision the wrappers have no objects: the search sees terrain only there.
In your own room under safe mode, creeps of other players are not obstacles in that matrix.
moveTo stores its path in creep.memory._move and follows it for reusePath ticks (default 5) before it searches again.

The stored path is dropped when the time is up, when the creep is in another room than the one it was made in, or when the target changed. A creep crossing rooms therefore searches again in every room.
When the creep is no longer on its stored path, moveTo searches a new one in the same tick. With noPathFinding it returns ERR_NOT_FOUND instead.
findClosestByPath is one search with every candidate as a goal at range 1, limited to the room of the position.
Game.map.findRoute plans on the level of rooms and exits only, at most 30 rooms from the start in each direction. Its routeCallback gives the cost of entering a room: default 1, Infinity to block.
For a long trip, take the room list from findRoute and return false from roomCallback for every other room. The search then stays inside maxRooms and maxOps.

entries.name: Visibility: what your script can see
entries.title: Visibility: what your script can see
entries.summary: Your script gets the full contents of every room in which you have a creep, a power creep or a structure, and of the rooms your observers looked at last tick. All other rooms are hidden, except for your own flags and construction sites and the static map data.
tasks: how to get vision of a room
why is Game.rooms undefined for a room
what can I do without vision
how long does observer vision last
pitfalls: Game.rooms[name] is undefined as soon as nothing of yours is left in a remote room, and Game.rooms[name].find(...) then throws. Guard every access to a room that is not your own.
A stored id of something in a remote room (a source, a container) gives null whenever the room is not visible. Keep the position as well and travel by position.
facts: A room is visible in a tick when you own an object in it that is neither a flag nor a construction site: a creep, a power creep, a structure.
A tombstone or a ruin left by something of yours carries your user id too and keeps the room visible while it lasts.
An observer adds the room it was pointed at in the previous tick. The order holds for one tick and must be given again every tick.
For a visible room you get every object in it, whoever owns it.
Game.rooms holds exactly the visible rooms. For any other room Game.rooms[name] is undefined.
Game.getObjectById returns null for an id in a room you do not see, for an object that no longer exists and for one created in this tick.
A claimed controller is your object, so your own rooms are always visible. A reservation is not: a reserved room is visible only while something of yours is in it.
Flags never give vision. Game.flags still lists all your flags in every room; flag.pos always works, flag.room is undefined without vision.
Construction sites never give vision. Game.constructionSites and Game.getObjectById still return your own sites in unseen rooms.
Works without vision: Game.map (exits, routes, room status, terrain), new RoomPosition and new RoomVisual for any room, PathFinder.search over terrain, Flag.setPosition to any room.

Needs vision: every Room method, and the RoomPosition methods that look into the room: the find and look methods, createFlag and createConstructionSite. Without vision they throw "Could not access room".
The one exception is RoomPosition.lookFor(LOOK_TERRAIN): it reads the static terrain.
What you see is the state at the start of the tick. What other players do in this tick shows next tick.

entries.name: Event log: what happened in a room last tick
entries.title: Event log: what happened in a room last tick
entries.summary: Room.getEventLog() lists what the engine carried out in a visible room during the previous tick, one record per action: {event, objectId, data}. It covers every player, so it shows who attacked, healed, harvested or moved resources.
tasks: what events are in the event log
how much was harvested last tick
see who took energy from a container
pitfalls: An id in the log can belong to an object that is gone or out of sight by now: Game.getObjectById may return null for it.
To find who hurt your things, match targetId against your objects; objectId is the one acting, except in EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED.
facts: EVENT_ATTACK: objectId is the attacker, data is {targetId, damage, attackType}.

attackType is EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_MELEE for attack, _RANGED for rangedAttack and for a tower, _RANGED_MASS for rangedMassAttack (one record per target hit), _DISMANTLE for dismantle, _NUKE for a landing nuke.
A creep hit by attack answers with its own ATTACK parts, and a power bank hits back as well. That is a second EVENT_ATTACK with the two ids swapped and attackType EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_HIT_BACK.
When the target stands under a rampart, the record names the rampart as targetId.
damage is what the attacker dealt. What a boosted TOUGH part takes off is applied later and is not in the record.
No attack record is written when the target is a wall or rampart protected by a fortify or invulnerability effect.

EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED: objectId is what is gone, data is {type}. type is "creep" for every creep death (old age, suicide and recycling too), or the structure type for a structure brought to 0 hits by damage.
EVENT_ATTACK_CONTROLLER: objectId is the creep; there is no data.
EVENT_BUILD: data is {targetId, amount, structureType, x, y, incomplete}. amount is the progress added; incomplete turns false in the tick the structure is finished.
EVENT_HARVEST: data is {targetId, amount}. Written for sources and minerals; harvesting a deposit writes nothing.
EVENT_HEAL: data is {targetId, amount, healType}. healType is EVENT_HEAL_TYPE_MELEE for heal, EVENT_HEAL_TYPE_RANGED for rangedHeal and for a tower.
EVENT_REPAIR: data is {targetId, amount, energySpent}. For a tower energySpent is always 10.
EVENT_RESERVE_CONTROLLER: data is {amount}, the ticks of reservation added.
EVENT_UPGRADE_CONTROLLER: data is {amount, energySpent}. amount includes the gain from boosts, energySpent does not.
EVENT_EXIT: a creep or power creep stood on an exit tile at the end of the tick. data is {room, x, y}: where it appears next tick.

EVENT_TRANSFER: objectId is the giver, data is {targetId, resourceType, amount}. A withdraw is written from the giving side: objectId is the structure or tombstone, targetId the creep. Link transfers are logged too.
EVENT_POWER: data is {power, targetId}, written when a power creep uses a power.
There are no events for pickup, drop, spawning, lab reactions or terminal sends.
A structure that decays away or is removed with destroy() leaves no record: only damage and creep deaths write EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED.
Invader cores write the same records for their reserve, attack, upgrade and transfer actions.
The log covers one tick. It is started empty each time the room is processed and stored at the end.

entries.name: Finding and looking: Room.find, findClosest and the look methods
entries.title: Finding and looking: Room.find, findClosest and the look methods
entries.summary: Room.find reads lists that the runtime fills once per tick, one list per FIND_* constant and room. findInRange and the findClosest methods walk such a list; the look methods read an index by tile.
tasks: find or look which is cheaper
cheapest way to get the nearest object
which FIND constant for containers and roads
pitfalls: room.find with the same filter inside every creep repeats the filter work each time. Run it once per room and tick and pass the result on.
find(...)[0] is not the nearest object; the order is the internal order of the room objects. Use findClosestByRange.
facts: When the tick starts, every visible object is put into the list of each FIND_* constant it belongs to. Room.find(type) hands out a copy of that list: the work is the copy, not a search.
With a filter the list goes through lodash filter on every call. The filtered result is not kept anywhere.
The exit lists (FIND_EXIT and the four sides) are computed from terrain on first use and kept for the rest of the tick.
The objects in the lists are the same instances that Game.creeps, Game.structures and Game.getObjectById give during the tick.
findInRange and findClosestByRange take the Room.find list and measure every entry: simple arithmetic per object, no pathfinding.
Both also accept your own array in place of a constant, so one filtered list can serve many creeps.
findClosestByPath is a path search with all candidates as goals. It costs far more than findClosestByRange.
Range is the larger of the x and y distance. A target in another room has range Infinity.
The look methods read an index by tile that is filled when the tick starts: lookForAt(type, x, y) is one array read.
lookAt asks every kind in turn and adds the terrain. lookForAt for the one kind you need does less work.
The area forms go through whichever is fewer: the objects of that kind in the room, or the tiles of the rectangle.
LOOK_ENERGY and LOOK_RESOURCES are the same list, all dropped resources. lookAt therefore reports a pile twice.
LOOK_TERRAIN gives the string "plain", "swamp" or "wall". Room.getTerrain().get(x, y) gives the number and suits loops better.
FIND_CREEPS, FIND_MY_CREEPS, FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS: creeps that have finished spawning. HOSTILE means "not mine": allies, invaders and source keepers are in it.

FIND_STRUCTURES: every structure. FIND_MY_STRUCTURES: the ones you own. FIND_HOSTILE_STRUCTURES: the ones with another owner. Roads, containers and walls have no owner and are only in FIND_STRUCTURES.
FIND_SOURCES_ACTIVE: sources that have energy left at the start of the tick.
FIND_DROPPED_RESOURCES: all piles on the ground, of any resource.
FIND_FLAGS: your flags in the room. Flags of other players are never visible.
FIND_CONSTRUCTION_SITES, FIND_MY_CONSTRUCTION_SITES, FIND_HOSTILE_CONSTRUCTION_SITES: all sites, yours, those of others.
FIND_EXIT_TOP, FIND_EXIT_RIGHT, FIND_EXIT_BOTTOM and FIND_EXIT_LEFT give positions, not objects: the open tiles of that edge. Their numbers equal the directions TOP, RIGHT, BOTTOM, LEFT.
All of this needs vision of the room. Without it there is no Room object, and the RoomPosition forms throw.
