entries.name: Server CLI: the admin console and its commands
entries.title: Server CLI: the admin console and its commands
entries.summary: A running server has an admin console on port 21026: a JavaScript prompt inside the backend with the objects `system`, `map`, `bots`, `strongholds` and `storage`. `npx screeps cli` connects to it.
tasks: which cli commands does the server have
what does help() show in the cli
send a message to all players
pitfalls: The CLI asks for no password and can change or wipe everything: whatever arrives on the port is run. Leave `cli_host` on `localhost`.
A command must fit on one line: every line is run on its own.
No output is not an error: a promise that resolves to nothing prints nothing. An `update` prints `{ modified: n }`, or `{}` when no document matched.
The game constants are not in the prompt, only `print`, `help`, `storage`, `map`, `bots`, `strongholds` and `system`: type numbers yourself.
A server with mods may show more commands: a mod can add objects and functions to the prompt.
facts: `npx screeps cli` opens the prompt. It connects to `localhost`, port 21026; `--host` and `--port` name another target.
The CLI server runs in the backend process and listens on `cli_host` and `cli_port`; the stock `.screepsrc` sets `localhost` and 21026.
Without `cli_port` the launcher takes the first free port counting up from the game port + 1.

Each line is run as JavaScript in a sandbox inside the backend. When the result is a promise, the prompt waits and prints what it resolves to, so `storage.db.users.findOne({username: "Name"})` shows the user without `.then(print)`.

`help()` lists the objects. `help(system)`, `help(map)`, `help(bots)` and `help(strongholds)` list their commands; `help(storage)`, `help(storage.db)`, `help(storage.env)` and `help(storage.pubsub)` list collections, keys and methods.
`print(a, b)` writes values to the prompt.
`system.resetAllData()` replaces the whole database with the default world.
`system.sendServerMessage(text)` shows a text to every connected player.
`system.pauseSimulation()` stops the tick loop, `system.resumeSimulation()` starts it again.
`system.getTickDuration()` shows and `system.setTickDuration(ms)` sets the minimum length of a tick in milliseconds.
`system.runCronjob(name)` runs one of the backend's timed jobs at once, for example `genInvaders` or `genPowerBanks`; an unknown name is rejected.
`map.generateRoom(name, opts)` adds a room with random terrain; `map.removeRoom(name)` deletes a room with everything in it.
`map.closeRoom(name)` takes a room out of play; `map.openRoom(name, [timestamp])` puts it back, at once or at a later time.
`map.updateRoomImageAssets(name)` redraws the map images of a room; `map.updateTerrainData()` rebuilds the terrain cache of the world.
`bots.spawn(aiName, roomName, opts)` creates a bot player with a spawn; `bots.reload(aiName)` loads the AI's code again; `bots.removeUser(username)` deletes a bot player.
`strongholds.spawn(roomName, opts)` places an NPC stronghold; `strongholds.expand(roomName)` makes one put a lesser core into a nearby room.
`storage.db[collection]` reads and writes the database, `storage.env` the key-value store, `storage.pubsub` the event bus between the processes.

entries.name: Server launch options (.screepsrc) and processes
entries.title: Server launch options (.screepsrc) and processes
entries.summary: Launch options are read from `.screepsrc` in the server folder and can be overridden on the `screeps start` command line. The launcher starts one storage, one backend and one main process plus runner and processor workers, each with its own log file.
tasks: which processes does the server start
environment variables of the server processes
pitfalls: `host`, `cli_host`, `assetdir` and `db` have no built-in default. Without the line in `.screepsrc` or the flag, the launcher or the process stops with an error; the help text that names 127.0.0.1 as default for `--cli_host` is wrong.
The option list in the README is out of date: it shows `--runners_cnt` with default 2. The launcher has `--runner_threads` instead, and reads `runners_cnt` only from the file, default 1.
The launcher's table of defaults spells the option `runners_threads`, but the code reads `runner_threads`: keep the line in `.screepsrc`.
The timed restart happens once per launcher start: the process that comes back is started without the timer.
Start from the server folder. The launcher looks for `./.screepsrc` and only warns when it is missing.
facts: `screeps start` reads `.screepsrc` (ini format) from the current directory; an option given on the command line replaces the value from the file.
`port` (21025): the game server, HTTP and socket. Left out, the launcher takes the first free port from 21025 upwards.
`host` (0.0.0.0): the address the game server listens on.
`password` (empty): a server password that every API request must then carry.
`cli_port` (21026) and `cli_host` (localhost): where the admin console listens.
`runners_cnt` (1): number of runner processes. It has no command-line flag; the file warns that more than one gives every player several global scopes at the same time.
`runner_threads` (4): how many player scripts one runner runs in parallel. When the variable does not reach the runner, the driver uses 2.
`processors_cnt` (2): number of processes that process rooms.
Paths, relative to the server folder: `db` (db.json), `modfile` (mods.json), `assetdir` (assets), `logdir` (logs).
`log_console` (false): also print the output of all processes to the terminal, each line prefixed with the process name.
`log_rotate_keep` (5): on every start each log file is renamed to `.1`, the old `.1` to `.2`, and so on up to this number.
`storage_disabled` (false): do not start the built-in storage process, for a storage that runs on its own.
`restart_interval` (3600): seconds after which the launcher kills each runner and processor; they are started again at once.
`steam_api_key`: the Steam Web API key, needed when no Steam client runs on the machine.
`storage_port` (not in the stock file): where the storage listens. By default a socket file `storage.sock` in the server folder on Linux, elsewhere the first free port after the CLI port.
Process names: `storage`, `backend`, `engine_main`, `engine_runner1`…, `engine_processor1`…; each writes `<logdir>/<name>.log`.
A process that exits is started again, one second later.
To start the processes yourself (service manager, several machines), give each the environment variables the launcher gives it; the README names `lib/start.js` of the launcher as the list.
The processes reach the storage through `STORAGE_PORT` and, when set, `STORAGE_HOST`; the launcher never sets the host, and the storage itself listens on `localhost` without it.
A variable that is already set in the launcher's own environment wins over the value the launcher computed.

entries.name: Server mods: mods.json, the config object, events
entries.title: Server mods: mods.json, the config object, events
entries.summary: A mod is a Node.js module listed in `mods.json` that exports one function. Every server process loads every mod and passes it a `config` object whose parts depend on the process; the mod changes settings, replaces functions or listens to events there.
tasks: install a mod on the server
which events can a mod listen to
which settings can a mod change
what is the config object of a mod
why does my mod run several times
pitfalls: Mods are read once, when a process starts. After editing `mods.json` or a mod file, restart the server.
A mod file is loaded by every process, so code outside the `if(config.…)` checks runs once per process: six times or more with the stock settings.
A missing `mods.json` is not an error: the process logs "not found" and runs without mods and without bot AIs.
Do not edit the server code itself; the README warns that updates are then blocked and official clients of other players stop connecting. Write a mod.
`console.log` in a mod writes to the log file of the process the code ran in, not to a player console.
facts: `mods.json` has two keys: `mods`, a list of script paths, and `bots`, a map from AI name to a folder with its code. Paths are relative to the file.
The file is named by the `modfile` option and reaches every process as the `MODFILE` environment variable.
A mod must export a function. Each process calls it once with the `config` object; a module that exports something else is skipped with an error in the log.
An exception while one mod loads is logged and the other mods still load.
Each process fills in only its own parts of `config`, so a mod checks first, for example `if(config.backend)`.
`config.common` exists in every process: `constants`, `strongholds` (templates and loot), `system`, `bots`, `storage`, `dbCollections`.
`config.backend`, `config.cli` and `config.cronjobs` exist in the backend process.
`config.engine` exists in the main, runner and processor processes. Its `init` event says which one: `main`, `runner` or `processor`.
`config.storage` exists in the storage process; `dbOptions`, `getDb`, `loadDb` and `socketListener` can be replaced there.
Engine events of the loops: `mainLoopStage` (with the stage name, from `start` to `finish`), `runnerLoopStage`, `processorLoopStage`.
Engine events while a room is processed: `processObject` (every object, before the intents), `preProcessObjectIntents`, `processObjectIntents`, `postProcessObject`, `processRoom`.
Setting `object._skip = true` in `processObject` makes the engine leave that object alone for the tick: no intents, no tick of its own.
`playerSandbox` fires before each run of a player script, with a sandbox object (`run`, `set`, `get`) and the user id.
`saveRoomHistory` delivers a finished chunk of room history; `strongholdDestroyed` fires when an invader core is destroyed.
Backend events: `expressPreConfig` and `expressPostConfig` (the Express app, before and after the stock routes) and `sendUserNotifications` (user, list of notifications).
`cliSandbox` on `config.cli` passes the sandbox of a new CLI connection, to add commands to it.

Settings on `config.engine`: `mainLoopMinDuration` (1000 ms), `mainLoopResetInterval` (5000 ms), `cpuMaxPerTick` (500), `cpuBucketSize` (10000), `historyChunkSize` (20), `customIntentTypes`, `enableInspector`, `reportMemoryUsageInterval`.
`config.engine.mainLoopCustomStage` is a function run at the end of every tick. `config.engine.getNextTickDelay(usedMs)`, when a mod defines it, decides the wait before the next tick.
`config.engine.driver` is the driver module itself: a mod can wrap its functions, as the example does with `getAllUsers`.

Settings on `config.backend`: `welcomeText`, `router` (an Express router mounted at `/api`), `onGetRoomHistory`, `customObjectTypes`, `customIntentTypes`, `historyChunkSize`, `renderer.resources`, `renderer.metadata`, `socketModules`, `socketUpdateThrottle` (200 ms).
`config.cronjobs[name] = [seconds, function]` adds or replaces a timed job of the backend.
`config.common.constants` is the table of game constants of that process. A value changed there also reaches player scripts: the runner copies its table into every player sandbox.
A mod can add a database collection: push its name to `config.common.dbCollections`. The list becomes `storage.db` when the process connects to the storage, which is after the mods have loaded.
Three ways to install a mod: add its path to `mods` by hand; run `npm install <package>` in the server folder for a package whose `package.json` has `"screeps_mod": true`; the Steam Workshop.
The npm way works through install hooks that `screeps init` puts into `node_modules/.hooks`: they add the package's `main` file to `mods` and take it out again on uninstall.

entries.name: Private server and official server: what differs
entries.title: Private server and official server: what differs
entries.summary: A private server runs the same engine as the official world, but every player gets 100 CPU from a database field, there is one shard, sign-in is by Steam, and NPC events come from real-time timers in the backend. Account features of the official server are missing.
tasks: difference between private server and official server
how much cpu do players get on a private server
what is missing on a private server
does a private server have power banks
is Game.cpu.unlock available on a private server
what is Game.shard on a private server
does a private server send e-mail
pitfalls: CPU does not grow with GCL. To give more, change the `cpu` field of the user.
Code that calls `Game.cpu.generatePixel()` or `Game.cpu.unlock()` throws on a private server, because the functions do not exist. Test for them first.
Timers that follow the clock do not speed up with a faster tick: at 5 ticks per second a raid that is due may come 1500 ticks later.
facts: A new player gets a CPU limit of 100, whatever the GCL. The limit is the `cpu` field of the user document; `Game.cpu.limit` reads it.
The bucket holds up to 10000 and one tick may use up to 500. Both are driver settings.

`Game.cpu` has `limit`, `tickLimit`, `bucket`, `getUsed`, `getHeapStatistics` and `halt`. `unlock`, `generatePixel`, `setShardLimits`, `shardLimits`, `unlocked` and `unlockedTime` are not defined in the open-source engine.
`Game.shard.name` is the host name of the server machine, `type` is `normal`, `ptr` is false.
There is one world. `InterShardMemory` is not defined in the engine or the driver, and `RawMemory.interShardSegment` is an empty string that is not saved.

NPC events are made by backend jobs on real-time timers, not on tick counts: raids, power banks, deposits, strongholds and NPC market orders are checked every 5 minutes, stronghold expansion every 15.
Power banks appear in rooms whose room document has `bus: true`; deposits also need a `depositType` there. The default world has both on its highway rooms.
NPC market orders are made only for terminals without an owner, and the default world contains no terminal.
The engine handles portals, novice areas and respawn areas, but nothing in the server creates them. They exist only when the administrator writes them into the database.
Sign-in is by Steam only. No route takes an e-mail and a password, so tools that log in that way need a mod.
Room history is not kept: the history request answers "not implemented" until a mod supplies `onGetRoomHistory`.

Notifications (`Game.notify`, script errors, attack reports) are stored in `users.notifications`. A job that runs every minute hands them to the `sendUserNotifications` event and deletes them; nothing is e-mailed unless a mod listens.
A user's notifications go out at most once per `notifyPrefs.interval` minutes, 60 when not set.
A `Game.notify` text is cut to 500 characters when it is stored.
Overview graphs stay empty: the statistics routes return no data.
There is no wait before a new spawn after a respawn: placing is refused for 3 minutes after `lastRespawnDate`, a field the server never writes.
A player without any object in the world is set inactive and the script is no longer run. Uploading code or placing a spawn makes the account active again.

entries.name: Tick duration and pausing on a private server
entries.title: Tick duration and pausing on a private server
entries.summary: A tick lasts at least `mainLoopMinDuration` milliseconds, 1000 by default; a tick that needs longer simply takes longer. `system.setTickDuration(ms)` in the CLI changes the value at once and keeps it over restarts.
tasks: how long is a tick on a private server
why does my tick rate mod not work
how fast does the server really tick
pitfalls: A mod that sets `mainLoopMinDuration` loses against a stored `tickRate`: the main process loads the mods first and then overwrites the setting with the stored value. On a server that has run before, change the rate with `system.setTickDuration`.
The backend sends room updates to clients at most once per `config.backend.socketUpdateThrottle`, 200 ms. With shorter ticks the display skips ticks unless a mod lowers it, as the example mod does.
Pausing stops the ticks, not the backend: its timed jobs keep running, so raids, power banks and NPC orders are still created while paused.
The minimum is not a promise. With many rooms or slow scripts a tick takes as long as the work takes; the log line shows the real time.
facts: After a tick the main loop waits for what is left of `mainLoopMinDuration`. When the tick took longer than that, the next one starts at once.
The default is 1000 ms.
`system.setTickDuration(200)` stores the value under the key `tickRate` and tells the main process, which uses it from then on. `system.getTickDuration()` reads the stored value.
The value must be a whole number above 0; anything else is rejected.
The stored value survives restarts: at start the main process reads `tickRate` and uses it. Only when the key is empty does it store its current setting there.
A mod can set `config.engine.mainLoopMinDuration`, or define `config.engine.getNextTickDelay(usedMs)` to compute every wait itself.
`system.pauseSimulation()` sets the key `mainLoopPaused`; the main loop then skips every tick until `system.resumeSimulation()`. The game time stands still.
The main process logs every tick with the time it took and the wait that follows, in `engine_main.log`.
`GET /api/game/tick` returns the shortest of the last 30 tick lengths in milliseconds.
A tick that takes longer than `mainLoopResetInterval` (5000 ms) makes the main process log "Main loop reset!" and reset its work queues.

entries.name: Signing in to a private server: Steam, server password, tokens
entries.title: Signing in to a private server: Steam, server password, tokens
entries.summary: Players sign in with their Steam account: through the Steam client running on the server machine or, on a machine without Steam, through a Steam Web API key. An optional server password guards the whole HTTP API. Tokens last 60 seconds and are renewed with every request.
tasks: how do players log in to a private server
steam api key for the server
why can nobody log in to my server
how is a new user created on the server
change a username on the server
how long is a login token valid
pitfalls: Without a Steam client and without `steam_api_key` the backend exits right after start, and the launcher starts it again in a loop. Look into `logs/backend.log`.
There is no login with e-mail and password in the stock server, so upload tools that send those get no token. The contributed guide installs a mod for that.
The backend writes the server password in clear text into its log at start.
The server password guards the game API, not the admin console: that port has no password at all.
facts: With `steam_api_key` set, the backend checks each player's Steam ticket through the Steam Web API. Without it, it uses the Steam client on the same machine and refuses to start when that is not running.
The only sign-in route is `POST /api/auth/steam-ticket`. It answers with a token.
The first sign-in of a Steam id creates the user: CPU 100, GCL points 0, and an empty code branch `default` that is the active one.
The player then chooses a name once: 3 characters or more out of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, not used by anyone else when compared without case. The API refuses a second change.
A token is valid for 60 seconds. Every authenticated answer carries the next one in the `X-Token` header; the socket answers `auth ok` with a new token.

With `password` set, every request to `/api` and `/room-history` must carry it in the `X-Server-Password` header; otherwise the answer is the error "incorrect server password". The start page `/` and `/assets` stay open.
`GET /api/version` needs no sign-in. It tells a client the protocol number, whether the local Steam client is used, the number of active human players, the package version and the welcome text.
A request body may be up to 8 MB.

entries.name: Server storage: db.json, collections, keys
entries.title: Server storage: db.json, collections, keys
entries.summary: All data of a server lives in one storage process: a LokiJS database that is written to `db.json` every 10 seconds, a key-value store and a publish/subscribe bus. Every other process reaches it over one socket.
tasks: where is the server data stored
which collections does the server database have
how often is the database saved
where is player memory stored on the server
force a global reset for all players
pitfalls: The file is written only by the 10-second autosave; the storage process does not save when it exits. Stopping the server can lose the last seconds.
Documents come back as copies over the socket. Changing a returned object changes nothing in the database: write with `update`.
To find documents in which a field is null or missing, write `{field: {$eq: null}}`; for the opposite, `{field: {$ne: null}}`. The storage widens exactly these two forms to cover missing fields.
`clear()` and `removeWhere({})` empty a whole collection without asking.
facts: The storage process holds the collections (`storage.db`), a key-value store (`storage.env`), an event bus (`storage.pubsub`) and the work queues of the tick loop.
The database is LokiJS: kept in memory and written to the file named by `db` every 10 seconds.

Collections: `users`, `users.code`, `users.console`, `users.intents`, `users.messages`, `users.money`, `users.notifications`, `users.resources`, `users.power_creeps`, `rooms`, `rooms.objects`, `rooms.flags`, `rooms.intents`, `rooms.terrain`, `market.orders`, `market.stats`, `transactions`, and three `leaderboard.` collections.
Every game object is one document in `rooms.objects` with `type`, `room`, `x`, `y`; a room is one document in `rooms` whose `_id` is the room name, and its terrain one in `rooms.terrain`.
Methods of a collection: `find`, `findOne`, `findEx` (with sort, offset, limit), `count`, `insert`, `update`, `removeWhere`, `clear`, `by`, `ensureIndex`, `bulk`. All return promises.

`update(query, change, {upsert: true})` understands `$set`, `$merge`, `$inc`, `$unset`, `$addToSet` and `$pull`. `$set` replaces a field as a whole; `$merge` goes into objects and keeps their other keys.
`insert` gives a document an `_id` when it has none.
`storage.env` is one set of names and values with Redis-like calls: `get`, `mget`, `set`, `setex`, `expire`, `ttl`, `del`, `hget`, `hset`, `hmget`, `hmset`, `sadd`, `smembers`.

Names in `storage.env.keys`: `GAMETIME` (the tick), `MAIN_LOOP_MIN_DURATION` (tick length), `MAIN_LOOP_PAUSED`, `MEMORY` + user id (player memory as a string), `MEMORY_SEGMENTS` + user id, `ACTIVE_ROOMS`, `ACCESSIBLE_ROOMS`, `TERRAIN_DATA`, `MAP_VIEW` + room, `ROOM_HISTORY` + room, `ROOM_VISUAL`, `ROOM_EVENT_LOG`.
Channels in `storage.pubsub.keys`: `TICK_STARTED`, `ROOMS_DONE` (once per tick, with the game time), `RUNTIME_RESTART`, `QUEUE_DONE`.
Publishing on `RUNTIME_RESTART` makes every runner throw away all player sandboxes, a global reset for everyone: `storage.pubsub.publish(storage.pubsub.keys.RUNTIME_RESTART, "1")`.
When it loads an older `db.json`, the storage upgrades it step by step to database version 9.
A process that loses the storage connection tries again every second.
The storage can be replaced: the README calls LokiJS the default and names community solutions for more performance; the launcher option `storage_disabled` leaves the built-in one out.

The contributed guide moves the data to MongoDB and Redis with a mod, because the built-in storage scales badly over time. After the switch the guide runs `system.resetAllData()` to initialise the new database.

entries.name: Spawning: who pays, how long, where the creep comes out
entries.title: Spawning: who pays, how long, where the creep comes out
entries.summary: A spawn makes one creep at a time: 3 ticks per body part, paid in full at the start from the spawns and extensions of the room. The finished creep is put on the first free tile around the spawn.
tasks: which extensions pay for a creep first
in what order is spawn energy taken
what happens when the spawn exits are blocked
why is my spawn stuck with a finished creep
does a spawn kill a creep that blocks it
how fast does a spawn regenerate energy
what does renewing a creep cost and add
how much energy does recycling give back per part
cancel a creep that is being spawned
which direction does a creep leave the spawn
pitfalls: Two creeps ordered under the same name in one tick: the second call returns ERR_NAME_EXISTS, because names used this tick count as taken.
The spawn does not read as busy in the tick of the order: a second spawnCreep on it in the same tick returns OK and replaces the first.
Do not park creeps on all eight tiles around a spawn: your own creeps are never killed to make room, the spawn just waits.
facts: The whole cost, the sum of BODYPART_COST, is taken in the tick of the call. Nothing is paid over time.
Without opts.energyStructures the spawn itself pays first, then the other spawns, then the extensions; inside each group the nearest to the spawning spawn first (distance: the larger of dx and dy).
With opts.energyStructures only the listed structures pay, in list order. Entries that are not active spawns or extensions of yours are skipped; a structure listed twice counts once.
Spawns and extensions above the allowance of the room level are switched off, farthest from the controller first. They neither count nor pay.
The return code is checked against the energy at the start of the tick. If another spawn of the room has spent it by the time the order is processed, no creep is made and nothing is charged.
Spawn time is 3 ticks per part: 150 ticks for a body of 50.
PWR_OPERATE_SPAWN cuts it to 90%–20% (by power level, rounded up) if it is active when the spawning starts. PWR_DISRUPT_SPAWN stops the clock for as long as it lasts.
Meanwhile the creep exists on the spawn's own tile with spawning = true and cannot act. Its life time starts in its first tick outside.
When the time is up the creep goes to the first free tile in direction order: TOP, TOP_RIGHT, RIGHT and on clockwise, or the order given in opts.directions or setDirections.
A tile is not free when it holds a creep or a non-walkable structure, a construction site for a non-walkable structure (anybody's), a creep moving onto it this tick, or wall terrain without a road.
No free tile: the spawn stays busy and tries again every tick; spawning.remainingTime reads 0 meanwhile.
Hostile-creep case: if every allowed tile is taken and one of them holds a creep of another player (ally and invader alike), that creep is killed and the new creep takes its tile.
With a restricted direction list that only happens when the other directions are blocked as well. A free tile outside your list means the spawn just waits.
A spawn gains 1 energy per tick while the active spawns and extensions of the room hold less than 300 together and the spawn itself is not full.
No regeneration in a room whose controller is not yours, and none for a spawn switched off by the room level.
It is the way back when every creep is dead: from empty, a [WORK, CARRY, MOVE] creep (200 energy) is affordable after 200 ticks.
spawning.cancel() removes the unfinished creep at once. The energy is not returned.
A spawn destroyed while spawning takes the unfinished creep with it.
renewCreep adds floor(600 ÷ parts) ticks of life per call.
One call costs ceil(0.4 × body cost ÷ parts) energy. Per tick of life that is body cost ÷ 1500, the price of a new creep; what is saved is spawn time.
A call that would lift ticksToLive above 1500 is refused (ERR_FULL).
The spawn must be idle; the creep adjacent, yours, out of the spawn and without a CLAIM part.
Renewing strips every boost from the creep; no compound comes back.
recycleCreep kills an adjacent creep of yours and returns per part min(125, part cost × ticksToLive ÷ life time): rate 1 instead of the 0.2 of every other death.
The refund does not go into the spawn: it lands in a container under the creep if there is one, else in a tombstone on the creep's tile.
Recycling works while the spawn is busy: the only checks are on the creep.

entries.name: Construction sites: where, how many, what they cost
entries.title: Construction sites: where, how many, what they cost
entries.summary: A site marks a structure to be built. A player may have 100 sites in all; whether one may be placed depends on the room, the room level and the tile.
tasks: where can I place a construction site
how many construction sites can I have
can I build next to an exit
what happens when a creep steps on a construction site
who can remove a construction site
what does a road cost on swamp or through a wall
what does a new structure start with
does a new spawn start with energy
can two structures share a tile
pitfalls: Structures left by a former owner count against your allowance: with their extensions standing you cannot place your own until you destroy them.
Your creeps wipe an ally's sites by walking over them, in your room as anywhere: path around them.
facts: At most 100 sites per player over all rooms, those placed earlier in the same tick included (ERR_FULL).
Rooms: your own; rooms whose controller nobody owns and nobody else reserved; rooms without a controller. Never a room owned or reserved by another player (ERR_NOT_OWNER).
Count per type: the structures and sites of that type already in the room, whoever owns them, must be fewer than CONTROLLER_STRUCTURES allows at the room level (ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH).
A room without an owner counts as level 0: roads and 5 containers, nothing else.
Tile: x and y from 1 to 48. Nothing on the outermost ring.
Tile: on the second ring (x or y equal to 1 or 48) only roads and containers, unless the three border tiles beside it are all wall. Everything else keeps two tiles away from an exit.
Tile: on wall terrain only roads and extractors.
Tile: one site at a time, and no second structure of the same type.
Tile: only roads and ramparts share. A road or rampart may go onto any structure; anything else needs a tile that holds no structure but roads and ramparts.
Tile: an extractor needs a mineral without an extractor.
A broken tile rule returns ERR_INVALID_TARGET.
Creeps do not matter for placing. They matter for building: a site for a non-walkable structure cannot be built while a creep stands on it.
Cost: CONSTRUCTION_COST of the type. A road costs ×5 on swamp (1500) and ×150 on a wall tile (45,000); the finished road has its hits and its decay multiplied the same way.
Placing costs no energy, only the 0.2 CPU of the intent, for each site.
Any creep may build any site: the processor only checks that the target is a site within range 3. 1 energy is 1 progress, 5 per WORK part per tick.
remove(): the owner of the site anywhere, the owner of the room on any site in it. With progress above 1, half of it (rounded down) drops as energy.
A creep that moves onto a tile with another player's site removes the site, with the same half refund on the ground. Whose room it is makes no difference.
Exception: in a room under safe mode only the creeps of the room owner do that.
Your own site for a non-walkable structure blocks your own creeps. Such a site, anybody's, also keeps a new creep from leaving a spawn onto that tile.
Sites do not decay. A nuke landing in the room removes all of them.
The structure appears in the tick after the last progress point, owned by the owner of the site, with a new id.
It starts empty: a built spawn has 0 energy, a tower 0. Only the first spawn a player places starts with 300.
It starts with full hits, except a rampart (1) and a wall (1).
Rampart, road and container have their first decay 100, 1000 and 100 ticks after completion.
An extension has capacity 0 in its first tick; after that the room level sets it.
A nuker starts with its full cooldown of 100,000 ticks.

entries.name: Body design: cost, weight, speed, part order
entries.title: Body design: cost, weight, speed, part order
entries.summary: A body is a list of 1 to 50 parts. Its cost is the sum of the parts, its speed follows from weight against MOVE parts, and the order of the list decides which parts are lost first.
tasks: how many MOVE parts does a creep need on roads
how many MOVE parts for swamp
how much does a body cost
where to put TOUGH parts in a body
largest creep I can spawn at each room level
how fast does a creep move
how many body parts can a creep have
pitfalls: A hauler sized for roads crawls off them: with MOVE = weight ÷ 2 it takes 2 ticks per plain tile and 10 per swamp tile when loaded.
WORK, ATTACK, HEAL and the like always weigh; only CARRY gets lighter when empty. A miner with 5 WORK and 1 MOVE needs 5 ticks per plain tile.
facts: Cost: the sum of BODYPART_COST over the parts. Spawn time: 3 ticks per part. Hits: 100 per part.
Size: 1 to 50 parts, else ERR_INVALID_ARGS. The second limit is the energy capacity of the room, because the whole cost is paid at once.
Weight: every part that is neither MOVE nor CARRY counts 1, destroyed parts included.
CARRY parts weigh only as far as the load needs them: one per 50 carried (more per part when boosted). An empty hauler weighs nothing.
A step adds weight × 1 fatigue onto a road, × 2 onto plain, × 10 onto swamp. The tile stepped onto decides, and a road on it wins over the terrain.
Each MOVE part with hits takes 2 fatigue off per tick, in the tick of the step too. Boosted: ×2 (ZO), ×3 (ZHO2), ×4 (XZHO2).
So ticks per tile = weight × step factor ÷ (2 × MOVE parts), rounded up, at least 1.
One tile per tick needs MOVE = weight ÷ 2 on roads, = weight on plain, = 5 × weight on swamp.
With fatigue above 0, or without a MOVE part that still has hits, a creep does not move unless another creep pulls it.
Damage empties the body from the first part of the list toward the last.
A part with 0 hits does nothing: no work, no capacity, no fatigue removed. It still weighs.
So put first what may be lost (TOUGH, then the working parts) and last what must work to the end: MOVE to get away, HEAL to recover.
Boosted TOUGH reduces only the damage that arrives while the TOUGH part itself has hits, and damage runs through the parts from the front. TOUGH behind other parts protects nothing in front of it.
Lost CARRY parts lose their capacity at once and the overflow drops on the tile.
What a part type does scales with the parts of that type that still have hits; a boost multiplies single parts.
Life: 1500 ticks. A body with any CLAIM part lives 600 and cannot be renewed.

entries.name: Ramparts and walls
entries.title: Ramparts and walls
entries.summary: Both are built for 1 energy with 1 hit and have to be repaired up. A rampart shields its tile and lets its owner through; a wall blocks everyone. Only ramparts decay.
tasks: rampart max hits by room level
how much energy to repair a rampart to max
what happens to my ramparts when I lose the room
rampart in a room that is not mine
can a wall be repaired in an unowned room
what does a public rampart allow
difference between a wall and a rampart
how many hits does a new rampart have
pitfalls: A rampart protects one tile. A creep or structure next to it is hit normally, and ranged attackers reach over it.
Close your ramparts when hostiles are in the room: an open one lets them in and then shields them.
facts: A new rampart has 1 hit, a new wall 1. Each costs 1 energy to build, is allowed from room level 2, up to 2500 per room.
Rampart maximum: by the level of the room, when the room is the rampart owner's: 300,000 at level 2 up to 300,000,000 at level 8. It is set anew every tick, so it follows a level change at once.
Wall maximum: 300,000,000 in any room whose controller is at level 2 or more, whoever owns it. 0 below that.
attack, rangedAttack, dismantle and a tower shot aimed at anything on a rampart tile hit the rampart instead.
rangedMassAttack leaves out everything on a rampart tile and damages the rampart itself.
The redirect asks neither whose rampart it is nor whose creep: an enemy standing on your public rampart is covered by it.
Damage beyond the rampart's hits is lost; what stands under it takes nothing in that tick. A nuke is the exception: what the rampart cannot absorb reaches the tile.
A melee attacker standing on a rampart takes no hit-back.
Creeps of other players cannot step onto a closed rampart; its owner's creeps can. A wall blocks everyone, the builder included.
Other players cannot withdraw from a structure under a closed rampart.
setPublic(true) opens it for the creeps of other players, to walk through and to withdraw from what is under it. It goes on absorbing damage. A new rampart is closed.
A rampart loses 300 hits every 100 ticks and is removed when that brings it to 0 or below. A wall has no decay.
A new rampart has its first decay after 100 ticks. Without at least 301 hits by then it is gone.
A creep repairs 100 hits per WORK part per tick at 0.01 energy per hit, range 3, never above hitsMax.
Holding a rampart level costs 3 energy per 100 ticks; filling one to the level maximum costs hitsMax × 0.01 (table).
A tower repairs 800 hits up to range 5, down to 200 from range 20, for 10 energy: 80 to 20 hits per energy against a creep's 100.
In a room that is not its owner's (lost, unclaimed, never owned) and in a room below level 2 a rampart has hitsMax 0: repair does nothing and it decays until it is gone, about hits ÷ 300 × 100 ticks.
Until then it works as before: it blocks other players and absorbs damage.
The owner of a room can destroy() any rampart or wall in it, as long as no creep of another player is in the room.
A built wall has no owner: anyone may repair or dismantle it.
Under PWR_FORTIFY a wall or rampart takes no damage from anything but a nuke. A rampart made by PWR_SHIELD disappears when the effect ends.
Neither may be placed on the two outer rings of tiles next to an exit. A rampart may share its tile with any structure, a wall only with a road or a rampart.

entries.doc: Execute a trade deal from your Terminal in `yourRoomName` to another player's Terminal using the specified buy/sell order.
entries.summary: Trade against another player's order from one of your terminals.
tasks: who pays the energy for a market deal
pitfalls: Your terminal pays the energy transfer fee, whichever side you are on.
At most 10 deals per tick (ERR_FULL), and the terminal used goes on cooldown (10 ticks).
The deal runs after the tick. If someone else took the order first, less or nothing is traded.
The traded amount is cut to what is left in the order, what the selling terminal holds, the free space of the buying terminal and the credits of the buyer.
When you buy energy the transfer fee must already be in your terminal; the energy that arrives cannot pay for it.
A second deal through the same terminal in one tick, or a deal after a send from it, returns OK and is dropped: the first action puts the terminal on cooldown.
When several players deal on one order in the same tick, the terminal nearest to the order is served first.
ERR_INVALID_ARGS for an order that is not active: only active orders are loaded.
notes: Only your terminal goes on cooldown; the terminal of the order owner neither cools down nor pays energy.
A deal has no credit fee: the buyer pays amount × price and the seller receives exactly that.
Selling to a buy order needs no credits; buying from a sell order needs amount × price (ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES).
Orders for account resources (INTERSHARD_RESOURCES) trade without terminal, energy or cooldown; yourRoomName is not used.
A deal on an account resource takes no room and no terminal and pays no energy; selling needs the amount in `Game.resources`.

options.desc: Weight to apply to the heuristic in the A\* formula `F = G + weight \* H`.

entries.returnsText: An object containing the following properties:
entries.doc: Find an optimal path between `origin` and `goal`.
entries.summary: The pathfinder: cheapest path from a position to one or several goals, across rooms, with your own tile costs.
pitfalls: It knows only terrain. Structures, creeps and roads count only through the CostMatrix your roomCallback returns.
Check result.incomplete: when maxOps (default 2000) or maxRooms (default 16) runs out you get a partial path.
The path does not contain the start position.
To prefer roads set plainCost 2, swampCost 10 and write cost 1 on road tiles.
Return false from roomCallback to keep the search out of a room.
A goal with range 0 on a blocked tile (a source, a controller) is unreachable; give range 1.
A matrix value from 1 to 254 on a wall tile makes that wall walkable for the search. Only write costs on tiles a creep can really enter.
If roomCallback returns false for the room the search starts in, the result is an empty path with incomplete true.
notes: CostMatrix values: 0 = terrain default, 1–254 = cost, 255 = blocked. 1000 ops cost about 1 CPU.
Defaults: plainCost 1, swampCost 5, maxOps 2000, maxRooms 16, heuristicWeight 1.2.
Values are clamped: plainCost and swampCost to 1..254, maxRooms to 1..64, heuristicWeight to 1..9.
When the origin is already within range of a goal the result is an empty path with incomplete false.
Without a goal, or with an empty goal list, it returns {path: [], ops: 0} and no incomplete field.

entries.name: PowerCreep
entries.doc: Power Creeps are immortal "heroes" that are tied to your account and can be respawned in any `PowerSpawn` after death.
entries.summary: A hero unit that does not die of age for good: it is created once per account, levelled with GPL, and respawned at a power spawn.
tasks: what can a power creep do
pitfalls: FIND_CREEPS, FIND_MY_CREEPS and FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS leave power creeps out: use the FIND_*_POWER_CREEPS constants for them.
notes: A new power creep has 1,000 hits and a store of 100; each level adds 1,000 hits and 100 capacity.
It has no body and no fatigue: one tile costs it one tick on any terrain.
It can move, carry, say, use powers, enable a room and renew. It has no call to harvest, build, repair, attack or heal.
POWER_CLASS.OPERATOR is the only class the code accepts; the docs describe two more as not built yet.

entries.doc: A static method to create new Power Creep instance in your account.
entries.summary: Create a new power creep on the account. It costs one free GPL level and does not appear in a room until spawn() is called.
notes: The reference marks this call as cheap, but it queues an account intent and the runtime charges the 0.2 CPU fee for it.
Free levels = GPL level − number of power creeps − sum of their levels. Without one the call returns ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES.
The new creep is level 0 with 1,000 hits and a store of 100, and is not on cooldown: it can be spawned in the next tick.
The call queues an account intent, so an OK adds the 0.2 CPU intent fee, although the docs list the method without it.
pitfalls: The call accepts a name of up to 100 characters, but the processor keeps the first 50. A longer name is stored cut, and Game.powerCreeps has it under the cut name.

entries.name: RawMemory
entries.doc: RawMemory object allows to implement your own memory stringifier instead of built-in serializer based on `JSON.stringify`.

entries.name: segments
entries.doc: An object with asynchronous memory segments available on this tick.
entries.summary: The segments active this tick, by id, as strings. Assign a string to write one.
pitfalls: Only the segments requested with setActiveSegments in the previous tick are present.
Each segment holds at most 100 KB. Segments are saved at the end of the tick.
A segment over 100 × 1024 characters, a value that is not a string, or more than 10 keys makes the end of the tick fail. Nothing of that tick is saved then: no intents, no Memory, no segments.
notes: Every key present at the end of the tick is saved, loaded or not: you can write a segment without requesting it first.
A requested segment that was never written arrives as an empty string.

notes: Undefined unless the owner has that id in the public list at the moment your tick is loaded.

args.desc: New memory value as a string.

entries.summary: Replace the stored Memory string.
pitfalls: Do not mix it with the Memory object in one tick: decide per tick whether the string or the object is the source.
Throws when the value is not a string or is longer than 2 × 1024 × 1024 characters.
set() drops the parsed Memory object: what you changed on Memory before the call is not saved.
If Memory is read for the first time after set(), it is parsed from the new string and written back after the loop, replacing what set() stored.

FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS contains every creep that is not yours: invaders, source keepers and allies too.
The unfiltered list is cached per tick, the filter runs on every call. Filter once and keep the result.
FIND_SOURCES_ACTIVE leaves out empty sources.
FIND_CREEPS, FIND_MY_CREEPS and FIND_HOSTILE_CREEPS leave out creeps that are still spawning.
The first find(FIND_EXIT, {filter}) of a tick stores its filtered result as the whole exit list of the room; later calls get that subset. Filter exits yourself.
notes: The filter is handed to lodash filter: a function, an object such as {structureType: STRUCTURE_TOWER}, or a property name.
FIND_EXIT_TOP, _RIGHT, _BOTTOM and _LEFT return the open edge tiles of that side as positions; FIND_EXIT returns all four sides.
FIND_FLAGS holds only your own flags. FIND_DROPPED_RESOURCES holds every pile on the ground, whatever the resource.
The result is always an array; a kind with no objects gives an empty one.

entries.name: Return codes (OK, ERR_*)
entries.title: Return codes (OK, ERR_*)
entries.summary: What the action methods return. OK means the intent was queued, not that it will succeed.
tasks: what does a return code mean

constants.name: OK
constants.note: The call passed its checks and the action is queued for the end of the tick. It can still fail there.

constants.name: ERR_NOT_OWNER
constants.note: The object, or the room it is in, is not yours to use this way.

constants.name: ERR_NO_PATH
constants.note: No path or route to the target was found.

constants.name: ERR_NAME_EXISTS
constants.note: The name is already in use (creep, spawn, flag or power creep).

constants.name: ERR_BUSY
constants.note: The object cannot act now: a creep that is still spawning, a spawn that is already spawning, a power creep that is not in the world.

constants.name: ERR_NOT_FOUND
constants.note: What the call refers to is not there: no step of the path at this position, no queued order to cancel, no parts to boost.

constants.name: ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_ENERGY
constants.note: Not enough energy for the action. Same number as ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES.

constants.name: ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES
constants.note: The object lacks the resource or the amount the action needs.

constants.name: ERR_INVALID_TARGET
constants.note: The target is the wrong kind of object, does not exist, or cannot take this action.

constants.name: ERR_FULL
constants.note: The target cannot take more, or a limit is reached (store, flags, construction sites, deals per tick).

constants.name: ERR_NOT_IN_RANGE
constants.note: The target is too far away for this action.

constants.name: ERR_INVALID_ARGS
constants.note: An argument has the wrong type or a value that is not allowed.

constants.name: ERR_TIRED
constants.note: Still cooling down: fatigue of a creep or the cooldown of a structure.

constants.name: ERR_NO_BODYPART
constants.note: The creep has no working body part of the kind this action needs.

constants.name: ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_EXTENSIONS
constants.note: Spawns and extensions hold too little energy for the body. Same number as ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES.

constants.name: ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH
constants.note: The room controller level is too low for this structure or action.

constants.name: ERR_GCL_NOT_ENOUGH
constants.note: Your Global Control Level does not allow one more room.

constants.name: ERR_ACCESS_DENIED
constants.note: You have no access to this restricted shard. Returned by claimController, reserveController and upgradeController.

notes: ERR_NOT_OWNER (-1): not your object, or a room owned or reserved by someone else. ERR_BUSY (-4): the creep is still spawning, or the spawn is busy. ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RESOURCES / _ENERGY / _EXTENSIONS (all -6). ERR_INVALID_TARGET (-7): wrong kind of target, or the target cannot take the action. ERR_FULL (-8). ERR_NOT_IN_RANGE (-9). ERR_INVALID_ARGS (-10). ERR_TIRED (-11): fatigue or cooldown. ERR_NO_BODYPART (-12): no working part of the needed type; also returned for hostile actions in a room under someone else's safe mode. ERR_RCL_NOT_ENOUGH (-14). ERR_GCL_NOT_ENOUGH (-15).
Only a call that queues an intent costs the 0.2 CPU fee: one that returns an error code does not, and neither do say and pull.

tables.title: Boosts
head: part
compound
effect
tables.foot: 30 compound + 20 energy per part. "damage ×0.3" means the part takes 30% of the damage. "capacity" multiplies 50; "fatigue" multiplies the 2 fatigue a MOVE part removes.

constants.name: PWR_OPERATE_POWER

constants.name: PWR_FORTIFY
constants.note: Makes the target wall or rampart take no damage from attacks.

constants.name: PWR_OPERATE_CONTROLLER

constants.name: PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY
constants.note: Sets the level of the target factory and lets it produce commodities of that level.

constants.name: EFFECT_INVULNERABILITY
constants.note: Effect id on a stronghold core before it deploys and on the controller of a stronghold room: attacks on the object are refused.

constants.name: EFFECT_COLLAPSE_TIMER

constants.name: POWER_INFO
constants.note: Per power: class, creep level needed for power levels 1–5, cooldown, and where they apply range, duration, ops cost and effect per level.

notes: A field missing in POWER_INFO means "not needed": no range = no target, no ops = free, no duration = instant.
duration and ops can be a list with one value per power level instead of a number.
POWER_INFO[power].level[k − 1] is the creep level needed before power level k can be taken.
PWR_REGEN_SOURCE and PWR_REGEN_MINERAL have a period: the ticks between two additions.
Hits and store of a power creep are not constants: 1,000 and 100 per level are written in the processor.
POWER_BANK_CAPACITY_MIN and _MAX bound the roll for a new bank; with a chance of POWER_BANK_CAPACITY_CRIT the bank gets _MAX on top.

entries.name: Factory commodities
entries.title: Factory commodities
entries.summary: What the factory makes from what, at which level, with which cooldown.

constants.name: COMMODITIES
constants.note: COMMODITIES[product] = {amount made per produce call, cooldown in ticks, components taken from the factory, level: the factory level needed (absent = any factory)}.

notes: A recipe with a level runs only in a factory of exactly that level while PWR_OPERATE_FACTORY is active on it; a recipe without a level runs in any factory.
"makes" is the output of one produce call; the components are taken from the factory's own store.

entries.name: Event log constants
entries.title: Event log constants
entries.summary: EVENT_* types and sub-types in Room.getEventLog.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK
constants.note: A creep, a tower or a nuke damaged something. data: targetId, damage, attackType.

constants.name: EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED
constants.note: A creep died, or a structure was destroyed by damage. data: type.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_CONTROLLER
constants.note: attackController was used on the controller of the room. No data.

constants.name: EVENT_BUILD
constants.note: A creep built on a construction site. data: targetId, amount, structureType, x, y, incomplete.

constants.name: EVENT_HARVEST
constants.note: A creep harvested a source or a mineral. data: targetId, amount.

constants.name: EVENT_HEAL
constants.note: A creep or a tower healed a creep. data: targetId, amount, healType.

constants.name: EVENT_REPAIR
constants.note: A creep or a tower repaired a structure. data: targetId, amount, energySpent.

constants.name: EVENT_RESERVE_CONTROLLER
constants.note: The controller was reserved. data: amount, the ticks added.

constants.name: EVENT_UPGRADE_CONTROLLER
constants.note: The controller was upgraded. data: amount, energySpent.

constants.name: EVENT_EXIT
constants.note: A creep left the room through an exit. data: room, x, y, where it arrives.

constants.name: EVENT_POWER
constants.note: A power creep used a power. data: power, targetId.

constants.name: EVENT_TRANSFER
constants.note: Resources moved from one object to another by transfer, withdraw or a link. data: targetId, resourceType, amount.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_MELEE
constants.note: attackType of Creep.attack.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_RANGED
constants.note: attackType of Creep.rangedAttack and of a tower attack.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_RANGED_MASS
constants.note: attackType of Creep.rangedMassAttack; one event per target hit.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_DISMANTLE
constants.note: attackType of Creep.dismantle.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_HIT_BACK
constants.note: attackType of the damage that a creep attacked in melee, or a power bank, deals back.

constants.name: EVENT_ATTACK_TYPE_NUKE
constants.note: attackType of the damage from a landing nuke.

constants.name: EVENT_HEAL_TYPE_MELEE
constants.note: healType of Creep.heal.

constants.name: EVENT_HEAL_TYPE_RANGED
constants.note: healType of Creep.rangedHeal and of a tower heal.
